8. For God permitted the Devil to venture all his remaining power: after which this enemy, on a certain day, stormed so mightily against her that she knew not what she should do, or what would become of her. It seemed to her as if all the evil spirits were about to carry her away; and the fire of unchaste love <note>In the context of 17th-century mysticism, "unchaste love" refers to intrusive, unwanted lustful thoughts that the individual views as a spiritual attack rather than a personal desire.</note> burned so fiercely that, because she no longer knew how to contain herself, she ran in great haste out of the house into the middle of a large meadow, in order to bewail and lament her misfortune there unhindered, without being seen or heard by anyone. But because the grace that God showed her in this place is very great and remarkable, it will not be unhelpful for us to hear her own words about it:

9. > "When I had arrived there," (she said,) "I threw myself down upon the earth, full of despair and quite beside myself, where I then began to sigh and lament my misery with the following words: Alas! I, wretched and unhappy! Why was I born, that I must now see myself in such great distress? Did I have to leave all my relatives and friends for this, only to see myself ignited and consumed here by a hellish fire? Must my heart, which is made for God alone, have no other love than for the creature? <note>original: "Creatur." In mystical writing, "the creature" refers to anything created (people, objects, worldly desires) as opposed to the Creator.</note> And must that which I have always feared so much strike me in such a wondrously strange way? Afterward, I turned to God and cried out to Him: My God, oh, take me away from this world, so that I may no longer offend Thee!
> 
> "While I was in the midst of my most vehement lamentations and in my greatest despair, behold, in an instant God changed my heart in such a way that, from the extreme of misery, I suddenly found myself transported into the extreme of joy and pleasure, nor did I know how, or by what means this happened; which occurred through such a singular effect of divine omnipotence that it may well be regarded as a miracle—indeed, a greater miracle, in my opinion, than if He had raised my body from death to life. For so great and sudden a change occurred within me that it is impossible to express it in words. At that moment, I found myself free and loosed from all things; and it felt to me no different than if a heavy and horrific burden had been taken away from my heart; and as if the chains, which until then had held me in such a heavy prison, were now entirely rent and broken forever; since I found myself inwardly in such freedom that I no longer even recognized myself. In that moment, the great care and goodness of God toward me during my misery was shown to me; but with such..."

Thus far her words.

10. It is impossible to say what heartfelt praise and thanksgiving she offered to the Lord once she had come to herself a little. She thought she would melt into tears, and indeed into nothing but tears of love and joy; and the peace she felt in her heart was so great that it far exceeded all her previous unrest; she also found herself so abundantly showered with the graces and gifts of the Lord that it is impossible to recount them sufficiently.

> "The Lord," she said at times, "had healed her through a very strange means, namely through the very sensation of the disordered love of the creature <note>Armelle refers here to the intrusive lustful thoughts she suffered during her trial; she interprets the very thing that tormented her as the tool God used to break her pride and purify her.</note>; and had given her through the very greatest evil she had ever feared the greatest good she had desired; and had used the filth <note>original: "Unflat"</note> itself as a means to cleanse her; just as He once used mud <note>A reference to the Gospel of John 9:6, where Jesus heals a blind man using a paste of spit and dust.</note> when He wished to make the blind man in the Gospel see."

## The Sixth Chapter.

->Of the wound of love which she received in her heart. How she then came to live in a convent; but according to God’s will returned again to her first dwelling.<-

->I.<-

Until now we have seen this blessed creature <term>Creature: A common 17th-century term for a human being, emphasizing their status as a created work of God.</term> in constant change, as she continually passed from one state into another, where the latter was always harder and more troublesome than the previous ones: now it is time to see her in a firm and constant state. For the Lord, from that time on, as she herself used to say, placed her in an invincible fortress, where the attacks of all her enemies could not reach; and the overwhelming love with which her heart burned from that time on strengthened her to such an extent that nothing, neither from the world nor from the devil, could have shown itself that would not have been instantly extinguished and annihilated.

# of the good Armelle. Chapter VI.

2. Nevertheless, around this time she also submitted herself in obedience to the guidance of a pious Jesuit <note>The Jesuits, or the Society of Jesus, were a Catholic religious order known for their rigorous spiritual discipline and role as confessors to many 17th-century mystics.</note>, to whom she was led by Divine providence; to him she then opened up her previous as well as her present state, and through him she was not a little strengthened and confirmed in her extraordinary experiences.

3. Shortly thereafter, once this holy woman was rescued from the miserable servitude in which we have seen her, it happened one day—as she was contemplating the love that God had shown her in so many various occurrences, and therefore desired to respond in turn with such a powerful, fiery love—that she felt herself inwardly quite moved and ignited. Thereupon she began to plead with the Lord with great fervor that He might wound her heart with His divine love <note>The "wound of love" is a common theme in mystical literature, representing a spiritual experience so intense it feels like a physical piercing of the soul.</note>.

4. Her guide arranged for her to become acquainted with two other clergymen, namely with the famous Father Johannes Rigoleve <note>Jean Rigoleuc (1595–1658), a notable Jesuit spiritual director and associate of the mystic Jean-Joseph Surin.</note> and Father Hubi, who visited her often (especially the former) and found great refreshment in her company. These Fathers indeed endeavored to moderate this so powerful fervor of her love a little, and accordingly advised her that she should not let herself be carried away by the all too great intensity that she felt; however, it was not in her power to resist it: for she believed she must have died had she not loved in such a manner. She used to say to them often,
> "love alone was the cause of both
> "her life and also her torment; and that the few strengths she still
> "had, as well as her illness itself, came from the excessive power of her love."

5. Three or four years after the mentioned period of temptation passed with partly persistent, partly alternating illnesses; after which it happened that we (in the Ursuline Convent <note>The Ursulines are a religious order of women, founded by St. Angela Merici, who in this period often employed laywomen to assist with the practical running of the cloister.</note>) had need of a lay servant. We therefore requested the confessor of this good girl, in whom we had great confidence, that he might assign one to us; he then brought the good Armelle to us. And upon such an occasion Armelle came into our convent, although with much displeasure from her master and mistress <note>This refers to her previous domestic employers, who were likely reluctant to lose a worker of such renowned character.</note>. When she was in our house, she gradually began to regain her strength: not that she regained her full health, but she found herself much better than she had been in a long time. Because of the uncommon virtues we saw in her, we had a singular love for her and sought to give her all possible help; we also did not wish for her to perform any work that might have burdened her health in the slightest. Furthermore, she had another good person as her companion, who had been in service with us for a long time and loved her so heartily that she would not let her suffer the slightest inconvenience; rather, she would sooner do all our business herself than allow Armelle to perform any work that might have fatigued her too much. And thus she led a very gentle, quiet life with us.

6. She behaved so virtuously, quietly, modestly, and submissively that all our convent sisters who had dealings with her were edified by her to the highest degree. Often several had permission to go to her and converse with her; there

...it then gave them great pleasure to hear her speak of God and His holy love, especially on those days when she had been to the Table of the Lord <note>original: "Tisch des HErrn"; a reference to receiving Holy Communion or the Eucharist.</note>. One would have believed they were seeing and hearing a second holy Catherine of Siena, or of Genoa <note>St. Catherine of Siena (1347–1380) and St. Catherine of Genoa (1447–1510) were famous Italian mystics known for their intense, "fiery" descriptions of divine love.</note>, so fervent and fiery were her conversations. However, to enjoy such conversations, one had to know how to approach her with good manners and, as it were, help her to speak without her thinking about it; for otherwise she would not have done it. Her humility, and the reverence she held toward our spiritual sisters, was so great that in their presence she maintained a perpetual silence; nevertheless, when love overwhelmed her, or when one knew how to lead her to this subject, she then spoke of wondrous things, and it was plainly seen that the heart spoke through the mouth.

7. In this state she spent about a year and a half with great pleasure, during which time she fairly regained her health. And it seemed as if God had led her here for that very purpose. But afterwards she began to feel a loathing and vexation toward all the ease and convenience she had with us, because her inward impulse was always such that she was inclined toward hard things that were unpleasant to [human] nature. The more she was loved and held dear, the more it tormented her. It was unbearable to her spirit to see herself so well-satisfied and comfortable.

8. Later she was employed in the service of the boarding children <note>original: "Kost-Kinder"; children placed in the care of the religious house for their upbringing and education.</note>: which she performed with such friendliness and diligence that the young girls all loved her uncommonly and had such trust in her that she was their refuge; they also had such reverence for her that, although she was only a maid, they feared displeasing her no less than their superiors. Her mere presence, and the modesty that shone forth from her countenance, was more than enough to keep them to their duty.

9. We have already noted above that the soul of this person, despite all this peace and pleasure she received in our house, nevertheless found itself anxious and tormented, in that she felt a certain movement which gave her to understand that this was not the place where God wanted her to be. Nevertheless, she applied all her strength to tear herself away from this opinion, as she held that she could and should be nowhere better than in this house, where she had so many examples of virtue before her.

10. But finally, God gave her to recognize quite clearly that His will was for her to leave <note>original: "quittiren"; to quit or depart from.</note> this house, where, by all appearances, she could lack nothing and her nature would have found much pleasure. To this end, He now permitted her to begin feeling the vivacity of her passions strongly within herself again, which until now had been, as it were, quite dead: moreover, she found her nature, quite contrary to her habit, inclined to seek its own appetite and pleasure; although she did not follow them. But what dismayed her most of all was that she [felt] a noticeable change in her in-

## The Seventh Chapter.

### Concerning the various levels of love, through which she was led by God.

-> 1. <-

After we have shown in the preceding chapter how God, through the counsel and guidance of His divine Providence, finally brought His faithful servant back to the place He had destined for her for the remainder of her life; we must now show how our Lord allowed her to ascend continually through different grades, which served her, as it were, as so many steps or rungs to reach the highest summit of His divine love. In this extract of her life, however, we shall have to touch upon everything only briefly.

2. Of the intense and burning love, in which she spent three or four years after she had been delivered from her painful paths of suffering, we have already spoken above; to which we now add that this love in its beginning, and indeed for about a year, was mingled with great sorrow and bitterness, as she saw that her heart had been occupied with a love other than for her God <note>This refers to a period of "purification," where the soul feels grief over any past attachment that was not centered on the Divine.</note>. At times it felt as if her poor heart would truly break into pieces: which did not happen merely in thought or imagination; for she felt, in fact, a very piercing pain, as if one were cutting her apart or quartering her <note>Quartering was a brutal historical method of execution; Armelle uses it here to describe the visceral, physical sensation of her spiritual transformation.</note> while alive.

3. Following this, she entered a second state, which completely erased the sight and memory of her misery from her mind, so that she might remember only and alone the great mercy of God, which He had shown toward her.

4. Following this, there ensued such a great love that she, as already mentioned, became ill from it and thought she might die of it. She felt incessantly how her heart was entirely ignited and, as it were, pierced with a pointed arrow <note>The "piercing of the heart" is a common motif in mystical literature, famously described by St. Teresa of Avila, symbolizing a soul wounded by divine love.</note>, which caused in her such a vehement desire, and at the same time gave her such incredible strength to work for God’s sake.

And just so, she was also inwardly active in a holy manner through constant acts of adoration, thanksgiving, sacrifice, praise, self-annihilation <term>Vernichtigung: a mystical term referring to the total surrender of the self-will and ego to God</term>, and the glorification of God and His perfections. All of this was given to her without her having to exert herself or doing the slightest thing to raise herself up to God. She did everything in her power merely to receive what was given to her by His Divine Majesty, who poured His graces into this blessed creature with such abundance that, as she herself said, it seemed like a powerful stream and a mighty flood that sank her into a deep abyss. Therefore, not without cause, she sometimes broke out into these words: "Ah, my dearest Love, if the world knew and
"recognized the great and most inward sweetness that You let me feel every moment, 
"it would say that Your love toward me is far too excessive;
"and if I were permitted, I would say it myself." And again: "It truly seems, 
"o my dearest Love, as if You had no one else but me to pro-
"vide for and look after, though I am but a wretched maidservant; and yet it has 
"the appearance as if all things must happen solely for my sake."

5. At that same time, it also seemed to her as if she were constantly in a fiery and burning furnace, which ignited and consumed her heart and her whole body, and swallowed her up entirely, if I may speak so and use her own words with which she expressed this love: "Yes, (she said to her spiritual directors,) I am in a furnace, but one that is a thousand times more fiery than 
"all the furnaces of this world, which, in view of what I feel 
"within myself, seem to me to be ice-cold." And she said to God, complaining to Him in a lover-like fashion, as it were: "My Lord and my All, Your love and 
"Your kindnesses will yet take my life."

6. After God had kept her for a long time in this state of love—which one can call a violent, strong, active, and untiring love—and had weakened and dampened the liveliness of her natural powers (which He had often used until now in His violent workings) through the force of this love, He let her enter into another state, which was entirely contrary to the previous one. Because her nature had almost no strength left, she fell into such a faintness and weariness that she could hardly keep herself upright. The love that she then felt was much more vivid and piercing; but because it was further removed from the effects of the senses, it caused her much greater weakness than before; so that her life was now nothing other than a constant state of lingering illness and fading away.

10. Her mind <term>Gemüth: a term encompassing the soul’s disposition, will, and emotional center</term> was at that time always occupied with God and in God, just as in the first four years; but it was now in a completely different manner, because she was not so divided and multifaceted as before. For it was not various different motives, but God alone and the desire for His glorification that were now both the source and the object <note>original: "Vorwurf," which in this archaic German context refers to the "object" or "aim" of her attention</note> of her love, without regard for herself or for any personal advantage or benefit, which she had so completely forgotten that it felt to her as if she were no longer in the world. Her inner occupation was now much stronger, more intimate, gentler, more piercing, and more unceasing, without interruption, than before. I say *without interruption*, because it happened without so many repeated inner acts produced with such great force, which she had previously performed before she fell into these holy wearinesses and fainting spells. <note>In the tradition of "bridal mysticism," these fainting spells (*Ohnmachten*) represent the soul being so overwhelmed by divine love that the physical body weakens.</note>

## The Eighth Chapter.

### God leads her into a completely Divine and spiritual life, through the excellent path of total abandonment.

I.

From such a state, the good Armelle entered into another, wherein she found herself, as it were, enclosed and well-secured within the bosom of Divine Providence; this caused her such great inner peace that, strictly speaking, she was like a child in its mother's lap, having no other care than to let itself be led by her wherever she wishes. It was exactly thus with her in regard to God. All her desires, and all her wishes and intentions, were (at that time) aimed at no other goal than to surrender herself solely to Divine Providence, for better or for worse <note>original: "auf Gnade und Ungnade," literally "for grace or disgrace," an idiom for total, unconditional surrender</note>, so that He might deal with her according to His pleasure: from which then arose such a gentle and intimate union with God within her as she had never before experienced.

### Of the Good Armelle. Chapter VIII.

...[this] blessed creature <note>Armelle often refers to herself or is referred to as a "creature" to emphasize her humility before the Creator.</note> completely overwhelmed, and entirely swallowed her up. Therefore, because she could no longer set any goal or measure for it, nor restrain or hold back her heart, she was often compelled to throw herself upon the earth or upon a bed; there she spoke with her own heart as with a thing over which she no longer had any power, and as it were, turned it away from herself and surrendered it completely with the following words:

> "O go then (she said) and love as long and as much as you will; for I can no longer hinder or hold you back in this; you no longer belong to me; you belong solely and alone to Love."

3. All of this served as a way and preparation for God’s intention for her—namely, to transition her into another state—which occurred in the following manner: It happened around this time that Father Rigoleve <note>Jean Rigoleuc (1595–1658), a Jesuit priest and spiritual director known for his mystical teachings.</note> and her other guide both had to travel away at the same time to live in another place. When she, Armelle, heard of this, she was indeed a little moved by it, but she said to them:

> "Your absence, dear Fathers, truly goes to my heart; but if I knew that you would love God better in the city to which you are traveling than here, then I would wish that you were already there, even if I should never see you again."

Now when the day of their departure arrived, and Armelle was in the church, she felt that the impending separation weighed very heavily on her heart. Whatever effort she made to withdraw her thoughts from it, she could not succeed; because God allowed it to happen this way in order to prepare her for the grace He wished to show her. She complained heartily to Him and said:

> "Ah, my Lord, You take away all my help and leave me alone, without any human being to whom I could hold, who might make Your adorable will known to me. What shall I do now all alone, and to whom shall I have my refuge? Give Yourself to me as my signpost and guide, since You deprive me of those whom You had given me."

As these words entered her mind, the Savior spoke the following words to her inwardly and clearly:

> My daughter, I deal with you as one does with children who are taken from the arms of their nurses to be received into their father’s house, and to be given better nourishment than they had before: so will I also now receive you into my house.

Thereupon she said to Him: "Yes Lord, where is Your house?" Our Savior showed her the wound in His sanctified side, and thereby let her enter into His heart, and said to her:

> This is my house.

When she had entered therein, she found herself in a great emptiness <term>Ledigkeit: a mystical term for a state of being "void" or "free" from worldly attachments and self-will</term> and nakedness <term>Entblößung: the spiritual stripping away of all images, concepts, and ego</term>, such that she saw and recognized nothing in the least; whereupon she began to say: "My Lord, You say this is Your house; and I see and find nothing at all therein." To these words, no answer at all was given to her; but she found herself in a wonderful peace and rest.

However, evening had hardly come—after she had finished everything and done what was necessary in her household—when this Friend of her heart fulfilled more than abundantly the promise He had made to come to her. For in a moment He overwhelmed her with so many graces and rich blessings, and gave her at the same time an infallible certainty of His Divine presence, that she thought she would have to die from the overwhelming power of the sweetness and loveliness that flooded her from all sides; as she felt herself drowned and sunken in the unspeakable and immeasurable abyss of Love itself. 4. Around All Saints’ Day <note>November 1st.</note>, her dear Bridegroom (who had seemed absent from mid-August until that time) revealed Himself anew within her with such an abundance of Divine love and joy that her heart almost wanted to pass away because of its greatness. 5. After she had enjoyed these sweetnesses and kisses of love for several days, her spirit was again enclosed, as before, in an unwavering and simple attention to God, without recognizing anything in particular about Him. Nature <note>In mystical theology, "Nature" refers to the human self, the physical body, and its fallen impulses, which often struggle against the "Spirit."</note>, on the other hand, allowed itself to be pulled down (though without any delight) toward those things that were suitable to it; this felt very burdensome to her spirit. Nevertheless, her spirit accepted everything with patience and was content to hold the reins tight so that nature might not receive even the slightest bit of pleasure: or rather, God did this within her; for on her own part, she was without any action in all things.

6. Here, however, it is to be noted—to clarify what follows—that despite all the graces and extraordinary favors with which our Savior adorned and gifted the soul of His faithful bride according to His heart's desire and pleasure, and notwithstanding the perfect submission under which He brought all her passions, as well as the absolute power He gave her over all devils and their schemes (whom she only laughed at and regarded as less than a fly), and finally the total silencing and mortification <note>The practice of "killing off" one's own desires to be closer to God.</note> of all her desires or inclinations in everything that did not aim at His holy service; that despite all this, I say, He left a Philistine <note>A biblical metaphor for a lingering enemy or persistent temptation that God allows to remain to test a person's faith, referencing the nations left in the land of Canaan to test the Israelites.</note> in her land for more than twenty-four years to exercise her virtue; I mean to say, another "nature" that was still always inclined and eager to seek its own small comforts and pleasures. And although the spirit mostly took care that nature found manifold suffering even in those things wherein it thought to enjoy itself, nature did not retreat for that reason, but always sought to snatch something for itself, as if by stealth.

Since God had opened to her the entrance into this Divine life, of which we have reported until now, this enemy had not dared to show itself; but after the spirit had entered into this great seclusion and stripping away <note>The mystical process of "divestment" or "poverty of spirit," where the soul lets go of all images and earthly attachments.</note> of which we speak here,

And from then on, it happened that the love and the inner joy within her increased greatly, together with such a sweet and most intimate union of God and her spirit, that it seemed to her she had become **One with Him.**

### Of the Good Armelle. Chapter X.

...who at such a time <note>Likely referring to the season of Carnival or Shrove Tuesday, a period traditionally associated with revelry and excess before the fasting of Lent.</note> give full freedom to all shame and vice. This poor soul did not know what she should do to turn away or restrain such things; with a heart full of love, she said to our **Savior**: “O my Love and my All, I see, alas! that all the hearts of men bar the entrance to You, and that You are rejected and driven away by everyone, so that You do not know in what place You should make Your dwelling. See, I offer and present myself to You, so that You may find Your rest and shelter in me.” When she had said this, it seemed to her that our Savior accepted her offer at that very moment. And indeed, He shared Himself with her so abundantly that she could not doubt His real presence at all; for He met her with such loving caresses and heart-enchanting friendliness that, when telling of it, she said it seemed to her as if **GOD** had no one else in this world but her alone upon whom He wished to bestow His love and kindness; so incomprehensibly great was the love with which He did this.

2. This took place in the year 1651. And because her love was now so greatly kindled, the pain over the many offenses committed against this adorable Majesty was also more violent and piercing within her; so much so that, in order to check such great sins and prevent so much evil, she offered herself to her Divine Love and pleaded fervently: “That He might lay upon her all the torment and pain that He Himself willed, in order to prevent Him from being offended any further.”

3. At another time, she found herself suddenly seized by such a burning desire to love her Beloved that she remained quite speechless and lost the use of her senses because of it. And because she saw that it was impossible for her to satisfy her desire due to her great weakness, she felt an incredible sadness over it; for, as she used to say: “To suffer for **GOD’S** sake is a delight; but not to be able to love Him enough is a great martyrdom.” Then our Savior spoke to her in the innermost ground of her soul <note>original: "innigsten Grunde ihrer Seele." In mystical theology, the "ground of the soul" refers to the deepest, most essential part of a person where they can encounter the Divine directly.</note>: *I give you my love; love me as much as you want.* In the same moment that she heard these words, her heart was seized and ignited by a burning fire of love, which seemed so Divine and piercing to her that everything she had felt until then was as nothing in comparison to this present fire; and it seemed to her, as she testified to me, that from this moment on, she only truly began to love as is proper.

## The Eleventh Chapter.

->She lives thereafter quite calmly in the enjoyment of her Good,<-
->without self-interest. She enters into GOD, and remains in Him,<-
->without fear of falling. Her transformation and loss of self<-
->in GOD.<-

1. After this holy person had obtained the glorious victories over her enemies that we have now described, **GOD** established her in the enjoyment and possession of her goods. "All my Good (she said then) is **GOD** alone: and because He is now, through His great mercy and goodness, entirely my own, just as I am entirely His own, I no longer have any need to labor to acquire anything new. I have nothing further to do than to retire to rest within His goods. And just as He rests in me, so I also rest in Him, after I have been completely enclosed in Him and fully annihilated <note>In 17th-century mysticism, "annihilation" refers to the total surrender of the ego or "self-will," allowing the soul to be filled entirely by God's will.</note>. There, I no longer find myself. And when I say I enjoy, I love, I possess, it is no longer I who receive such things; rather, His love is my love; His wealth is my wealth; His peace is my rest; His ways are my delight and pleasure: and so it is also with all His other divine perfections. And now there is nothing left that I could desire. For I am quite overwhelmed with goods, nor do I need to fear—

2. Once, as she was moved to pray in merciful love for all people, it happened that while she was in the midst of prayer, a curtain was drawn, as it were, before her eyes; whereas previously she had possessed a singular insight into the needs of her neighbor. At that same time, our Savior <note>German: Heyland</note> made His presence felt in the innermost ground of her soul, according to His usual way, and spoke to her as if He were jealous over the love of His beloved: **My daughter, love me alone:** whereupon she answered with very great fervor: **“Yes, my Love, I will do it, I will, I will!”**, and could not refrain from constantly repeating these words, *I will, I will*, within her interior; but with such love and such fire as is inexpressible.

3. She went to receive <term>Holy Communion</term> <note>The central Christian ritual of the Eucharist, where the bread and wine are received as the body and blood of Christ.</note> and still kept saying those same words; which, however, at that time were changed into the following: **Finally Love is enclosed, finally Love is enclosed;** she could have nothing else in her heart but these words, which she always said to herself, just as she had done with the previous ones; until she went home again, at which point these words ceased in the middle of the way. And at that same time, our Savior performed such a sweet and loving effect in the most secret ground of her soul that it is a wonder she did not remain lying there on the spot, motionless. For He gave her to understand that just as He, the essential and infinite Love, was enclosed in her; so He (a) also wished to lead her into Himself, to transform her, and to incorporate her into Himself. And in that same moment, she truly found herself in the immeasurable love of the Godhead, as if dead and passed away. What she then experienced within herself is impossible to express with words. She herself knew nothing else to say of it, except that she could not say the slightest thing about it.

4. But this show of grace was not the only one she received. Her dear Love, who had given her, so to speak, a taste or a glimpse of the glory of the blessed, wished also (in a certain way) to make her a partaker of the same. For just as she, in the bliss of the saints, had most wondered at the great love and the unceasing beholding of the Godhead, wherein the essence of their bliss consists: so our Savior also granted her the grace that He let her behold His glory and divine attributes, and especially His infinite love, within herself, with such clarity that she was thereby completely deified <note>German: vergöttert; a mystical term for being united with God's nature.</note> and transformed by Him, or changed into Him; indeed, it seemed to her she had now (b) become one with Him. Therefore, you also take care that you remain always faithful and submissive to my will. Yet do not fear that this misfortune of falling from my grace shall ever befall you. For I will always preserve you through my mercy, as a fruit that I have gathered and set aside for myself alone.

9. The inexpressible love and sweetness that flowed to her through this divine mark of grace brought forth these enamored words from the deepest ground of her heart, which she directed to our Savior: “O my Love and my All, so You are then the Jailer <note>original: "Kerkermeister"</note> of my heart, which You hold captive and bound.” After she had said this, she remained quite still, and enjoyed in great peace, according to every desire, the wonderful and magnificent delight and pleasure of her pleasant prison.

10. At the same time she commonly said: “If even the least thing were still in or about me that existed through myself, it would long ago have been consumed by the intensity of this love. But because I no longer see myself, nor anything that is in me, as being in myself, but rather my whole being is in God, and never departs from Him—so that no nourishment can be given to my own self-interest <note>original: "Eigenheit," referring to the "self" or ego</note> (as I am lost and swallowed up in Him)—so I exist, and carry my life about, solely through the power that He gives me, until it pleases Him to cut short its course, which stands alone in His pleasure. For on my part, through His great mercy, there is nothing more that could keep me longer in this world.”

11. On the following Thursday, our Savior showed her yet another very special mark of grace. Namely, He gave her to understand: He wished that from now on she should be like the little snails <note>The snail was a common 17th-century emblem for the contemplative life, representing a soul that carries its "home" (God) with it and withdraws from the world at the slightest touch.</note>, which always, wherever they go, carry their house and dwelling with them and never depart from it; and as soon as something strikes or attacks them, they draw themselves in and hide in such a way that nothing but their shell is seen, while they themselves no longer let themselves be glimpsed in the least. Thus, He Himself wished to be her dwelling, her house, and her place of refuge, from which she should never depart; He wished to hide and enclose her within Himself in all places and in all circumstances, so that nothing more should be seen in her but He Himself alone. At that very hour, she found herself enclosed in this Divine dwelling more than ever before, with such a clear and certain knowledge <note>original: "Erkentniß"</note> of the glory, excellence, and beauty of the place where she was, that she cried out from the innermost part of her heart: “O my dear Love, it is two years today since You, through Your great mercy, let me enter into Your house; nor have You ever permitted me to depart from it for even a single moment: and nonetheless, it seems to me that I am only now just entering, so many things do I now see and recognize within it which I have not recognized or perceived until now;” which she said because of the magnificent insights that God revealed to her of His Divine perfections, which until then had not yet been discovered by her.

# The Twelfth Chapter.

## The Savior imprints His name into her heart. She falls into a sickness. Powerful drawings of love. Revelation of the Holy Trinity; and other Divine communications.

---

->1.<-

On the first day of the following year, 1652, at the very break of day when she awoke, she found her heart seized by a living flame of love, which seemed to ignite her through and through. At the same time, she had a certain inner premonition that her Heart-Beloved would undoubtedly give her a New Year’s gift on this day; although she did not know in what way or manner it might happen, because her heart was so full that she thought it was not capable of holding more. Nevertheless, she had a strong impression that He had still reserved a most magnificent favor for her. She said to Him several times, without even thinking about it: “My Love, I believe You wish to give me my New Year’s gift this morning.”

And such indeed came to pass; for on this very day, the Savior imprinted His blessed name JESUS into the ground of her heart in a most wonderful manner; so much so that she said to everyone she came to speak with, as if with a Seraphic tongue <note>Like a Seraph, the highest order of angels, traditionally associated with burning love and fire.</note>:

> “Give, oh, do give your hearts to Jesus,
> “so that He may imprint His Holy name therein. He desires nothing but this. He is
> “quite ready to do this grace for all those who wish to surrender themselves to Him. Yes,
> “give Him your hearts, so that He may do with them whatever pleases Him.”

2. Some time thereafter, the good Armelle fell into a severe illness, in which she also expected to die. During this, she noticed a small fear of death within herself, for which she had otherwise so greatly longed. When she wondered at this and searched for the cause, she found that it came from the fact that [death] would see her freed from sickness and pain, and thus she would no longer be able to suffer for the sake of her Love. Her own words, with which she made known her state of mind in this regard, were as follows:

> “I wondered at the fact that I
> “feared death, because my Love is my witness that, through His great mercy,
> “I no longer have any will of my own, and His will alone is my will;
> “furthermore, I do not fear being judged by Him, nor do I shrink back before
> “Hell itself, because, if it were His Divine will, I would be just as
> “willing and ready to go into it as into Heaven: although I also
> “well know that I deserve nothing other than the hellish fire. The only cause
> “which made me fear death was because it would take away the means
> “of suffering for the sake of my Divine Love, for whose sake I would nevertheless gladly
> “suffer until the Last Judgment.”

In the meantime, she recovered from this illness within a few weeks.

->of the good Armelle. Chapter XII.<-

> "[the]se words spoken, (she says further,) the following were answered to me, and indeed with such emphatic power that I could not doubt at all that our Savior Himself had said them to me: **Nothing in the least.** And He repeated for the second time: **Nothing, nothing in the least, except only to surrender yourself, and let me act.** At these words, everything was calm and content in my soul; and I could do nothing further than to remain lying under the yoke and gentle burden of love that overwhelmed me, and to die from its flames."

8. Once again, the Savior gave her His Divine Presence to feel in a quite extraordinary way, as it seemed to her as if she saw one person who wanted to hide and protect another; and at the same time He gave her a strong impression, through which it was given to her to recognize that He Himself would henceforth always stand between her and all misfortune that might happen to her, in order to prevent anything from approaching her. From that time on, she found herself so surrounded and guarded by Divine protection that it seemed to her as if JESUS and His holy love had made Himself, as it were, into a strong wall to keep and protect her; and as if she were enclosed in God, as in a firm tower and invincible fortress, where not the least thing could approach or come to touch her. And in truth, everything that might thereafter have moved or contested her, God Himself took upon Himself, as she saw, so that she felt nothing of it, no differently than if she had entirely lost her own being; over which she, full of wonder, often said to herself: 

> "O you poor Armelle, where are you? Because neither the world, nor the devil, nor sin, can find or touch you anymore."

Whereupon the Divine inner-word answered her: 

> **You are no more; you are lost in the great sea of my Divinity, much more than a fish in the ocean.**

9. On the first of October of this year, God showed her a very singular token of grace, which consisted in a entirely new strengthening and confirmation of her being in God; of which she afterwards said: 

> "Since then, I feel myself held and strengthened so powerfully in God that one might say it is no longer possible in any way that I should be moved or drawn out of it, and this is the place of my right and natural dwelling in time and eternity."

> "I see my soul (thus she further described her state of mind at that time) loose and free from all things, so pure, so solitary, so detached, that it seems as if it no longer dwells in my body, which, as it seems to me, does nothing else than follow the soul, as if insensibly. Second Part. The Life.

„[consu]med; and through this consumption it is spread out in such a way that I can see no goal nor end to it. Before, I wanted to do everything and grasp everything; but now it is quite different with me, for nothing approaches me anymore. I grasp everything, and am grasped by nothing. My soul is solitary, simple, and pure; and when I see it thus, I see a great wonder. If this continues in me for some time longer, I believe that I shall have to die from it. I go and act in outward things according to my habit, without losing this vision: but my God takes it from me at times, as He allows some thoughts to come into my mind that turn me away from it; otherwise, I would have already died. The love that consumes me, no one can either express or comprehend. It is as if infinite; and yet it grows more every day." Thus far go her own words.

„The Spirit of God (she said further) animates my soul, and gives it all the life and all the movement it has. His life is my life; His heart is my heart; through Him alone it is that I draw breath and live."

---

# The Thirteenth Chapter.

### Concerning the graces that God showed her from the beginning of the year 1653 until the end of the same.

->I.<-

In the following year, 1653, the Lord showed her, among other things, a special grace, which she herself expresses in the following words: "I found myself lodged and enclosed in the sacred heart of Jesus <note>Devotion to the Sacred Heart (the physical heart of Jesus as a symbol of divine love) was a central theme in 17th-century Catholic mysticism, particularly in France.</note>, with such great love, glory, and freedom that I could not comprehend it myself. I dwelt there very spaciously and quite comfortably. Nothing shut me in or narrowed me. I saw this divine heart to be of such great vastness that a thousand worlds would not be enough to fill it. Moreover, I saw that all those who betake themselves to dwell therein out of love enjoy true and perfect freedom, as well as a glorious peace. However, on the other hand, I saw that the door through which one had to enter was so small and narrow that very few found the entrance; whereat, full of wonder, I said: O my Love and my All, why is it that your heart is so great and so wide, and one has such good room when one is inside, yet the door through which one enters is so small and narrow? Then our Lord gave me to understand that this was because He did not want anyone else to come in but small, naked <note>In this context, "naked" (nackende) refers to a soul stripped of all worldly attachments, pride, and self-will.</note>, and solitary people. The small are those who humble and abase themselves with all their heart for His sake. These can come in; but the others not at all. For how is it possible that a thick, large [person], and [one full] of great self-esteem—

### Of the Good Armelle. Chapter XIII.

...arrogance and imagination, an inflated person, go through such a small door? The naked are those who strip their hearts of the desire for the goods and comforts of this life. For the others, who are hung and burdened with much gold and silver, or other things, it is impossible to pass through such a narrow place, unless they first lay down their burden. The solitary ones are those who withdraw their love from all creatures <note>In 17th-century spiritual writing, "creatures" refers to any created thing or person other than God.</note>. For love binds and joins the heart with that which it loves; but now, two persons bound together cannot pass at the same time through a place where there is room for only one, and even then, a rather small person."

2. At another time, she reflected within herself whether anything would henceforth be powerful enough to turn her gaze away from such a lovely object <note>original: "Vorwurf" - here meaning the object of her contemplation or the focus of her attention.</note> again, and she made the resolution to avoid all opportunity in the future through which she might fall into this misfortune; whereby she spoke from the deepest ground of her heart:
"O nevermore, my Love, no, nevermore will I allow myself to be found
with anyone who could give me cause to think of anything other than
Thee! For I cannot remain anywhere else for even a single moment
but with Thee."
As she was in these holy movements of love, our Savior gave her to understand that she was fixed to the trunk of the Tree of Life: this tree was **GOD**; no matter what might come, nothing would be able to separate her from it for all eternity.

These latter words caused a very great effect in her heart, through the exceeding love that they ignited within it. Indeed, it seemed to her as if for several days she constantly heard the voice of her Beloved, who always said this very thing to her; whereby she was then moved to make the following request to Him: "Why, my Love and my All, do You say to me that I am fixed to the trunk of the Tree of Life, and not to the branches?" "Therefore, my daughter," our Savior answered her, "because you are fixed to me alone, who am the stock and the trunk of eternal life; but not to my gifts and graces, which are only the branches that can be cut off and separated, along with those who cling to them: but those who, just like you, unite themselves with the trunk and want nothing but **Me Alone**, they shall not be separated from it for all eternity."

3. That this pure soul was truly one who clung not to the graces and gifts, but to the Giver Himself, was shown in the new state into which she was placed around Easter of this same year, which she describes with the following words: "I found myself, in regard to my Divine Love, like one who, after having associated much and conversed familiarly with his intimate friend, and having seen and heard all his secrets and fully enjoyed the delight of his love, notices that his friend wants to do something for his benefit, of which he, out of even greater kindness, wants him to know nothing until he has completed his undertaking, and therefore [he] **holds** <note>The catchword at the bottom of the page indicates the next word in the sentence is "holds" (hält).</note> everything he does hidden from him."

# Second Part. The Life etc.

“...holds. See how it was with me at the beginning of this state. I knew well that my only Love was enclosed in the innermost part of my soul, and that He worked there for His glory and my benefit; but I did not know what He was doing. My spirit was at the door of this sanctuary, yet in such a way that it neither dared nor wanted to go inside. Thus I was during the Easter holidays and the eight following days, after which time I saw myself so poor and stripped of everything that I had never been in such great need. Nothing, either from without or from within, remained in my spirit with which it could occupy itself. It seemed to me that I no longer had faith, nor love, nor attention toward my God, except occasionally, and rarely enough. I wondered a little at this so new condition; but nonetheless wanted no other, because, through the mercy of my God, I had no other will than His.

4. “After eight or ten days, as I went to receive <term>Holy Communion</term> <note>original: "H. Communion"</note>, my Divine Love gave me to understand that He had taken from me everything I had; just as one does to those who are declared spendthrifts and are deprived of the freedom to use their goods <note>In the 17th century, a 'spendthrift' (Verschwender) could be legally declared incompetent, losing control over their property to a guardian. Armelle uses this as a metaphor for God taking control of her soul's 'assets'.</note>. Then I said to Him: ‘I do not wonder then, O my Love, when You hide Yourself from me: for when one wants to have someone declared a spendthrift, one tells him nothing of it until all is done. So You have also done toward me, in that You have made me poor and stripped me of all things. O may Your holy name be praised into eternity!’ After these words I remained as I was before; and when I gave my spiritual director <note>original: "geistlichen Führer"</note> news of my condition, he said to me that things had never stood better with me than now; because everything that one can see, receive, or experience of God in this world is not purely God: God intended a still closer approach in my soul through this stripping and poverty, which was certainly so great that I clearly saw my nothingness. My spirit was entirely free, and nothing occupied it, and it remained thus until Ascension.

5. “In these openings and inclinations of love, I spent many days; whereupon I returned to my first state, where I now feel nothing but a holy and divine flame; which is nothing else but the pure, unadulterated love of my God, who takes His pleasure in me and loves Himself in me: and while He loves Himself in this manner, He annihilates and consumes me, and transforms me entirely into Himself, and thus He makes my life more than human.

6. In this same year, God allowed Himself to be seen for a certain time in the innermost part of her soul, in the manner of a great sea which had no goal nor boundaries. “When I was there,” (she said,) “my Love gave me to understand that, just as a fish cannot live or exist outside the water; in the same way, I could no longer live a single moment outside Him: and just as a fish, wherever it turns, always finds the water; so too would I always find Him, in whatever place or in whatever state I might be.”

# The Fourteenth Chapter.

## The Lord leaves her on earth only so that she may further the salvation of mankind, and that she may feel their sins.
## Love’s close watch over the slightest faults.

---

->1.<-

After we have touched upon some of the graces that God bestowed upon this blessed servant <note>The original term "Dienstmagd" refers to Armelle's social station as a domestic maidservant, which she maintained despite her deep mystical life.</note> in the year 1653, we now come to the remarkable things that occurred with her in the following year. On the first day of the year 1654, Divine Mercy gave her such a violent and burning desire for pain and suffering that she thought she could no longer live in this world if her Divine Love did not provide her with the means to quench this thirst, which God Himself had ignited in her heart. Therefore, she complained incessantly with heartfelt and loving words to the Savior, saying: “It was not right that He should overwhelm her with such graces and kindnesses; at the very least, He should give her something to suffer, or even take her out of this world.” To comply with her wish, our Savior gave her to understand that this year would be a year of suffering and pain for her.

2. She had not yet traversed much of the year when her Divine Love revealed to her the source of such impending suffering; which was the very same source that had been powerful enough to put God Himself into suffering and to take His life: namely, the sins of men and the loss of their souls.

3. Not long before Lent <note>original: "Fasten"</note>, her Heart’s Beloved—full of mercy and compassion over the loss of so many souls bought with His precious blood—gave her to understand through a divine impression that He willed for her to work with all her might to rescue poor, miserable sinners from sin. To this end, He said to her in the innermost part of her soul: *My heart’s beloved, you have become so much the property of Love that I leave you in this world for no other reason than that I may draw your brothers, who distance themselves from Me through their sins, back to Me.* And in that same moment, He gave her such a deep, painful sensation of seeing her God so despised by His own creatures <note>original: "Creaturen"</note>, as well as such a piercing sorrow that they were thus being lost, that she could no longer doubt what kind of suffering our Savior intended to strike her heart with when He prompted her to desire it so fervently at the beginning of the year. And just as a sick or sorrowful person can express their pain and agony better than another, I will also cite her own words to represent, to some extent, that which she experienced:

8. How very much the most holy eyes of Divine Love watched over the purity of this His bride can be inferred from the following, among other things: It once happened, after she had gone to the country after All Saints’ Day, that she had heavy work there which caused her a great indisposition <note>The text uses "Unpäßlichkeit," suggesting a period of illness or physical malaise brought on by overwork.</note> for more than five weeks. It then happened that she relaxed a little from the great severity that she otherwise used against her body, under circumstances that seemed quite reasonable to her and even seemed necessary to regain her health. But this Divine Eye, which always looked upon her and could not tolerate the slightest blemish in this beautiful likeness <term>Contrefait: A term borrowed from French meaning a portrait or image; here it refers to Armelle's soul as a reflection of the Divine.</term>, did not delay in showing her how these small liberties did not please Him at all, in that He hid His Divine Presence a little from her, so that she was less united with His Majesty than usual and was left more to herself.

As soon as she recognized this, she went and threw herself at the feet of her confessor with frequent tears and bitter remorse. She accused herself of her minor faults just as the greatest evildoer, moved by a living contrition <term>Zerknirschung: A deep, spiritual "crushing" of the heart or profound remorse for having offended God.</term>, might do for his gross vices.

9. At another time it happened that she encountered a certain person who claimed to lead a godly life, and yet made no conscience of many small faults for which she had often been reminded, but after which no improvement followed. From this, the good Armelle wanted to conclude that this person’s godliness must undoubtedly be a feigned pretense; but then these words were spoken to her inwardly: *To judge hearts belongs to me.*

# The Fifteenth Chapter.

**Her state of mind during the long-term illness of her mistress and other members of the household. The effects of Divine Love in her, in the year 1657. The great purity of her life.**

->I.<-

When our Savior wished to call the mistress of our good Armelle to Himself, He sent her a long and arduous illness in which this faithful maid showed her every possible service and help, and indeed with such untiring diligence that she left her neither day nor night, except when the highest necessity required it. This caused Armelle to come to me very rarely during the two and a half years that this illness lasted; for which reason I cannot say what might have occurred in her soul until the departure of her dear mistress, which took place in the month of October of the year 1656.

2. When I saw her some time thereafter, and inquired after the particular circumstances in which her soul had been, she said to me: "She could not remember them, nor think of anything else other than **bare love**, <note>original: "bloße Liebe." In mystical tradition, this refers to a state of simple, direct focus on God without the use of images or complex thoughts.</note> which usually held her in the state of **purity and poverty** (which I have described previously)."

3. I asked her whether, during the illness of her mistress and the other members of the household—most of whom had also been sick—any resentment or impatience had come upon her, because all these sick people had sought refuge with her, and she had often been almost as exhausted as those she attended? She answered: "Not in the least, through the mercy of my God; for His goodness toward His worthless creature is so great that He keeps me constantly in perfect obedience toward Him, so that nothing moves within me except by and according to His command."

4. It should also be noted here that God, during that entire time as long as the illness of her mistress lasted, allowed the soul of this holy maid the free use of her natural powers, and communicated to her almost no extraordinary grace that might have prevented her from performing all the services she was bound to show her dear mistress. However, soon after the passing of her mistress, she again felt the **Divine Influences**, <term>Göttlichen Einflüsse: A term for the direct "inflow" of God's grace or presence into the soul, often experienced as a physical or emotional sensation.</term> which poured into her soul with much greater intensity, the more they seemed to have been held back and suspended by the previously mentioned occasion.

5. It happened, therefore, around the time of Christmas 1657, that the Savior revealed to her, through a ray of His light, the deep abyss of His goodness, His friendliness, His peace, and His rest; all of which Divine qualities she saw as infinite, and yet dwelling in the very center of her heart. Then He showed her how she possessed all these treasures in the innermost ground of her soul; He also gave her, at the same time, these qualities of His which He had revealed to her—as far as she was capable of receiving them—to feel within herself; in such a way that it seemed to her she had become nothing but goodness, nothing but peace, nothing but friendliness and rest. No other thought came into her mind, nor could she speak any other words than these: "O goodness of my God! O friendliness of my God! O peace of my God! O, it seems to me, if I were permitted to throw only the smallest little spark of the holy love I feel into the hearts of men, it would be powerful enough to ignite them all, even if they were ice-cold."

6. As she told me of this high grace, she was in such an exalted state, and so filled with love and gratitude for the kindnesses God had shown her, that it appeared as if her heart would burst into pieces; and she let out such deep and piercing sighs that one might have said her soul was about to part from her body. Her conversation with me was so sublime that it is not in my power to recount it. I will only add something of it here: "O infinite goodness of my God (she said), how great is Your love toward Your worthless creature! O, who can comprehend this union which You have made! A union of an **earthworm** <note>original: "Erdwurm." A common 17th-century metaphor for human humility and lowliness in the face of the Divine.</note> with the Divine—

# of the good Armelle. Chapter XV.

„Divine Majesty! A union that is never interrupted! A union
„that has made me like You! Then my love, which is the bond
„of this union, is a communication <note>original: "Mittheilung." This refers to God sharing or imparting His own attributes to the soul.</note> of Your infinite love toward Your
„creatures; and the holiness that makes me holy is a communication
„of Your holiness. Oh, how long it has been since any unrest or conflict
„has been in this poor heart, because You govern it. In short,
„my God, I no longer exist; but You alone live in me.„

7. In this very year, it happened once that she committed a fault which
seemed hardly to be one; nonetheless, the Lord reminded her of it with these words:
**This misfortune has happened to you because you looked at yourself. Therefore, go
out, out of yourself, without any goal or measure, so that you look at no one but
Me.**

8. Another time, as her heart was as if swallowed up in the great overflows of love,
our Savior let her hear these glorious and truly wonderful words: **See, my daughter, how I give
Myself to you as nourishment? Thus I will, on My part, in turn, that you also serve
Me as nourishment and food.** <note>This bold metaphor of reciprocal "eating" is common in 17th-century mysticism, symbolizing a union so complete that the individual's identity is "consumed" by God.</note> These words put her into such a deep annihilation <term>Vernichtung: In this context, it does not mean destruction, but "ego-death"—the total emptying of the self to make room for God.</term> of herself, and caused her such a piercing fire of love, that she no longer
knew herself, and in this excessive fervor said such sweet and loving words to our
Savior that they cannot be described. Especially, however, she implored Him
that He would rather give all these marks of favor to so many other poor souls
who did not yet love Him, because they did not yet recognize His Divine goodness.

9. This request of hers, which she made very often in her life, was partially
heard. For since this last grace, she spent almost the rest of her days in such a way
that our Savior no longer communicated any extraordinary grace to her. God, however,
had by no means forsaken her; rather, what He worked in the deepest ground of her
soul was so high and Divine that she herself could not grasp it, nor could she
make it understood to others.

10. I wish to add here what she once spoke to her spiritual director,
and afterward at various times to me, when I inquired of her concerning her inward
condition; and I will summarize it all into one speech.

„My Father, <note>original: "Pater." Armelle's spiritual director was likely a Jesuit or Franciscan friar.</note> (she said to her spiritual director,) I believe that my Love
„and my All has finally heard the prayer which I have so often made to Him: that He
„would withdraw all His tokens of grace and favor from me, and give them to those
„who do not know Him; so that by this means they might be moved to love Him
„with their whole heart; and that I would most gladly deprive myself of all goods
„so that my God might be loved even by a single soul. He
„knows that I have never desired anything else but Him alone; and now He gives
„Himself to me in this way as well.„

> „He is enclosed in this poor heart and governs it as God. I am certain that He is within it. O how great is the peace and the stillness that reigns there! Truly, there is nothing more in this poor heart than God alone; a state which is almost like eternal life.“

Upon this, she turned to her Divine Love with these words: „O my Love and my All, who would have ever thought to see this heart in such a state as it is now! O Love, although You are always the very same, You are nevertheless varied in Your workings; and how finely You know how to adapt Yourself to our weaknesses! Where is the time, O Divine Love, when You showed Yourself in this heart as a victor and a conqueror, armed with fire and flames, to burn, ignite, and consume everything that opposed Your Divine Will? At that time, You pierced it with Your arrows in such a way that I thought daily I must die from it; You also gave it no rest until You had completely overcome and conquered it. Afterwards, O Divine Love, You ruled within it as a mighty and peaceable King, as a kind and merciful Father, and as a most beloved and generous Bridegroom, when You distributed Your tokens of grace and favor with such abundance, known only to You, O Divine Love: and now You rule within it as God; yes, my God, You are within it just as You are in Yourself, incomprehensible and inaccessible, in this poor heart, which You preserve in such a way that nothing can approach it except You alone.“

11. From these words one can perceive the inward state of this precious soul in her final years, in which God communicated Himself to her in the manner mentioned above, namely, as God. Not that He did not occasionally let her feel the flames of His Divine Love much more strongly and piercingly at one time than at another; but because it did not occur by means of an external object <note>original: „Vorwurfs.“ In this context, it refers to a mental representation or a specific object of thought that triggers an emotion; her experience was now direct and formless.</note>, she could not make it understood. She also possessed this presence of God constantly, just as we have said: and as for her outward appearance, nothing extraordinary was found therein, revealing nothing other than a high holiness in all her actions. She was, moreover, in reasonably good health, with a free and self-possessed mind, in order to fulfill the duties of her station.

# The Sixteenth Chapter.

# of the Good Armelle. Chapter XVI.

...to proceed toward the conclusion, we shall examine in a few chapters, first, her humility and dying to self <term>Abgestorbenheit: A mystical term referring to "mortification" or the process of becoming "dead" to worldly desires and the ego</term>, as the true fundamental virtues, in particular; and then, secondly, her daily exercises or her walk with God, in general. See here some expressions of her self-disregard:

> 2. „How is it even possible (she said) that a worthless maid, a poor peasant girl, an earthworm such as I am, could have any pride or haughtiness? I would have to be either deprived of my senses if I were to fall into that, or else not know at all what I do know. That God has mercy on me; that He has so greatly dignified me that He Himself took care to teach and instruct me, and to impart more light and knowledge to me than other peasant women like me are usually accustomed to having; that He has preceded me with His grace and ignited and even consumed me through His Divine Love: all of this has surely happened solely through His pure goodness and mercy, and not through me, nor through any of my good works. For if God wanted to deal with me according to these works of mine, He could give me nothing but Hell, and in Hell no other place than under the feet of Lucifer <note>The name for the fallen angel or the devil</note>, because that would actually be the place I deserved; although His great mercy nonetheless gives me hope that He will deal with me not according to my works, but according to His goodness.„

> 3. „This knowledge and feeling of her own lowliness and nothingness was so deeply rooted in her soul that she said: „Even if an angel or a saint came down from heaven and assured me that there was something good in her that came from herself, she would not believe him at all; for (she added) as soon as the matter came from me and belonged to me, it would, for that very reason, be worthless and evil. My greatest honor consists in seeing that I have nothing, and that everything I may have is not mine, but belongs to God, my only Love. I also want to let everything return purely to Him without claiming the slightest bit of it for myself. If, through His mercy, I have committed no great and coarse sins, He alone has preserved me from them; and I know that if He were to leave me to myself for one moment, I would commit much greater sins than any human being has ever committed. And thus I can well believe that I have deserved nothing but Hell, and that I would be the very greatest sinner in the whole world if my Divine Love were to leave me.„

4. Regarding the extraordinary favors and graces that God allowed to happen to her, she received them with such inward gratitude and such deep humility that she often did not know where to go or how to behave. And if she had not been powerfully encouraged by Love, she often would not have dared to lift her eyes toward heaven, so greatly ashamed and bewildered was she by so many graces. Hear how she herself spoke of it:

### Second Part. The Life

> „The more kindness my Divine Love <note>Armelle frequently refers to God as "my Love" or "Divine Love."</note> showed me, the more I saw my own lowliness and my nothingness; so that I was often completely confounded and outside of myself that such a High Majesty would choose to communicate in such a way with a poor servant girl. And sometimes I said to myself: If I did not know all too well that God, my Love, knows and sees everything, I would believe He did not see my misery. Often, even these thoughts were completely taken from me: for Love led me beyond myself, and did not permit me to keep my eyes and mind fixed on myself, or on anything that concerned me. And as for the great graces that my Love showed me, they were forgotten by me as soon as I had told them to my confessors <note>original: Beicht-Väter; spiritual directors to whom she confessed her internal experiences</note>: for Love filled me so completely that nothing could remain in me but Love alone.

5. The praises of men she heard with the highest indifference. Various people, who had neither seen nor known her, came to her and asked with folded hands that she might remember them before God and present certain matters of great importance to Him; and some time later they came back and reported to her that through the help of her prayer they had achieved a happy outcome in their affairs. These and many other such things she listened to as if nothing at all had been said to her.

She merely presented the persons or things for which she had been asked to the Lord in all simplicity, if she could remember them. And when I asked her once, from what spirit or impulse she did this, she answered:

> „I do it because I believe my Love wishes it to be so, and that the people have great need of it. When I further said that if people had said such things to her in the past, it would surely have been quite burdensome to her; she answered that if these things had been said to her then, she would rather have fled away into the wilderness and among the wild beasts than to have been able to suffer such a thing. But now, through the mercy of her only Love, it was all the same to her; because she now knew so well what she was, that she did not fear the praises at all. They were also not actually to be understood as being about her. For everything that was of her had long since been lost, consumed, and forgotten in such a way that she no longer existed; but God alone was the only goal toward which everything was directed and guided; and consequently the creature <note>A term used to describe any created being, emphasizing their dependence on the Creator</note> had no more place, but existed now solely and alone in her first origin; and thus she claimed nothing more for herself.„

This answer she has given several times since she was placed in this state by God.

## The Seventeenth Chapter.
### Of her daily walk with GOD.

->1.<-

One day I asked Armelle if she would please show me what had actually been the
primary focus <note>original: Vorwurf; in this 17th-century context, it refers to the "object" or "subject" of her meditation</note> with which her heart and thoughts remained occupied throughout the 
entire day; what the form and condition of her soul <note>original: Gemüth; refers to the inner disposition, mind, and emotional state</note> was while 
performing her chores; and how she otherwise carried out her remaining duties, from the time when GOD called her to His service until He took full 
possession of her—as we have seen in Chapter VIII. To this she gave me 
the very answer I had expected, namely: „If one desired to have the actual 
account of it, one would have to ask Love itself; for through the great 
mercy of God, she had never known any other art but <term>loving</term>: all 
her exercises, motivations, intentions, and advancements consisted 
merely in this: that she might love, and daily burn more and more in love; 
through this, she had learned all her duties and also performed them.“

2. „As soon as I awoke in the morning (she said), I threw myself into the 
arms of my Divine Love, like a child into the arms of its father. I stood 
up to serve Him and to do my work, solely that I might please Him. When I had time to pray, I lay on my knees in His Divine presence and spoke to Him as if I had 
seen Him before me with my physical eyes. There I surrendered myself to Him and 
asked Him that He would perfectly fulfill His holy will in me and by no means 
allow me to offend Him in the slightest matter throughout the day.“

3. „I dressed myself in His company; and He showed me that His 
love provided my clothing. When I thereafter went to my work, oh, 
He did not leave me because of it, and I did not leave Him either. He worked with me, 
and I with Him; indeed, I found myself just as united with Him in my labor as 
if I had been in prayer. Oh, how sweet and how easy it was for me to do all my

„...to endure toil and difficulties in such good company! Yes, this company gave me so much strength and such courage that nothing felt difficult to me, and I thought I could surely perform all the housework alone. I had nothing more than my body in and with the work; but my heart, and I myself entirely, burned with love in the sweet and intimate fellowship I had with Him.“

4. She also said further: "At that time I had two eyes and two ears, namely a left and a right. The left was for my housekeeping alone; for the right, and my whole heart, was always intent on looking at and loving Him who had deigned to visit me: and it seemed to me as if I heard these words in the depths of my heart: **Watch how I do it; and you do the same.**" <note>The "two eyes" is a classic mystical metaphor: the right eye gazes at eternity (God), while the left eye gazes at time (the world and daily tasks).</note>

5. "I had never (she said) asked for anything so urgently from my Divine Love, and never repeated any request daily with more fervor than this: that it might please His Divine Mercy to take me into the number of His female disciples and into His school, to make me a member of His household in His holy house, and just as formerly His apostles and disciples, to let me into His company. And oh! while I asked this with such great fervor that I was often quite outside of myself <note>original: ausser mir selbst; this refers to an ecstatic state where the soul is so focused on God that it loses awareness of the physical body</note>, behold, I did not know or understand in the slightest what I was saying. But, O my **GOD**, how well I understood my words afterward; and how well You granted me my request! For through Your great mercy You have taken me into Your school and company, where I, a poor ignorant woman, learned more in one day than all people together could have taught me in my whole life."

6. "I performed (she said further) each thing as if I had only this one thing left to do, without the slightest haste, because my Divine Love protected me from it. For otherwise, it would have been impossible for me to free myself from it, considering the manifold <term>hubbub</term> <note>original: Getümmel; refers to the chaotic noise and busy activity of a servant's life in a large household</note> under which I constantly was. Regardless of that, however, my Love stood by me in such a way that everything and each thing was performed without hindrance and at the right time."

7. Whenever there was anything in the house that everyone else pushed away and held in contempt, the good Armelle always chose such things for herself, both in her work as well as in her eating and in everything else she needed; and she rejoiced that she could keep the poorest and worst for herself and leave the better for others.

Then she later said herself: „When I was healthy, all my joy consisted in being able to perform everything that was the lowliest and most contemptible in the whole house. Every task that was perhaps tedious and slighted, or of which one might have been ashamed, I took up with great zeal; because Love, which led me, as it were, outside of myself, made me perform such things with delight and joy.“
