### Of Mary of the Incarnation. Chapter IV.

...found my relief, so that I could have gone to enjoy Him whom I could conceive of as nothing other than Love. Even outside of **prayer**, my heart was unceasingly turned toward Him, so that He, through His goodness, might grant me to possess His Spirit. For nothing seemed good to me, nothing beautiful, nothing desirable, except that I might possess the Spirit of **Jesus Christ**. All the powers of the soul wanted and wished for nothing else but to be in **Jesus**, through the Spirit of **Jesus**, and to follow Him in His life and in His mind. But although the soul had these burning desires, it was nevertheless in a very deep inward **humiliation** <note>In this context, "humiliation" refers to a state of profound spiritual lowliness or modesty before God.</note>, as it considered itself entirely unworthy of possessing the Good for which it longed.

8. The soul also sought all kinds of means to suppress the <term>lower part</term> <note>original: "unteren Theil". This refers to the "sensual" or "animal" soul—the part of human nature driven by physical desires and ego, as opposed to the higher "Spirit."</note>, to the extent that it would gladly have annihilated it entirely, if that had been possible. This <term>soulish part</term> <note>original: "Seelische Theil". In 17th-century mysticism, the "soul" was often seen as the seat of emotions and senses, which must be brought into harmony with the "Spirit."</note> allowed itself to be led here and there, wherever the Spirit wanted; which, however, also made it a partaker of its goods through a sweet anointing that eased its sufferings. Since the soulish part was thus in harmony with the Spirit, it ran into humiliations just as if they were precious things; and the soul held such things so dear that it feared people might notice it suffered too much, thereby robbing it of the happiness of its **humblings**.

Indeed, in the first three or four years that I was in my brother's house, the Spirit of Grace who led me caused me to try to hide all my natural skills, which God had given me for various business affairs, so that I might remain unknown, like a poor creature who knew nothing and was useful for nothing, except to be a servant to the manservants and maidservants in the house. And so I actually conducted myself in the most contemptible and most humbling things; and God's goodness permitted that I should be treated as such, and that I was dealt with quite strictly and masterfully in an astonishing way. But I so loved lowly and insignificant things and services that I once said to my <term>director</term> <note>original: "Führer". A priest or mentor who provided spiritual guidance.</note> that I feared I might cling to them too strongly; but he only smiled, for he knew well how far such things went; I only feared that he might help me out of this humbling state. I sometimes had to wait on and provide for five or six sick servants alone; I did the most contemptible tasks in the house in secret, so that when the maids came to perform them, they found everything already finished.

9. As soon as His Divine Majesty had communicated the gift of prayer to me, He also gave me the grace of His **holy presence**, which was my only support and placed me in constant conversation with the Savior. Though my mind at that time looked upon Him as the <term>God-man</term> <note>original: "Gottmensch". A theological term referring to Jesus Christ as being simultaneously fully God and fully human.</note>, my imagination had no part in it; instead, everything took place in the understanding and the will, in a very spiritual manner and with great purity. Sometimes I had an internal feeling that our Savior **Jesus Christ** was near me and by my side to keep me company: and this presence and company **was**

### Fifth Part. The Life

...was so sweet and so Divine to me that I could not express how it happened.

10. In this state, everything that occurred in the soul was more spiritual and detached <note>original: "abgeschieden." A key term in German mysticism meaning "set apart" or "secluded" from worldly or sensory distractions.</note> than coarse and sensory; nevertheless, God gave the soul to understand that He wanted to withdraw her from the support of the physical to place her in a more detached state, and into a purity that was until then unknown to her, and through which she had not yet been led; namely, He wanted to withdraw her from the support and help she received to some extent through the senses, which were filled with the fullness that came forth from the **Holy Humanity of our Savior** <note>The "Holy Humanity" refers to the physical life and human nature of Jesus, which mystics often used as a starting point for meditation before progressing to his purely divine nature.</note>. For the enjoyment of His company gave her a real experience of His sweetness, so that she said (a): "Your name is like an ointment poured forth."

<margin>(a) Song of Solomon 1:3 <note>original: "Hohel. 1, 2." The German text cites the Song of Solomon (Hohelied), where this imagery of "poured out ointment" represents the irresistible nature of divine grace.</note></margin>

11. Accordingly, the soul felt that her spirit was opened so that she might enter into a state of light, wherein God let her see that He was like a great and wide sea. For just as the visible sea can tolerate nothing impure, so too this God of infinite purity neither will nor can suffer anything impure, but He rejects all dead, sluggish, and impure souls. This new light worked great things in the soul.

12. O my God, what impurities must be cleared away to reach the goal of Your union and fellowship, toward which the soul—touched by the love of her highest and only Good—stretches forth so fervently and constantly! Such is incomprehensible; as is the importance of the purity of the heart, which is absolutely necessary in all internal and external workings: for the Spirit of God is like an inexorable **judge** <note>original: "Censeur." Like a moral censor or critic who scrutinizes every thought.</note>. Nevertheless, the state of which I speak here is only the first step; and a soul that has arrived there can fall from it in a moment. I tremble when I think of it, and how much depends on being faithful.

13. It is indeed the truth that a creature can do nothing of itself: however, when God calls her to this way of life, faithfulness and responsiveness are highly necessary, alongside a total surrender of oneself to Divine Providence.

14. The withdrawal of the aforementioned supports had occurred only so that the soul might advance much more in grace through the thorough practice of the virtues that come forth from the Spirit of **Jesus Christ**, which were then given to her—especially humility, patience, and the love of neighbor, in which virtues she greatly increased. I was then about twenty-three years old. I counted myself happy and felt that a great favor was shown to me whenever someone gave me the opportunity to suffer some humiliations; and I felt in my heart a very special love for such persons. I humbled myself under them with a completely sincere inclination; and as soon as I committed some imperfection in this, I was inwardly punished for it; as such...

### of Mary of the Incarnation. Chapter IV.

...which then especially happened to me at a certain time, when I was rebuked, though with love, through these internal but very clear words: **"If you had a beautiful pearl or a precious stone, and someone came and defiled it in a dung pit, would you be satisfied with that?"** These words plunged me into a state of shame before GOD, of whom my soul had no other concept than that He is Purity itself.

Nevertheless, my soul did not cease to turn incessantly toward GOD, through a perpetual and purely spiritual inclination. I wanted to possess Him in a way that was unknown to me, and for which He Himself was preparing me.

<margin>(a) Revelation 4:11. <note>original: "Offenb. 4, 11."</note></margin>
15. I found Him in all creatures, and in the purpose and end for which they were created. But this happened in such a spiritual manner, and through a ray of contemplation <term>Beschauung: a form of wordless, meditative prayer where the soul "sees" divine truths</term> which was so purified of all coarseness that creatures caused me no distraction. I had an infused knowledge (bestowed upon me from above without any effort) of the nature of every thing; and without thinking that this was anything extraordinary, I sometimes spoke of it with great simplicity. At other times, when I turned toward the Divine Majesty and had this saying in my mind (a): **"O GOD, you have made all things, and by your will they are created;"** my soul grasped a thousand times more than all these words expressed through their outward sound, and in this understanding, she poured herself out in praise and thanksgiving.

<margin>(b) This state and title was the state of spiritual marriage <note>original: "geistliche Vermählung." In mystical tradition, this is the highest stage of union between the soul and God.</note>, as was made known to her not long after through the explicit inspiration of the words of the prophet: **"I will betroth you to me in faithfulness; I will betroth you to me forever."** Hosea 2:19-20. <note>original: "Hos. 2, 19. 20."</note></margin>
16. It was revealed to her, however, that for this, abilities were required which she still lacked, and that she did not yet possess the ornaments corresponding to such a sublime possession.

17. Fifth Part. The Life

The inner Spirit <note>The "inner Spirit" refers to the internal voice of God or the Holy Spirit guiding her conscience.</note>, who had made himself the lord and leader of her soul, gave her to understand that inner purity required her to go once more and reveal all the sins and imperfections of her life to her spiritual director. She was to give them to him in writing, with the request to post them on the church door, along with the name of the person who had committed them, so that the whole world might know that she had been so unfaithful to her God. He had shown her a ray of His great purity, such that the smallest speck of dust of imperfection seemed like a mountain to her. My director, however, took the paper without saying a word. I begged him very earnestly to post it on the church door; but I believe that he burned it—at least, I did not see it posted, even though I had asked him to do so.

# Chapter Five.

-> **The multiplicity of her business affairs does not hinder her communion with God. Her humble and inward longing for spiritual marriage. Her temptations. Her intimacy with the Savior, who unites her heart with His own. Unwavering communion with Him.** <-

Around this time, I became entangled in all the business affairs of my (a) brother and was forced to deal with many people outside the house. All of this did not deprive me of the opportunity to perform works of charity; our Lord also gave me an increase of His grace and the strength for everything He wanted from me. I had unique opportunities to practice patience; but everything was pleasant to me, as I looked upon Him who brought me such close access to His Divine Majesty.

2. I sometimes found myself in the middle of the bustle of merchants, while meanwhile my spirit was submerged in this Divine Majesty. Whoever had seen me would have judged that I was listening with devotion to everything being said; but if I had been asked about it afterward, I would likely have known very little of it. Nevertheless, God gave me the grace to properly carry out those business matters that were entrusted to me. I spent almost entire days in a certain stable, which served as an armory; and sometimes it was even at midnight, when—

...since I was still at the harbor, seeing to the loading or unloading of merchant goods. My usual company consisted of porters, carters, and some fifty or sixty horses for which I had to provide. Whenever my brother and sister were in the country, as often happened, I had all their business on my shoulders; but when they returned home, they took over the care themselves, and I served them, immediately forgetting all the worries I had during their absence upon their arrival, just as if I had never thought of them before.

3. Yet all this unrest did not draw me away from God; rather, I found myself strengthened in Him, because everything was done out of love and not for my own benefit. At times I found myself so overloaded with business that I did not know what to take hold of first. At such times I turned to my usual refuge and said:

> My Love <note>original: "Meine Liebe"; Marie frequently addresses God or Christ with this intimate title.</note>, it is not possible for me to do all these things; You must do them for me, otherwise everything will remain undone.

And when I trusted in His goodness in this way, everything became easy for me. I spoke tenderly to Him during the time I did all this, and I was as calm and still as if I had been in the most remote solitude in the world.

This powerful support meant that I confidently and willingly took upon myself all the works that I recognized to be pleasing to Him. Sometimes I withdrew to show Him my affection away from the commotion; but I was immediately called, and then I went down joyfully and said to Him:

> Let us go, my sweet Love, You will it so; it is enough if I only keep You; this work shall be for You.

And I felt an incomparable ease in doing everything in this way for my Beloved.

4. All my strictness <note>This refers to her private ascetic practices or penances.</note> did not burden my body either. I was very joyful among the people I had to be with; and they believed that I took a special pleasure in being with them. However, it was the union I had with God that made me so joyful and cheerful; for in the world I found nothing in which I should have taken pleasure.

5. I felt a great love for those who gave me opportunities for suffering. I looked upon them as people chosen by God to bring me such a great good, which I also feared losing because of my sins.

6. For the rest, I recognized that I was nothingness itself, worthy of all contempt; and whenever another thought occurred to me, I was quite ashamed within myself and disciplined myself for it. I was dismayed that the Lord showed me so many graces and met me so lovingly, making me so bold that I dared to strive for the honorable state of the Bride <note>A reference to "Spiritual Marriage," the highest state of mystical union in Catholic tradition.</note> and wished to consume myself in these Divine embraces. I spoke to Him with great intimacy and said:

> Oh, my Love, when will this marriage finally be consummated?

He enraptured my spirit and inflamed my heart, which He wished to grant its request; but some further adornment had to be prepared for it first, and for this my soul sighed.

# Fifth Part. The Life

7. While I was experiencing these feelings, the first verse of the 127th Psalm was suddenly brought to my mind: *Unless the Lord builds the house, etc.* <note>Psalm 127:1 reads: "Unless the Lord builds the house, those who build it labor in vain."</note>, along with a great light that gave me the understanding of these words. It allowed me to see the nothingness <note>In mystical theology, "nothingness" refers to the "annihilation" of the ego or self-will to make room for God’s action.</note> and the inability of the creature to raise itself to God by its own strength, or to be advanced in His special graces; in a word, the inability to progress in all the requirements and efforts to possess Him, if He Himself does not build the house and bestow upon it the ornaments befitting such a high undertaking. I saw this nothingness of the creature so terrifyingly and with such certainty that I could not even grasp the depth of it; this then placed me in a state of great self-denial and granted me a noble humility which, because it expects nothing from itself, hopes for everything from God. My soul was as if assured that it would one day possess Him in that intimate union toward which He gave it such a great attraction. It was subject to all the commands of His Divine Majesty; but all its desires longed, like the yearning of the Bride, for the kiss of His mouth. <note>This is a reference to the Song of Solomon 1:2, a central text for Christian mystics describing the soul's marriage to God.</note>

8. It is unutterable how much pain and suffering this love causes: yet the soul would not wish to escape them, unless it desired to do so only so that it might possess the One whom it loves (a). It seems to the soul that it has internal arms which are constantly stretched out to embrace Him.

The soul accounts its life as nothing compared to the possession of its Beloved, where it may possess Him in the manner toward which He draws it; for it can be satisfied with nothing less.

> "No," she says, "my chaste Love, I do not want You in part, but entirely. If my life prevents You from coming, then take it away, for it is harmful to me. You are so good and so powerful in love, and yet You take pleasure in my torment. You can release me from it through death; ah! why then do You not let me die? Yes, You can make me give up my spirit with a single sigh, and can thereby draw my spirit into Yours; ah! why then do You delay so long, either to come to me or to draw me to Yourself? But You are everywhere, and I know that You are in me; why then do You take pleasure in my pain? What is Your pleasure that I should do? Command me, and Your words will produce in me the works that are pleasing to You, and will even capture Your heart."

9. All this took place on the way to where my business led me, amidst the bustle of domestic cares and in the company of many people, with as much devotion of mind as if I had been in a small prayer closet: for the soul was taken up passively <note>The term "passively" (German: *leidentlicher Weise*) refers to "passive or infused contemplation," where the person feels they are not "doing" the prayer, but God is acting upon them.</note> by a pull that gave it a great peace at its core; otherwise, however, Divine Love held the soul in an anguish that can well be felt, but cannot be expressed.

# Of Marie of the Incarnation. Chapter V.

10. I have not previously mentioned that from the time my bonds (of the state of marriage) were broken <note>Marie’s husband died in 1619, leaving her a widow at age 19 with a six-month-old son.</note>, and I had begun to find a taste for spiritual goods and recognized the vanities of the things of this world, I felt myself called to the monastic state. However, I still had another bond which did not yet allow me to carry out my intention at that time, according to the judgment of my guide <note>Referring to her spiritual director or confessor.</note>, who nevertheless said to me for my comfort that he believed Divine Goodness would grant me this grace in His own time. And so I bore this necessary yoke <note>This "yoke" refers to the responsibility of raising her young son, Claude, which delayed her entry into the convent.</note> out of contentment with the decrees of God, who meanwhile held my heart in a monastery and my body in the world.

11. However, just as His overwhelming love for my insignificance seemed to take pleasure in incessantly showing me new mercies, He allowed me to see and experience the great, infinite treasures hidden in the counsels <note>original: "conseils"</note> of the Holy Gospels, to the observation of which He calls chosen souls. In particular, He let me see those treasures hidden in poverty, in chastity, and in obedience <note>These are the "Evangelical Counsels," the three traditional vows taken by members of religious orders.</note>, which I recognized as excellent virtues that our Savior Jesus Christ chose and practiced in this mortal life to give us a model, so that He might work and cause our salvation through His example just as much as He earned and brought it about for us through His merit.

12. [Our dear Marie further expresses here the excellence of these Evangelical virtues, and says that they are worked in us not through our own effort, but solely through the gracious communication of the Spirit of Jesus; she then recounts various other extraordinary graces shown to her by God, along with her extraordinary austerity, in which she practiced out of an inner impulse at that time: but since space must be saved for the necessary matters that follow, we have only wished to suggest this here, and thus proceed with the account of some alternating trials that she encountered afterward.] <note>This bracketed section is an editorial summary by the original German publisher, who condensed Marie's lengthy descriptions to save space.</note>

13. Our Lord allowed (these are again Marie's own words) my soul to be tested by various temptations, from Satan and the world, as well as from my own self-love. My God! How I was tossed to and fro! I cannot express the various thoughts that tormented my mind, which found itself all the more burdened because it was also in a state of great inner darkness regarding God and the perfection toward which I strove. In short, everything caused me difficulty, and wherever I turned, my mind found nothing but plague everywhere. I did not, it is true, neglect my exercises; yet I found no inner support in them at all and had to use great force upon myself to perform them.

# The Sixth Chapter.

## God communicates to her in an ecstasy a high knowledge of the Holy Trinity. Effects of this grace. The difference between the lights that come from God. Continuation of her desire for the spiritual marriage.

->I.<-

Just as the Divine Majesty continued unceasingly to communicate His graces and lights to me, and as He intended to bestow an extraordinary grace upon me at this time, He gave me for that purpose a singular kind of disposition <note>original: "disposition"</note> of purity, which brought me to the humiliation and annihilation of myself. Thereupon it happened that one morning, on the second day of Pentecost <note>Whit Monday</note>, while I was in the church, my eyes were closed in an instant, and my spirit was lifted up and swallowed up in a vision of the most holy and most Majestic Trinity, in a way and manner that I cannot express. In that same moment, all the powers of my soul were held still, and received passively <note>original: "patissantes," from the Latin word for undergoing or receiving an impression without active resistance</note> the impression that was given to them by this holy mystery—an impression which was without form or figure, but was nonetheless far clearer and more intelligible than any light; and this immediately gave me to understand that my soul was in the truth.

Afterwards, I saw in this impression, in a single moment, the Divine fellowship <note>original: "commerce," referring here to the internal relations or communication within the Godhead</note> which the three Divine Persons have among one another: namely, the Understanding of the Father, who, contemplating Himself, begets His Son, which has been from all eternity and will be into eternity. My soul was instructed in this truth in an inexpressible way, which caused me to lose all power of expression, because the soul was sunk in this light. After this, she <note>The soul is traditionally referred to as "she" in German and French spiritual writing.</note> saw the mutual love of the Father and the Son bring forth the Holy Spirit, which occurred through a reciprocal immersion of love <note>original: "reciproque plongement d'amour"</note>, but without mixing or confusion. I received the impression of this production, and I understood what the breathing <note>original: "spiration," a technical theological term for the way the Holy Spirit "proceeds" or is "breathed" from the Father and the Son</note> and the...

...bringing forth, the active and passive breathing <note>original: "Athemen," referring to the theological concept of "spiration," the process by which the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son</note> (or spiriting). But the purity of this breathing and bringing forth is so high and so exalted that I have no words to say or express it. As I then saw the distinction, I also recognized the unity of the essence in the Divine Persons. And although I would need many words to speak of this most holy Trinity, I nevertheless recognized, in a single moment and without any interval of time, the unity, the distinctions, and the workings, both within itself and outside of itself. Yet I was enlightened in a certain spiritual way, step by step, according to the workings of the three Divine Persons outside of themselves, without any confusion being found in any instruction of the things that were revealed to me; rather, everything happened in an unspeakable purity and clarity.

2. In that very same impulse, and in the same impression, this most holy Trinity instructed my soul in that which it worked through communication in the highest hierarchy of the angels, making known to them His holy will without the mediation of any created spirit. And I saw with distinction the effects and the relationships <note>original: "rapports"</note> of each of the Divine Persons of the most holy Trinity in each choir of this highest hierarchy. I saw that the eternal Father dwelt in the **Thrones**; which gave me to recognize the purity and the unshakable firmness <note>original: "solidité"</note> of His eternal thoughts. I saw that the **Word** <note>The second person of the Trinity, Jesus Christ</note> communicated Himself to the **Cherubim** through the brilliance of His light; which gave me to understand that He is, from within Himself, entirely light and entirely truth through His eternal birth, and also from without, when He communicates Himself. I saw that the **Holy Spirit** poured Himself into the **Seraphim** and filled them with His fervors; which gave me to recognize that this adorable Person is entirely fire and entirely love, because He thus ignites an entire angelic choir. Finally, I saw that the entire Most Holy Trinity communicated itself to the unity of the Divine Essence of this highest hierarchy, which then revealed the Divine Will to the remaining heavenly spirits, according to the commands it had for that purpose.

3. My soul was entirely lost in these great glories, and it seemed that it pleased the Divine Majesty to enlighten it more and more in such things, which infinitely exceed the weakness of the creature. It was also shown to me that, although the Divinity has created subordinations among the angels so that some might be enlightened by others in stages, He nevertheless, when it pleases Him, enlightens them through Himself, according to what the Divinity’s purpose for them may be; which He also does for some chosen souls in this world. And although I am nothing but mud and filth, my soul nevertheless had the vision and, as it were, the certainty that it was one of these souls. As it received this light, it also perfectly understood how it was created in the **image of God**; and that, just as the most holy Trinity was threefold in Persons and (yet only) a single Divine Essence, so too the soul is threefold in its powers <note>The "three powers of the soul" typically refer to Memory, Understanding, and Will, a concept popularized by St. Augustine</note> and unified in its essence.

Afterward, I saw in this impression, in a moment, the Divine <term>Communion<note>original: "commerce," referring to the internal relationship and exchange between the Persons of the Trinity</note></term> which the three Divine Persons have among one another; namely, the understanding of the Father, who, beholding Himself, begets His Son, which has been from all eternity and will be into eternity. My soul was instructed in an unspeakable way in this truth, which caused me to lose all expression, because the soul was submerged in this light. bringing forth, the active and the passive **spiration** <term>spiration<note>original: "Athemen (oder Geiſten)." But the purity of this breathing and bringing forth is so high and so sublime that I have no words to say and express it. As I then saw the distinction, I also recognized the unity of the essence in the Divine Persons. And although I need many words to speak of this most holy Trinity, I nevertheless recognized in a moment and without interval of time, the unity, the distinctions, and the effects, both within itself and outside of itself. Nevertheless, I was enlightened in a certain spiritual way step by step, according to the effects of the three Divine Persons outside themselves, without any confusion being found in any instruction of the things revealed to me, but everything happened in an unspeakable purity and clarity.

2. In that same movement, and in the same impression, this most holy Trinity instructed my soul in what it itself worked through communication in the **highest hierarchy of the angels** <note>In traditional Christian theology (following Pseudo-Dionysius), the angels are organized into nine choirs; the highest hierarchy consists of the Seraphim, Cherubim, and Thrones.</note>, giving them to know His holy will, without the mediation of any created spirit. And I saw with distinction the effects and the **relationships** <note>original: "rapports" (French)</note> of each of the Divine Persons of the most holy Trinity, in each choir of this supreme hierarchy. I saw that the eternal Father dwelt in the **Thrones**; which gave me to recognize the purity and the unshakable **steadfastness** <note>original: "ſolidité" (French)</note> of His eternal thoughts. I saw that the **Word** <note>The "Word" (Logos) refers to the Second Person of the Trinity, Jesus Christ.</note> through the radiance of His light communicated Himself to the **Cherubim**; which gave me to understand that He from within in Himself is all Light and all Truth through His eternal birth, and from without, when He communicates Himself. I saw that the **Holy Spirit** poured Himself into the **Seraphim**, and filled them with His fervors; which gave me to recognize that this adorable Person is all fire and all love, because He ignited an entire angelic choir in such a way. Finally I saw that the whole Most Holy Trinity communicated itself to the unity of the Divine Essence of this supreme hierarchy, which accordingly revealed the Divine Will to the remaining heavenly spirits, according to the commands it had for it.

3. My soul was quite lost in these great glories, and it seemed that it pleased the Divine Majesty to enlighten her more and more in such things, which infinitely exceed the weakness of the creature. It was also shown to me that, although the Godhead had made subordinations among the angels, so that some would be enlightened step-by-step through others, it nevertheless, when it pleased it, enlightens them through itself, according to whatever the Godhead's purpose for them is; which it also does to some elect souls in this world: and although I am nothing but mud and filth, yet my soul had the vision, and as it were the certainty, that she was one of these souls. As she received this light, she also fully grasped how she was created in the **image of God**; and that, just as the most holy Trinity was threefold in Persons, and (yet only) a single Divine Essence, so also the soul is threefold in her powers, and one in her essence. <note>This refers to the classic Augustinian teaching that the human soul mirrors the Trinity through its three faculties: Memory, Understanding, and Will.</note>

### Fifth Part: The Life

4. [Our exalted Mary of the Incarnation <note>Marie de l’Incarnation (1599–1672) was a French Ursuline nun and mystic who later became a prominent figure in the early history of New France (Canada).</note> wrote a letter to her son shortly before her death regarding this vision, in which she explains various details to him at his request. See here an excerpt of the same:]

As this happened to me (she writes), I was still being instructed in the most adorable mystery of the Holy Trinity; and even if I had read and re-read much about it, such reading or instruction from men could not have given me that impression which I had then, and which has remained with me since that time. This occurred through a sudden impression, which caused me to remain as if immovable upon my knees, for in a single moment I saw what cannot be said or written.

I do not say that it was a light, because such a thing still falls under the senses; rather, I say that it was an impression, although even that seems to me to be something too coarse; I cannot, however, express myself otherwise, for the matter is so spiritual that no manner of speaking can reach it. And when I say that GOD let me see it, I do not mean to say that it was an act of personal reflection <note>original: *acte réfléchi* (French)</note>, for an "act" can still be described and seems coarse; this, however, is a Divine thing, and from GOD Himself. Everything was contemplated there, and presented itself to the soul to be seen with a steady and purified gaze, which was free from all ignorance and was unspeakable.

<margin>(a) This she wrote about half a year before her death, 45 or 46 years after the time this grace occurred.</margin>
But note that these great things are never forgotten, and they are as new to me now as when they happened (a). Regarding the manners of speaking, they are unstudied, and I have only intended to indicate what my mind <note>original: *Gemüth*—referring here to the internal disposition or soul.</note> suggested to me; but they are always lesser than the things themselves, because one can find no words to express them better.

5. This great light of which I have spoken caused me to enter into a new inward state. For a long time, I could not remove the memory of the three Divine Persons from my mind; which then brought me into a fear that I might perhaps be deceived, and that it might perhaps be a snare of the evil enemy <note>The "evil enemy" is a common historical term for the Devil.</note> or of the imagination, to hinder me in the spiritual life—even though I imagined nothing to myself, and my guide also gave me assurance on this point.

6. I remained thus always in this fear until once, while I was in prayer and stood in actual doubt and fear (over this matter), an inward voice said to me: **"Stay there; this is your nest."** In that moment I was placed in safety, and this word, through its power, brought peace and serenity into my heart to such an extent that I remained in this holy mystery as if in a Divine bed, wherein I took my rest and my nourishment. 7. It is also true that these lights, which come from God (for I make a distinction between that which is mere light, or light and love together, and that which is mere love—namely, such a love which suddenly ravishes the soul through a pull from God), it is, I say, true that these lights, which are intended to instruct and strengthen the soul in Divine Truths, are so perfect in the soul that receives them, and in the matter presented to it, that no doubt remains, nor any curiosity <note>The original German "Fürwiß" refers to a restless or intrusive desire to know things that are beyond human understanding.</note> to know more of it. This is because the soul has a certain reverence in its spirit which causes it to stand gently still, or, better said, which perfectly satisfies it. For although the soul understands this truth of the Scripture, that (a) the one who is a searcher of the majesty of God shall be overwhelmed by the weight of His glory <note>original: *Scrutator est maiestatis opprimetur a gloria* (Latin). This was a common warning in mystical theology against over-intellectualizing the divine nature.</note>; yet it is not this which makes her stand still, but rather because she is satisfied and can desire nothing more.

8. Regarding those impressions which are light and love together, love always retains the precedence: for the soul has no desire to recognize more, but always to love more, and to be united in the one whom she loves.

Finally, that which I call mere love is when God suddenly gives Himself to the soul to possess, and grants her a very intimate communion through His pull. In this state, she desires nothing else but only to enjoy; and it is enough for her that she knows, through an experiential knowledge <term>Erfahrungserkäntniß: knowledge gained through direct spiritual experience rather than through the senses or intellect</term> of love, that God is in her and with her, and that He is God. She is then satisfied; yet she is not <gloss>fully</gloss> contented. For, just as there are infinite delights in this lovely Object, and He is an abyss of love whose depth she cannot fathom, so she longs to be swallowed up in it, and to be so completely lost that nothing more is seen but her Beloved, who will then have entirely transformed her into Himself through the power of His love.

The soul then has no curiosity to see <gloss>and to know;</gloss> but rather an insatiable desire to love: and this very thing is an effect of those lights which God communicates in a supernatural way. Nevertheless, in the degree of mere light, and in the degree of light and love, light gives birth to love; but in the degree of mere love, love gives birth to light. The soul loves in a passive way; and she sees that it is a God who causes her to undergo this love: not as if the one state were not just as passive <gloss>passive</gloss> as the other, but this latter one is the Good of all goods.

Even though the soul’s enjoyment in the (a) wine cellar <note>original: "Weinkeller." A traditional mystical reference to the Song of Solomon, representing a place of intimate, intoxicating divine love.</note> is great, because she is filled with the wine of His love, there are still further preparations through which she must be made capable of the spiritual marriage. To be sure, the soul does everything she can on her part, as far as her lowliness <note>original: "Geringheit," referring to the mystic's sense of their own smallness or unworthiness before God.</note> allows; but such a sublime work must be carried out here that the Beloved must necessarily set His own hand to it. He does this through His secret workings and through paths that are hidden from the soul herself, so that when she one day attains the possession of this happiness, she may confess that it was entirely the work of her Beloved. It was not my intention to write all of this, but the inner Spirit has carried me away. May He be praised eternally!

My guide <note>Referring to her spiritual director or confessor.</note> regulated my external exercises at that time; but regarding my inward life, he prescribed nothing to me, because I was engaged in prayer in all places and experienced what the Bride says in the Song of Solomon: (b) My Beloved is an ointment poured forth. It was languishing with desire and sighed without ceasing with these words: "Ah, my Beloved, when will this union finally happen?" I felt an Agent <note>original: "Wirker [Agent]." In mystical theology, an 'agent' is a divine force or power that acts upon the soul, often without the soul's conscious control.</note> within me who was much stronger than I, who urged me to voice all these lovelorn complaints.

It seems that You distance Yourself from me: I run, I fly, I seek You, even though I already know that You are within me. But You have a dwelling place there which is unknown to me. When I spread out my arms to embrace You, my impurities create a hindrance and set—I know not what—boundaries between You and me.

4. These hidden paths were (in part) internal touches and Divine emanations, which were so subtle, so intimate, and so imperceptible, that it seemed to the soul as if she were absent from her Beloved; or when He was near, she felt the same longing as the bride in the Song of Solomon, and invited Him, saying to Him just as she did (a): *Come, my Beloved, come into my garden.* <note>original: "Hohel. 5, 1." - Song of Solomon 5:1. This biblical book was a primary source of imagery for Christian mystics to describe the relationship between the soul and God.</note> Then she recognized that He was near her; and she heard His voice, which was nothing other than a revelation of Himself, occurring as if in a secret manner, which made her leap for joy, and through loving sighs of the heart say to Him (b): *I hear the voice of my Beloved; behold, He looks out, He stands behind the wall, and looks at me through the lattice.* <note>original: "Hohel. 2, 9." - Song of Solomon 2:9.</note> In this revelation, the matter stood thus: This wall, and this lattice, was the great space that existed between God and His heights, and between the soul and her lowliness <note>original: "Geringheit." This refers to the "littleness" or insignificance of the human creature compared to the Creator.</note>; nevertheless, He was, so it seemed to me, so in love with her that He wished to draw near to her. Now, as the soul felt herself drawn in a passive manner <term>passive: "leidentlicher Weise" - a state where the soul does not act of its own will but receives the action of God.</term> through the excess of love, she was compelled (though she had a vision of her lowliness and her nothingness) to pour out her intimate sighs, which corresponded with this drawing, without her being able to resist in any way. I confess that I speak here only in a stammering way of what passed between God and the soul in this communication, of which He deemed her worthy by uniting her lowliness with His infinite Majesty.

5. These Divine and very delicate, but very painful touches, are a purification of the innermost part of the soul, so that the same may be made worthy to be a Royal bed for the Bridegroom. I saw myself almost sinking into a swoon at the sight of the height of His Majesty, which is so unlike the soul, because of her lowliness, that she therefore falls into a faint and finds herself lost in this ocean. Then she comes to herself again; but soon she falls into a swoon once more: and so it lasts for a considerable time, with various such alternations. One must not think, however, that there is anything imaginary <note>original: "bildliches." She means these are not literal mental images or hallucinations, but direct spiritual experiences.</note> here; the imagination has no part in it; indeed, the powers of the soul draw together into unity and remain suspended and in silence: everything happens in a passive state, where the soul suffers the impressions of the Divine Majesty, who wishes to make this inner part the object of His delights as well as His mercies. According to the measure of this purification, the soul becomes ever more capable; and her confidence <note>original: "Freymüthigkeit." Literally "free-spiritedness" or holy boldness in the presence of God.</note> increases according to the measure of her light (or knowledge), which produces just as much love within her.

Just as I (she says) was expecting the highest grace (namely, the **Spiritual Marriage** <note>original: "Vermählung." In mystical theology, this refers to the highest state of union between the soul and God, often described using the metaphor of a wedding.</note>), I saw myself descending into an abyss. It seemed as if all things had conspired together to cause me suffering. All comfort was taken from me, and I remained in a total abandonment of all the graces I had received. Even the memory I had of them doubled my pains, because I was tempted, and almost convinced, that they were not true graces, but rather a waste of time and a delay. I found no comfort, no matter what was said to me; and when my confessor spoke with me, it tormented me even more. I carried my suffering everywhere, and the most common subject of my meditation was my cross, which was always present to me. That which increased my pains the most was the memory of God, whom I did not lose from my sight; for then my greatest sorrow was that I did not love Him, or so it seemed to me. I saw myself falling into imperfections; I no longer had the heart to endure myself; everything said to me, if it had even a hint of offense, caused my soul to suffer: I had unheard-of anxieties of the heart, so that I saw myself fallen from a paradise into a **purgatory**.

7. My guide <note>A "guide" or "director" was a priest responsible for overseeing a mystic's spiritual health and ensuring their visions aligned with church teaching.</note>, who feared I might become ill, for a time cut back some of my **penances** <term>penances: "Bußübungen" - voluntary acts of self-discipline or physical hardship intended to show repentance.</term>. He took the trouble to translate various passages for me which he believed might relieve me; but nothing diminished my suffering. My body was such a burden to me that I had to bear it with resentment. Yet I was like a small child, wrapped up from all sides, who is peaceful and says not a word. I saw, but only from afar, this peace that was hidden in the **ground of the soul** <term>ground of the soul: "Grund der Seelen" - a mystical term for the deepest, innermost part of a person where they can meet God directly.</term>. This ground of the soul consented to everything God did with me; but I could hardly perceive this consent.

<margin>(a) Hosea 2, 20.</margin>

A translation of the Latin Vulgate's Hosea 2:20, "et desponsabo te mihi in fide."</note> Through this, my whole spirit woke up, as I was inwardly instructed that, in order to reach the goal for which I strove, the Savior wanted faith alone to be my support from now on, and that I should seek no other life than the purity of this faith. Then I no longer had any trouble carrying my cross and suffering; rather, I loved them, and was willing to carry them until the Last Judgment, if His goodness had willed it; I was also well satisfied and rejoiced that He kept His graces for Himself; and I thanked Him with all my heart for preserving them in their purity, since I, on the contrary, defiled them all through my wickedness as soon as they were within me: and so I felt once more my peace, which had moved so far away.

### Fifth Part. The Life

4. These hidden ways were (on one hand) internal touches <note>In mystical theology, "touches" (Berührungen) refer to subtle, direct spiritual sensations of God's presence that do not involve the physical senses.</note> and Divine outflows, which were so subtle, so intimate, and so imperceptible that it seemed to the soul that she was absent from her Beloved; or when He was near, she had the very same longing that the Bride had in the **Song of Solomon**, and invited Him, saying to Him just as she did (a): *Come, my beloved, come into my garden.* Then she recognized that He was near her; and she heard His voice, which was nothing other than a revelation of Himself, which happened as if by stealth, and caused her to leap for joy, and through sighs of a heart in love to say to Him (b): *I hear the voice of my beloved; behold, He looks, He stands behind the wall, and sees me through the lattice.* In this revelation, the matter stood thus: This wall and this lattice were the great chasm that existed between God and His heights, and between the soul and her lowliness; regardless of this, He was, so it seemed to me, so in love with her that He wished to draw near to her. Now, as the soul felt herself drawn passively through the excess of love, she was compelled (though she had a vision of her lowliness and of her nothingness) to breathe out her inward sighs, which corresponded with this pull, without her being able to resist in any way. I confess that here I speak only with a stammer <note>Mystics often use the term "stammering" to describe the impossibility of putting transcendent spiritual experiences into human words.</note> of what passed between God and the soul in this communication, of which He deemed her worthy by uniting her lowliness with His infinite Majesty.

5. These Divine and very tender, yet very painful touches, are a purification of the innermost part of the soul, so that it may be made worthy to be a Royal Bed for the Bridegroom. I saw myself almost sinking into a swoon at the sight of the height of His Majesty, which is so unlike the soul, because of her lowliness, that she therefore falls into a faint and finds herself lost in this ocean. Then she comes to herself again; but soon she falls anew into a swoon: and so it lasts for a considerable time, with various such alternations. One must not think, however, that there is anything figurative here: the imagination <note>German: "Einbildungskraft." The author is emphasizing that this is an intellectual or "infused" spiritual experience, not a mental hallucination or "imagined" picture.</note> has no part in it; indeed, the powers of the soul draw together into unity and remain inhibited and in silence: everything happens in a passive (<term>passive</term> <note>original: "leidentlich." In this context, it refers to "Passivity," a state where the soul does not act by its own effort but allows God to act upon it.</note>) state, as the soul suffers the impressions of the Divine Majesty, who wishes to make this inner part the object of His delights as well as His mercies. According to the measure of this purification, the soul becomes ever more capable; and her boldness increases according to the measure of her light (or knowledge), which produces just as great a love within her.

6. [In yet another, no less painful way, this soul beloved by God was purified and prepared for the impending intimate marriage, namely through the way of internal sufferings and temptations, as her son relates in the following manner using her own words, which I cannot omit to quote here in full:]

### of Mary of the Incarnation. Chapter VII.

6. Just as I (she says) was expecting the highest grace (namely the spiritual marriage), I saw myself descending into an abyss. It seemed as if all things had conspired together to cause me suffering. All comfort was taken from me, and I remained in a state of total abandonment of all the graces I had received. Even the memory I had of them doubled my pains, because I was tempted, and was as if convinced that they were not true graces, but a waste of time and a delay. I found no comfort, no matter what was said to me; and when my confessor <note>A priest who hears confessions and offers spiritual guidance.</note> spoke with me, it tormented me even more. I carried my suffering everywhere, and the most common subject of my meditation was my cross, which was always present to me. That which increased my pains the most was the memory of God, which I did not lose from sight; and then my greatest sorrow was that I did not love Him, as it seemed to me. I saw myself falling into imperfections; I no longer had the heart to bear myself; everything that was said to me, if it had even a hint of offense, caused suffering to my soul: I had unheard-of anxieties of the heart, such that I saw myself fallen from a paradise into a purgatory <note>Here used metaphorically to describe a state of intense spiritual cleansing through suffering.</note>.

7. My guide <note>Her spiritual director.</note>, who feared I might become ill, for a time cut back some of my penitential exercises <note>Physical or spiritual acts of self-discipline, such as fasting or extra prayers.</note>. He took the trouble to translate various pieces for me which he believed might relieve me; but nothing diminished my sufferings. My body was such a burden to me that I had to carry it with resentment. Yet I was like a little child that, wrapped up from all sides, is peaceful and says not a word. I saw, but from very far away, this peace that was hidden in the depth of the soul. This depth of the soul consented to everything God did with me; but I could hardly perceive this consent.

<margin>(a) Hosea 2, 20.</margin>
8. I was in this state for several months: but at the end of them it happened one day, as I wanted to perform my prayer exercise, that these words were spoken in my interior (a): *In faith will I betroth myself to you.* <note>Original: "Im Glauben will ich mich mit Dir vermählen." A reference to the biblical book of Hosea, where God promises a permanent, faithful union with His people.</note> Through this, my whole soul awoke, as I was inwardly instructed that, in order to reach the goal for which I strove, the Savior wanted faith alone to be my support from now on, and that I should seek no other life than the purity of this faith. Now I no longer had any trouble bearing my cross and suffering; rather, I loved them, and was willing to bear them until the last day, if His goodness had willed it. I was also well satisfied and rejoiced that He kept His graces to Himself; and I thanked Him with all my heart for preserving them in their purity, since I, on the other hand, defiled them all through my wickedness as soon as they were in me: and so I felt my peace again, which had departed so far away.

9. I was also tempted to abandon prayer entirely: however, no matter how much trouble and difficulty I had in it, I nevertheless held myself in the presence...

This nourished me and kept me content and peaceful; and I was well satisfied to be obedient to His Divine guidance. Meanwhile, I always saw myself as a despicable and lowly object <note>original: "Vorwurf"; in this archaic context, it refers to the object of God's attention or a target of His action.</note>, unworthy of His mercies, as I continually experienced my own inability and how constantly I must depend on this infinite goodness, without whose support I did not see how I could exist for a single moment.

10. The higher part <note>The "superior" part of the soul, which mystics believed was the seat of the intellect and will directed toward the divine.</note> had become lord and master; and it seemed that it took pleasure in maintaining the upper hand in this way. From there, it looked at the lower part in all its raging, without being troubled by it, but remained in its peace as if in its castle. Indeed, it seemed that it was satisfied that its enemies—namely the imagination and the desires of the lower part—suffered and could not harm it. In this state, one fully recognizes the difference between these two parts and how very distinct they are from one another.

11. Gradually my sufferings decreased, and from moment to moment my spirit woke up to cherish Him who was my love. But this spirit was stern and exact, letting nothing break out for the comfort of the lower part <note>The "inferior" part of the soul, associated with physical senses, emotions, and worldly desires.</note>, which sought to have a share in it; whereas the spirit wanted to go to God beyond all sensation, through a very great purity to which it was drawn. And in this way, the delights of the soul were held up and kept in by the power of the spirit; I mean to say, they sought to pour themselves outward into the lower part, but the spirit would not have it, rather sending everything back to God, in whom everything was preserved in its purity; whereas, when the lower part gets a taste of it, it stains everything through its own presumptions and immoderate desires.

12. But just as faith does not consist in sensation, so I had the words that had been spoken inwardly to me deeply impressed upon my heart: *In faith I will betroth myself to You.* <note>original: "Im Glauben will ich mich mit Dir vermählen." This caused me, lifting my heart to this infinite goodness, to say: I have faith, oh my great God; I know that You are, and in that I delight. It was my pleasure to look upon Him in this way; and if someone had asked me about my thoughts, I would have said: I delight in Him who is, and who fills all things. This is a state of great purity,

## The Eighth Chapter.

### Impression of the Divine Perfections. Second Revelation of the Holy Trinity, and Marriage with the Eternal Word. Description and Effects of this Marriage.

->I.<-

After this state, the Divine Majesty gave my soul a very vivid impression of the Divine attributes and essential perfections, all of which together were both love and light to me. As my soul beheld God in its impression as Life, its sighs could say nothing else but: *O Life! O Love!* It possessed within itself a substantial and foundational love which, while loving this Divine primary source of life, would have well desired that its own life were entirely lost, in order to venerate the same most submissively.

<margin>(a) Psalm 133:3</margin>
2. She understood, through a certain kind of logical deduction <note>original: "Folgerung [consequence]"; here meaning a spiritual insight that follows naturally from her experience.</note>, the high truths which are contained in the first chapter of the Gospel of John, where it is said that the Word is Light and Life; and it speaks further of the fullness of this Divine life, which has made us partakers of its abundance; of the infinite happiness of souls who are born not of flesh and blood, but of God; of the inexpressible communication of this life through grace and love; and of the influence of the Word, as the Head of Christians and of holy souls. This influence comes from the fact that His Father did not give Him grace by measure, but in a completely perfect fullness as our Head, so much so that, just as (a) the balsam flowed down from the head of Aaron to the hem of his garments <note>A reference to Psalm 133:2, depicting the anointing of the High Priest as a metaphor for divine grace spreading through the community.</note>, so He also flows in through an overflowing of love into holy and truly Christian souls. Oh, who can express the excellence of this communication! I speak not only of that which happens through [common] grace, but also of the [extraordinary] experiential communication of which I have already spoken several times, and will speak again. No human tongue can signify it; nevertheless, one can easily perceive from what I have said that these impressions are a Divine nourishment for the soul and in no way merely speculative.

3. But to return again to the Divine perfections: When the impression was of the Essence of God, my soul could say nothing else but: *O Essence!* and thereupon she worshipped Him, and had a very deep reverence and very great esteem for the loftiness of this Divine attribute.

Fifth Part. The Life

When I reflected on purity and holiness—which are two closely related divine attributes—all my soul could say was: "O Purity! O Cleanness! O Holiness! O Bottomless Abyss!" I believe I spent more than a year under the impression of these divine attributes (though the deeply rooted foundation of them, which had become like second nature, was never taken from me), but with such clarity and simplicity that I saw their differences as nothing but unity.

My spirit found itself directed toward the unity of God; and in this unity, I was shown His immeasurable greatness, His adorable infinity, and His eternity without beginning or end. I was in a state of wonder that I cannot express; and, as if outside of myself, I said: "O Goodness! O Immensity! O Eternity!" Everything that can be said is nothing compared to this vision; and one must sink down even to hell to worship this great God. <note>The author uses "sinking to hell" as a metaphor for the deepest possible humility and self-abasement—placing herself as low as possible to honor the height of God.</note>

4. I recognized more in this majestic God than can be said or written. All the perfections one might name—that is still not it. One must lose all words and names and be content simply to say, "God, God"; for everything else is less than what must be said of this most adorable Majesty. O God, in what a state was this soul! This filled and transformed me entirely. I saw that all things belong to this God, from whom comes everything beautiful and everything good; and in this vision, I cried out: "O more than good! more than beautiful! more than adorable! Ah, You are God, and a great God!" This word, "God," remained so impressed upon my soul that it knew nothing else but that.

5. But after this great effect of love, my spirit was occupied with each of the divine perfections, consuming itself in acts of adoration, wonder, <term>annihilation</term> <note>In the context of 17th-century mysticism, "annihilation" (Vernichtigung) refers to the soul's attempt to strip away its own ego and will to become "nothing" so that God can be "everything."</note>, and surrender to this great "All." My spirit was pleased that its God is pleased, and that He is and shall eternally be what He is. It was far from my soul to inquisitively investigate or want to know more about this God; for she had such reverence for God that she was like a tiny midge in her own eyes—so greatly was she humbled and annihilated within herself. All this did not hinder love; but it was quite different from before. That is, it was not in tenderness and tears, but was strong and courageous. I was twenty-six or twenty-seven years old at that time.

6. Since I have now said that which the Spirit who leads me urges me to say, I am full of fear and shame while writing this. I am truly convinced that my imperfect life has not responded, and still does not respond, to such high graces. Therefore, I write this in no other way than with a humbled and dejected mind. Obedience alone consoles me, along with the Spirit who gives me what I should write.

### Of Marie of the Incarnation. Chapter VIII. ###

7. I have always noticed that whenever the Divine Majesty wished to show me some extraordinary graces, He would—aside from the preparations which He worked in me (as it were) from afar—dispose me for it in a quite singular way when the time came for the matter to be fulfilled. This happened through a foretaste of His peace, which had something truly paradisiacal about it: because of the loftiness of the matter, I cannot express myself any other way. In these premonitions, I said to Him: "What will You do to me, my worthy Love?" Thereupon I experienced His working, and generally, a change in my state followed.

8. So it happened then, after the grace of which I spoke previously, that one morning while I was at prayer, God devoured my spirit into Himself through an unusually powerful pull; I do not know in what position my body remained. Then the sight <note>original: *veuë, nicht vision*. In mystical writing, a "sight" often refers to a direct intellectual or spiritual perception of truth, whereas a "vision" might imply a sensory or pictorial image shown to the mind's eye.</note> of the most holy Trinity was again communicated to me, and its workings revealed, in a more sublime and more distinct way than the first time. The impression I had previously had of it had its primary effect on the intellect; and it seemed to me that His Divine Majesty had given it to me only to instruct me, to strengthen me, and to prepare me for what He wished to show me later. On this occasion, however, although the intellect was just as much—indeed, even more—enlightened than the previous time, the will held the upper hand. The first time I was more in wonder than in love and enjoyment; but this time I was more in love and enjoyment than in wonder, as my soul found itself entirely in the communion and the enjoyment of a God of love.

9. I saw the <gloss>internal communications</gloss> of the three Persons with one another, just as I had seen them the first time: but I was more fully instructed concerning the eternal birth of the Word. O, how unspeakable it is: that the Father, beholding Himself, begets another "Himself," who is His Image and His Word; and that this birth never ceases; that this Word is equal to His Father in power, in loftiness, in majesty; and that the Father and the Word, through their mutual love for one another, bring forth this Spirit of Love, who is likewise equal to them in all things! This seeing is a good above all good, and a knowledge above all knowledge, for it is the blessedness of souls.

10. Now, as I was as it were sunken in the presence of this most adorable Majesty—Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—in recognition and confession of my smallness, and was paying my due debts of adoration and reverence to them; then the most holy Person of the Word gave me to understand that He is in truth the <term>Bridegroom of Souls<note>A central concept in Christian mysticism where the intimate union between God and the human soul is described through the language of marriage and spiritual intimacy.</note></term> who are faithful to Him. I understood this truth with certainty, and the knowledge given to me of it was the immediate preparation for seeing the same thing accomplished in me. At that very moment, this adorable Person took possession of my soul; and as He, with...

### I.

In the spiritual marriage, the state of souls is entirely changed. Where she was previously in a perpetual striving toward the marriage, she now has no more striving [ *tendance* ] <note>original: "Bestrebung [ tendance ]". ### Fifth Part. The Life

2. It is caresses, it is impulses of love which consume them and cause them to die in Him, whereby the soul suffers very sweet deaths—or, more accurately, these deaths are sweetness itself. I wonder if I might find any comparison on earth; but I find none that I could use to describe what the embraces of the Word <note>The "Word" (Logos) refers to Jesus Christ, the second person of the Trinity.</note> and the soul are. For although the soul recognizes that He is the great GOD, of one essence, <insert>[*consubstantial*]</insert> <note>original: "consubstantiel"; a theological term meaning "of the same substance," used to describe the relationship between Christ and God the Father.</note> and equal to His Father—immeasurable, eternal, infinite, through whom all things were created and through whom they exist in their essence—nevertheless, she embraces Him and speaks with Him mouth to mouth. She sees herself exalted by this state of honor: that the Word is her Bridegroom and she is His Bride. She says to Him: "You are mine, and I am yours; that is enough. Let us go, my Bridegroom, let us go about the business that You have commanded me."

3. The soul then has no more desire; she possesses the Beloved. She speaks with Him because He has spoken with her, and that which she says is not even her own language. She carries out her duties to seek His honor in everything and everywhere, according to the knowledge He shares with her, so that He may reign as a sovereign Lord and Master over all hearts.

She continues her exercises of penance <term>Bußübungen</term> <note>Devotional acts performed to show sorrow for sins and to strengthen the spirit.</note>, she consumes herself in works of love toward her neighbor, and becomes all things to all people in order to win them for her Beloved.

4. At times, I had around twenty of my brother's servants <term>Knechte</term> <note>Domestic laborers or farmhands working in her brother's household or business.</note> with me, and I sat with them at the table so that I might have the opportunity to speak with them about what concerned their salvation. They even gave me reports of what they had done and lovingly accused one another of their faults when they had forgotten their duty in any way.

At times I gathered them together to speak of GOD and to instruct them in the keeping of His commandments. I rebuked them without hesitation; yet no matter what I said to them, they remained as submissive to me as children. I compelled some to get back out of bed who had lain down without praying first. They took refuge in me in all their needs, especially in their illnesses. I had a powerful calling for all of this, as well as for looking after them in their sicknesses. At times I had a great number of them lying ill, so that their chamber resembled a hospital <term>Spital</term>, and I was then their nurse. And in all these works, I thought I was serving my divine Bridegroom; hence it happened that I had such physical agility that everything was easy for me; I made the beds for both the sick and the healthy.

5. I was often compelled to surrender myself to those inner stirrings which He who possessed my soul gave me for the purpose of refreshing me in the toil and labor to which I had given myself for His love’s sake. I threw myself down upon the ground to humble myself and to testify to Him that I was infinitely indebted to Him for providing me the opportunity to [serve] Him a

### Of Marie of the Incarnation. Chapter IX.

->U u 3<-

...to perform some small service in these lowly works, wherein I found a treasure. There He then doubled His caresses, and I was forced to withdraw and close myself away so that no one might come upon me. As His immeasurable [working of love] <note>The German text uses "Liebeswirkung," referring to the internal effect or operation of divine love upon the soul.</note> ignited such a fire within me that I could not draw breath, I said to Him aloud, for my own relief:

> O my love, I can no more! Either let me catch a little breath, because my weakness cannot bear the excess of Your love, or take my life from me entirely: for Your impulses of love cause me such suffering as a soul locked in the prison of the body <note>The "prison of the body" is a common mystical theme, suggesting the soul feels restricted by physical existence while yearning for total union with God.</note> cannot endure.

It seemed to me that He took pleasure in what I said to Him: and it was also His Spirit that made me speak, and which did not allow me to remain silent.

Though He is such a great GOD, and I am nothing, I nevertheless said to Him:

> O my love, if You were to send me into hell, I must still love You, I must still caress You, and You must still be the entire possession of my heart: for I can long for nothing else but You alone, O my great GOD, O my great love.

6. The Savior afterward lessened these great and violent attacks and gave me in their place such a great inner occupation that it caused me to forget everything. In this forgetfulness of all worldly things, I said to our Savior:

> Oh, my love, I pray You, allow me to think of that which I have to do for my neighbor, and afterward I will caress You again;

thereupon He permitted me to think of it, and I performed all the business well which, by His allowance, constantly came before me.

7. The necessity of the body caused me, unobserved, some small interruptions <note>original: "entre deux"; French for "intervals" or "in-betweens."</note> which, however short they might be, caused the soul a certain kind of martyrdom, as she could not be parted for a single moment from the embraces and the sight of the Beloved. The greatest hindrance, however, was sleep, which yet did not last long; therefore the soul said:

> Oh, my Beloved, when shall I at last sleep no more?

As soon as I awoke from my hard bed, I sang a song (in the spirit) to my Divine Bridegroom, which His Spirit produced within me, and which would have been capable of bursting my heart if He had not supported me in an extraordinary way. Because my body was now extremely exhausted, I was forced to say:

> My Divine Love, I pray You, let it sleep a little, so that when it has rested, it may serve You anew tomorrow, since You still wish it to live;

thereupon it slept a little: but in the moment that I awoke, I entered again into active <note>original: "actuel"; in mystical theology, "actual" or "active" love refers to a conscious, focused state of adoration as opposed to a general or habitual state.</note> love, of which sleep had robbed me, and said:

> Ah, my precious love! When shall I at last sleep no more?

> What do You not do with us! Now You wound us; now You bind us through Your sweet slaveries <term>sweet slaveries: a common mystical paradox where being "bound" to God is experienced as the ultimate spiritual freedom</term>. Ah, what a sweet Love You are!

> Love, what do You so gladly wish to do? What pleases You? Are these Your delights, and the sweet play of Your love?
>
> Yes, my sweetest Love, You take pleasure in our amorous longing. Ah, how true it is that You are Love!
>
> I know what I will do to You: I will throw myself toward You <note>original: "me lancer vers vous," a French phrase reflecting Marie's native tongue</note>, and do to You again as You do to my soul.
>
> Yes, yes, You shall be my slave; I will never let You go; I will have You according to my wish and desire; and You shall always be my sweet Love.
>
> But what shall I do with You? For You are entirely mine: mine You are forevermore, O my desired life!
>
> Ah, my All, what is it that I want from You? I want Love from You, and I want nothing else but Love. Ah, it is You I wish to have, my sweet and my beloved Love, in the sweetest death of Love, and so that I may be entirely consumed in the flames of Love.
>
> O Love, O great Love, You are everything, and I am nothing: but it is enough that the All loves the Nothing, and that the Nothing loves the All.
>
> O my GOD, O my great GOD, be praised by all tongues, be loved by all hearts!

My soul is so accustomed to speaking thus, that even in the night, when I happen to wake and am still half-asleep, I already perceive these words in the depths of my soul: O my GOD! or others that I have recounted here.

# The Tenth Chapter.

## Her Various Torments of Love and Intimacies. Further Simplification of Her Spirit. She Does What the Blessed in Heaven Do. Her Desire and Vocation for the Cloistered Life. Entrance into the Cloister.

->I.<-

[(As I continue with this excerpt of this incomparable biography, I see that it is growing under my hands; I therefore find myself compelled to pass over, untouched, various miracles of Divine Love in this beloved bride of the Eternal Word <note>The "Eternal Word" refers to Jesus Christ, based on the Gospel of John’s description of the "Logos."</note>, both here and elsewhere. In particular, at this time, all sorts of wonderful torments of love <term>torments of love: in mystical tradition, this refers to a state where the soul's longing for God is so intense it feels like a physical or spiritual wound</term> and wounds of love befell her, which wrung from her the most tender and intimate complaints against her Bridegroom. These may be read with wonder in her full biography; here, I will only set down the conclusion of these effects. The first part that follows she wrote to her spiritual guide, and the last to her sweet Love (in the form of a letter), though in the first part she also addresses her Love more than her guide.]

> 2. My sweet Love, my sweet Love, my adorable delights, do You then find pleasure in my languishing? Do You not know that my desire is true? Yes, You know it, for my heart is laid bare in Your presence, near the altar of Your holy heart. Let me then be entirely Yours, just as You are entirely mine: possess me, and let me possess You, through a commingling of love. Once again, most holy altar, let this sacrifice take place upon You. O adorable glow, ignite the one who cannot live except in Your flames. Would it be possible that I see myself so near to You, and laid upon a fiery altar, without being consumed by love? But, O mysteries! O mysteries! You find pleasure in my cross and suffering. For, O my sweet Love, I am united with You, and with Your ignited heart; and yet I live and die at the same time. I live; for one cannot be united with You without Your life living in us and expressing itself through us. O wonderful life! And I die; because this union is also a death that puts an end to everything that You are not. Since I now so live and die, I am not my own, but Yours, O my dear All, O my Love, O my only Desired One.

3. These were my conversations during (external) work and unrest, both at the time of prayer and in the streets, and in whatever place I was. I languished for love, and yet I also enjoyed love. I do not know how to say it; one suffers, one languishes, one enjoys. It is a great self-denial for me to write such things; but I cannot tell the manner of my guidance without at the same time making known such things which I wished might remain forever secretly hidden in my heart.

# Chapter Ten.

## Her Various Martyrdoms of Love and Intimacies. Further Simplification of Her Spirit. She Does What the Blessed in Heaven Do. Her Longing and Calling to the Cloistered Life. Entrance into the Monastery.

->1.<-

[(As I see, in continuing the extract of this incomparable biography, that it is growing under my hand, I find myself compelled to pass over, untouched, various wonders of Divine Love in this beloved **Bride of the Eternal Word** <note>original: "Braut des ewigen Worts"; a mystical title for a soul deeply united with Christ/the Logos</note>, both here and elsewhere. In particular, there befell her around this time all manner of wonderful **martyrdoms of love** and **wounds of love** <note>In mystical tradition, these refer to the intense, almost painful longing for God that "wounds" the soul with desire</note>, which pressed from her the most tender and intimate complaints toward her Bridegroom. ### Fifth Part. The Life

4. [In another letter to her guide, she says:] I have suffered the utmost pain because I did not love enough; this causes a pain that tortures the heart. In view of this, our Savior gave me such a powerful drawing of love <note>original: "Liebeszug"; a mystical term for the soul being irresistibly pulled toward God</note> that it seemed to me I held my heart in my hands and offered it to Him as a sacrifice. And as I could do nothing more, I saw in the spirit the love which so many saints of both sexes have borne for Him, and yet all this love was not enough for me. For I can endure no limited love within myself; and all of this seemed small to me in view of my **JESUS**. In short, my soul was insatiable; she wanted the fullness of love. In this drawing of love, these inner anxieties oppressed me beyond measure through the lovely presence of my Beloved, who was so present to me that I cannot express it. Oh, how sweet is this martyrdom, in which the soul sees herself entirely transformed into the Object of her love <note>original: "Vorwurf"; in this mystical context, it refers to the divine Archetype or the focus of her contemplation</note>, which keeps her so closely united with Him! This is a taste without taste; I cannot express it.

5. After this occupation of the spirit, I could do nothing else for two or three days but say to Love: "Oh, how can this be? A miserable heart, is it truly worthy of Jesus? And can people who are as wretched as I truly love Jesus?"

I see quite clearly that He is everything and that I am nothing; that He gives Himself entirely to me, and that I can give Him nothing. Am I not then rich in my poverty, since I see that "Everything" within my "Nothing"? Bear with my childish ways and my foolishness.
