### Of Saint Catherine of Genoa. Chapter VIII.

<meta>catchword: 6. But</meta>

pass through; for **Pure Love** passes through, transcends, and elevates itself above all these things; and it is as if she said: “I shall never have rest until I am enclosed within this divine Essence, where all created powers are lost; and where they, after being lost, are transformed <note>original: "vergestaltet," meaning reshaped or refashioned into a new form</note> and remain Divine.” Outside of this, this Pure and true Love can find no rest.

2. Therefore I am resolved for my whole life long to say to the world: Do with my outward self whatever you will; but as for my inner self, leave it as it is; for I cannot and will not allow it to be occupied (or taken up with anything) other than God, who has taken it for Himself and has so enclosed Himself within it that He will open it to no one. As great as His omnipotence is, so strong is He; and He does nothing incessantly but consume this human creature, from within and without, through His love; then when it is entirely consumed, and thus united with God, it will depart from this body, and the soul will enter into Paradise above.

<margin>(a) Galatians 2:20 <note>“I have been crucified with Christ; it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me.”</note></margin>
3. Therefore it happens that in my inner self I can tolerate nothing other than God; He Himself permits neither me nor anything else to enter there; yes, me even less than anything else, because I am a greater enemy to Him than all the rest <note>Catherine refers to the "self" or ego as the primary obstacle to God’s work</note>. Whenever it happens that I must speak this word *I* in order to talk with the world, which cannot speak otherwise—whether I name myself or am named by others—I say within myself: this *I* is (a) God, and I no longer know any *I*, but only my God. Just so I say, when I speak of being <term>Wesen: essence or being</term>: Everything that has being has it only from the Supreme Being of God through His communication.

4. Only man alone has made for himself his own essence, which is entirely different from that which God had given him, and it is impossible for it to exist together with man’s salvation. Therefore, we must necessarily subject this "own essence" <note>original: "eigene Wesen," the false self or ego-identity</note>—which we have made for ourselves and which causes us so many preoccupations and distractions that we are prevented from living as we ought—[this "own essence," I say, we must] subject it to God, so that He may consume it in us, and bring it about that nothing else dwells in us but He alone. Outside of this, the soul will never find rest, nor stability, nor pleasure; because it was created for no other end than for God.

5. This is the reason why God, in every possible way, draws the free will of man to Himself through a thousand sweet caresses; <insert>holy deceptions</insert> <note>original: "tromperies" (French), a mystical term for the "pious frauds" or "traps of love" God uses to lure the soul away from worldly attachments</note>; once He has it in His power, He places it in a state where He can lead it toward the **annihilation** <term>Vernichtigung: the mystical process of making the "self" into nothing so God can be everything</term> of its own essence; and there one finally finds oneself lost in the Essence of God. Thus God has become my *Being*, my *I*, my *Fortress*, my *Salvation*, my *Good*, and my *Delight*.

# Tenth Section. The Life

<margin>(a) Psalm 73:25, in the original <note>original: "im Grund," likely referring to the original Hebrew or the foundational meaning of the verse: "Whom have I in heaven but you? And earth has nothing I desire besides you."</note>.</margin>

6. But this word *mine*, which I use so often and add to all these things, I use only because I cannot speak otherwise. And yet, I do not know what kind of thing this is—this *I*, *mine*, *delight*, *good*, *fortress*, *stability*, *blessedness*. Indeed, I can no longer turn myself toward anything that may be in heaven (a) or on earth. And although I may speak some words that perhaps suggest images or feelings of humility and spirituality, I nevertheless know and feel nothing of them in my inner self; and I am ashamed that I speak so many words which are so far removed from the truth and from that which I feel of it.

7. I see it in truth, that man here below is grossly deceived when he looks upon and esteems things that are not, while in the meantime he withdraws his sight and his esteem from Him who is in Truth. Were the inner eye of man truly pure, he would see quite clearly that a thing which passes away so quickly—however beautiful, good, and useful it may be esteemed in this world—cannot in truth be called *Being* <term>Wesen: In this context, "Being" or "Essence" refers to that which is permanent and unchanging, as opposed to temporary worldly objects</term>; for this word *Being* belongs alone to that which has no end. Therefore, when man seeks to make himself great in temporal things, and not (as he rightly should) in heavenly and eternal things, he deviates from the character of his Noble Nature; he humbles and bows himself down to lowly things, which are far too small to correspond with his greatness.

8. Our spirit is created to love and to delight; this is what it seeks in all things. But never will it be satisfied by temporal things, though it always hopes that it might be able to satisfy itself through them; and while it thus deceives itself, it loses in the meantime—with pure follies—the precious time given to it to seek **GOD**, who is the highest good, in whom it would find the true love and the holy delight for its thorough satisfaction and pleasure. But what will he do at the end, when all his present occupations shall leave him, when the deceptions of vain hope shall reveal themselves, and when he, after having lost his time, shall see himself robbed of all good and plunged into all evil? And finally, when—contrary to his nature—he shall be forcibly robbed of all love and of all pleasure? Ah! I see in this something so wretched and so unbearable that the mere thought of it makes me tremble with terror. When I look upon the terrifying blindness of those who are so senseless that they let themselves be drawn away by such worthless trifles <gloss>original: *bagatelles*</gloss> into such a terrifying abyss of an eternal and infinite evil, I feel my innermost heart <note>original: "Eingeweide," literally "bowels," an archaic term for the seat of deep compassion</note> moved and pierced with dismay and pity.

9. When man lies in his death-throes, then all his pleasures leave him, and all evils approach him, without any help against them. With what distress and sorrow will this soul then be surrounded? Of this I must remain silent, because my heart is so oppressed that I cannot speak of it.

### Of Saint Catherine of Genoa. Chapter VIII.

->K k<-

<meta>catchword: then</meta>

O wretched creature! Then you will see how God had brought about your **blessedness** <term>Seligkeit: A state of eternal happiness and union with God; often translated as salvation or beatitude.</term> with far more care than you yourself were willing to take for it. All the time of your past life will be placed before your eyes, together with all the good opportunities you will have had to do good, and all the good inspirations **[of grace]** that you will have rejected. You will see all this in a moment, without being able to say anything against it. In what state do you think your soul will then be, which, having lived in great injustice, will pass over and appear before true **Justice**? I cannot think of it without trembling; and I am forced to cry out: Consider it well! Consider it well! For the matter is of such great weight that if I knew people would hear and understand me, I would never speak of anything else.

10. For this reason, it happens that when I see a person die, I say to myself: Oh, what exceedingly great and new things this soul will now begin to see! And when I see people die almost like cattle—that is, without fear, without light, without **grace**, even though the matter is of such great weight—then, if God did not preserve me through His **providence**, I would have one of the greatest pains for my neighbor that I could ever have. And when I hear people say: "God is kind, He will forgive us our sins," while in the meantime, despite this infinite kindness, they do not stop doing evil—oh, what distress I endure because of it!

11. When I see that man turns his love toward **creatures** <term>Creaturen: In this mystical context, it refers to any "created thing"—animals, objects, or people—that is not God.</term>, such that he loves a dog, a cat, or another created thing; that he takes such great delight in it and thinks of nothing else; that he also makes himself more of a slave from day to day to the thing he loves; and how, because of this, no other love or other good stirrings of grace find room to enter into him, even though they were so very necessary for him; so an impulse comes over me that I would like to take away from him by force that which keeps him so entangled, and causes him to lose such a precious thing as the love of God, which alone could make him contented and blessed.

12. God created man for eternal blessedness with such a great love that it cannot be grasped; He also provides him with all the means for such a purpose with an infinite, pure, and righteous love. Yes, no matter how great the sins he might have committed, He nevertheless never ceases to give him all necessary good stirrings of grace, reminders, and disciplines <note>original: "Züchtigungen," referring to the trials or "chastisements" God uses to steer a soul back to the right path.</note>, to bring him to the level of blessedness for which He had created him with such fervent love; to such an extent that when man recognizes this after his death, and sees how he never allowed himself to be led to the goodness of God, and how it was his own fault alone that he was not saved; he will be more tormented by this—that he resisted Divine goodness—than by all the pain of hell that he will endure.

<summary>Saint Catherine warns of the soul's profound regret after death when it realizes how it ignored God's constant grace in favor of trivial earthly attachments. She expresses deep distress over those who treat death with indifference or presume upon God's mercy while continuing to sin.</summary>

## The Ninth Chapter.

->Hatred of her own part, or of the corrupted ground of nature, of the self-will, and so forth. Three ways of God to purify man from it.<-

->I.<-

This holy soul recognized her **nothingness** to such an extent that she no longer even wanted to say that she was evil: "I will," she said, "call myself neither good nor evil, for fear that I might imagine myself to still be something; and when I hear someone speak something good of me, I say within myself: 'Ah! if you only knew how I am constituted inwardly, you would not say such things.' And thereafter I turned to my **own part** <note>original: "eigenen Theil." Catherine uses this to refer to the ego, the flesh, or the sinful nature independent of God’s grace.</note>, and said: 'When you hear someone say something of you which might have some appearance of good, know that they speak of nothing that belongs to you, or in which you could have glory; for the good is from **God**, and your own earthly and fleshly part is no more similar to the good than the devil is. But when someone speaks evil of you, think and believe firmly that they cannot say as much evil of you as there is yet much more within you; yes, believe that you are not even worthy to be named in evil, because it then seems as if you were still worthy for someone to remember you.'"

She became an enemy to herself in such a way that when she had to speak of herself in any matter, she did so no longer in the singular, but she said **Us**, in the plural, both in good and in evil. "For," she said, "the own and malicious part of man takes pleasure in being named."

2. She troubled herself over no thing, but kept herself peaceful in everything she did and in everything that happened to her, as much in regard to the soul as to the body. If she happened to commit some fault, she said within herself: "All these things are produced by my malicious part, which of itself can produce no other than such entirely evil fruits; and when it produces no more of the same, it is only because God holds it back and prevents it. But I know this part well; God has given me to clearly recognize the imperfection and malice of our inclinations; to such an extent that I am certain that without the **grace of God** I can in no way do anything other than evil; but as for the good, <insert>to be able to produce such</insert> I have as little hope for that as the devils have, where the grace of God is not with me."

She emphasizes that all good originates from God's grace while all faults stem from the inherent malice of human nature.</summary>

# Of Saint Catherine of Genoa. Chapter IX.

3. When I wish to draw near to **God**, I must be an enemy to His enemies; because I find nothing that is more an enemy or more evil to Him than I, I am forced to hate this "I," this **wicked part**, more than any other thing: therefore, I wish to despise it; and since it is entirely contrary to the Spirit, I wish to separate it from all goods of both this world and the next, and to value it as little as if it no longer existed. For this reason, I have prayed to **God** that He would not allow me to rejoice or grieve over any created thing, out of fear that this **wicked part** might seek itself in some joy or sorrow. I have also prayed to Him that He would take my free will into His hand <insert>[and power]</insert>, so that I may no longer be able to do what I want, but only that which pleases Him; and these things I have also received from His goodness.

4. If I were so foolish (she said further to her own part) as to give you your nourishment according to your so corrupted inclination, which is so contrary to the clarity and purity one owes to **God**, I would commit two very dangerous evils: first, I would never be able to satisfy you; and second, I would make you stronger from day to day, so that you could strike me all the more fiercely and wound me ever more deeply; yes, because you are so full of malice, you would secretly disguise yourself in a spiritual form <note>Catherine warns that the ego is deceptive and can even hide behind religious activities or spiritual pride.</note>. Therefore, speak not another word to me of what you need for the maintenance of your life, for I am determined to listen to your speeches no more.

Know that you are in such contempt with me that I would rather be in **Hell** without you, than be deified and glorified through your mediation, if one may speak so.

5. Finally, as this **wicked part** <note>original: "boshaftige Theil." A term Catherine uses to describe the "self-will" or the lower, fallen nature of a human being.</note> saw that it was thus cornered, it could give no more answer, but withdrew from me in such a way that it no longer dared to speak. It looked neither to the body nor to the soul, neither toward Heaven nor to the earth; but I saw that it retired and hid itself as if in a corner of the house of my soul, with all its wicked inclination, which was so evil that if **God** had let this part have its way, it would have acted worse against **God** in its desperation than **Lucifer** <term>Lucifer: Literally 'Light-bringer'; referring here to the fallen angel whose pride led to a rebellion against God.</term>. Only, I saw that **God** constantly held back this **own part**; and this sight did not pain or grieve me, but rather gave me joy; for he who loves justice rejoices that thieves are hanged. Now, he who is evil according to the nature he has brought upon himself through sin, and yet wants to be regarded as good, just as if he possessed such goodness through his own nature, he is a thief; because he robs **God** of what belongs to Him alone: and therefore he is worthy to be hanged in **Hell**.

6. As I now saw that its wicked mind and inclination were so greatly brought down, punished, and annihilated by **God**, I became truly content with it; and I had all the more pleasure in it, the more the malice of this own

### Part Ten. The Life

...was known, and so I had all the more reason to place my glory in the frank recognition and confession of my great malice, as justice required. It seems to me that if I should fear anything, it would have to be this "own part" <note>German: *eigenes Theil*. This refers to the self-centered ego or the fallen human nature that Catherine views as the source of all sin.</note>. But because I saw this very thing in **God’s** hand, and I had given myself entirely over to Him in trust, I no longer had any fear; I no longer thought of that "own part"; I esteemed it as little as if I had never had anything to do with it.

7. I saw then that others wept over their evil minds and malicious inclinations; that they sought to oppose them through many kinds of effort; but that the more they struggled to remedy their failings, the more they committed. Whenever someone recounted all their pains to me, I answered: "You have miseries and weep for them; I have miseries too, and I do not weep for them. You do evil and you weep for it, and I would do exactly as you do if the Almighty **God** did not hold me back. You cannot protect yourself from it, and I cannot do so either. Therefore, we must of necessity abandon ourselves and entrust the care of our work to Him who alone is powerful enough to preserve us from evil; and then He will do that which we cannot do of ourselves." In this way, one can have peace from this malicious part which, by its nature, torments us always and from all sides; but when it is thus taken captive by **God**, bound and held back, it bows under the yoke and no longer opens its mouth.

8. "I see," she said, "three kinds of means and ways that **God** employs to purify man. First, He gives him such a bare love <note>The term "bare" or "naked" love (*blosse Liebe*) refers to a love for God that is stripped of all self-interest or desire for emotional reward.</note> that he can want or see nothing other than this love; because it is so bare and pure, it allows him to see the smallest specks of dust and the subtlest movements of self-love. As he perceives this truth, he can no longer be deceived by the 'own part,' but instead places this part into such great despair that he will allow it no nourishment, whether physical or spiritual. In this manner, self-love is gradually consumed. Nevertheless, this self-love is so manifold and so malicious that it accompanies man almost to the end of his life. I experience this well, for from day to day I become aware that various inclinations have been consumed in me that previously seemed good and perfect; but after they are consumed, I recognize that they were evil and stemmed from my physical and spiritual weakness, which I did not see and thought I no longer possessed."

9. "The second means of purification, and the one which pleases me better than the former, is this: when **God** imparts to man a spirit that is kept in great suffering and tribulation; for this allows him to recognize his own smallness and nothingness. Because he keeps himself, through this knowledge, in a very great poverty regarding everything that can have any 'taste' <note>In mystical literature, "taste" refers to the pleasurable feelings or emotional satisfactions found in spiritual practices.</note>, the 'own part' can nourish itself in no way but must of necessity consume itself, and the soul finally recognizes that if **God** did not lay His hand upon it and offer His divine being as an object...

# The Tenth Chapter.

->She describes in her own person how **God** arranges a soul that has completely surrendered to Him, according to all its faculties <note>German: *Gemüthskräfte*. This refers to the traditional philosophical powers of the soul: understanding, will, and memory.</note>, and holds it bound to Him through pure love: her pure love: **God's** order in conversion: the wonderful state of transformed souls.<-

->I.<-

This holy soul said: When **God** wants to properly order a soul, and it only follows Him <note>original: *corresponde*. This implies a cooperative response or "correspondence" between the human will and divine grace.</note> with its free will, surrendering itself entirely into His hands, He leads it to all perfection. He did this with a certain soul whom, after He had touched and converted her, never again fulfilled her own will. In her innermost ground, she was always attentive to the will of **God**, which she felt imprinted upon her soul; and she had such trust that she sometimes said to **God**: "I have this trust in You, that You will not let me fail in everything that I think, or speak, or do."

2. Regarding the understanding <note>German: *Verstand*. Here meaning the intellect or the faculty of reason.</note>, such an arrangement was made in this soul that she never sought to understand any matter, whether in heaven or on earth, not even the spiritual workings occurring within her. She practiced this so faithfully that she thereafter sought nothing more, neither in herself nor in others.

<header>Tenth Section. The Life</header>

One might ask here, what then kept the power of the **intellect** <term>Verstand: the faculty of logical reasoning and comprehension</term> occupied? I answer that all the powers of the soul were constantly guided and moved by **GOD**; and whenever she was required to act, it was made known to her at the very moment it was necessary to do so, and immediately afterward the gate was closed.

3. Regarding the memory of things that had passed through the intellect, she could say nothing; for just as little remained of them as if she had possessed no memory or intellect at all. This did not come from human reflection <note>original: *menschlichen Nachsinnen*; the deliberate, analytical thinking process of the ego</note>; rather, it was because she was moved by **GOD** so that she saw, recognized, and performed something in one and the same moment. This was to such an extent that she could easily perceive it must be **GOD** who was acting during the time she was held so occupied; she had neither time, nor space, nor will, nor freedom to turn anywhere else but where **GOD** turned her in an instant. She could attend to nothing else but what **GOD** presented to her from moment to moment, in such a way that she paid no further heed to her actions than what the necessity of the matter at hand required. But as soon as the task was done, the memory let the matter drop again, and just as little remained with her as if she had never performed it.

4. It was in the very same manner with her natural affection, which from the beginning was taken away by her love, so that she could have no affection for any created or uncreated things—even for **GOD** Himself, that is to say, for the sensibilities, visions, tastes, and other spiritual gifts [correspondences] <note>original: *correspondances*; refers to spiritual communications or perceived mystical connections</note> of which she saw others made so much account. She fled these as much as she could; but the more she sought to flee them, the more she received them, and they increased within her to such an extent that, after she had done much violence to herself to resist them, her body was completely crushed by it. When she could no longer bear such a burden, she threw herself, as if broken, into a corner and remained there until this intensity had passed, which greatly weighed down the body; but her spirit was entirely rapt out of her and completely sunken in divine sweetness. When she stood up again, it seemed to her that it was better for her soul and her body, even though she sought this "better" nowhere else but in **GOD**, her love.

5. This uprightness of the will made her deliberate and careful, and always so united and enclosed with **GOD** that between her and Him neither any deception, nor imaginings, nor any inspirations or truths could intervene which were not immediately [such] in **GOD**.

6. After **GOD** had delivered this soul from the heavy burden of self-interest <note>original: *eigenen Theils*; literally "own part," referring to the ego, self-will, or the tendency to claim actions as one's own</note>, the spirit found itself entirely lightened and fit to perform great works. And as the impulse of love that **GOD** had given her saw itself separated and freed from this self-interest, it found itself entirely free, indeed so powerful and great, that

# The Life of Saint Catherine of Genoa. Chapter X. #

...that it found no place in all things below **God** where it could rest in peace.

7. When **God** now saw this soul so prepared and well-ready, He threw to her from heaven one end of the most holy rope of His pure, clean, and straight love, with which He kept her constantly occupied in Himself; and she responded to Him just as promptly, purely, and in the same manner as He lowered Himself to her. For she could no longer touch, see, or feel Him through her own self <note>the "own part" or ego</note>. And in this way, she let the water flow as pure and clear as it came down from the living source: so that through her love, and because of her great purity, she discovered the very smallest little straw that might be a hindrance to her vision. And had she been able to say how significant the very smallest hindrance was to her, the hardest hearts would have turned to dust out of great consternation.

8. It happened one day that a certain Preaching Friar <note>original: *Prediger-Mönch*; a member of the Dominican Order</note>, either to test her or out of a false imagination (†) [as often happens], said to her: that he was much better able to love **God** than she was. At that time, she was still living with her husband. He wanted to prove this by the fact that, upon entering his Order, he had renounced all things internally and externally, and therefore could love **God** much more freely and ardently than she. He cited other similar reasons that are often used by people who are more learned than they are holy or devout, specifically basing his argument on the fact that she was married in the world, while he lived in a religious order. When he had spoken many words on this, the blessed Catherine was set into such an inflammation of this pure love that she could no longer listen to his talk. Instead, she rose up with such zeal that she seemed to be entirely outside herself, and said to him: "If I believed that your habit <note>the distinctive clothing of a religious order</note> could give me but a single tiny spark of love more, I would tear it off you however I could, if I were not otherwise allowed to wear it. As for the rest, that you should earn more merit <term>Verdienst: the spiritual 'credit' for good works or sacrifices</term> than I because you have renounced all things for **God’s** sake and live in a religious order, I grant you that; for that is not what I seek—you may keep all of that for yourself. But that I should not be able to love **God** as much as you, you shall never persuade me, say what you will."

Afterward, when she came home, she spoke to the **Lord** (as she was accustomed to speaking so intimately to Him): "O my Love! who shall prevent me from loving You? Could the state in which I find myself do so? Oh no! Even if I were in the midst of an army of soldiers, I would still not be prevented from being able to love You. If the world or husbands could prevent the pure love of **God**, then it would surely be a weak virtue and a love that was not worth much. But from what I have experienced of it, and as much as I still feel of it, I see that nothing can overcome this love, and thus nothing can hinder it; rather, it overcomes and surpasses all things."

3. 4. # Tenth Part. The Life

9. This holy soul affirmed that she never expressed anything so great to anyone without it seeming to her as if she were merely mocking [the truth] and saying nothing (†) in comparison to what she felt in her pure and direct love. This purity and clarity of love was unspeakable, and she possessed this love so abundantly that she could not conceive how it could have grown further [no matter what anyone might have suggested to the contrary (†)] because she was always so full that she could desire nothing more than that which completely satisfied her. Nevertheless, love did not cease to be diligent in cleansing this precious and chosen vessel, expanding its capacity, and filling it ever more. Therefore she said: I feel every day that small splinters of imperfection are taken from me, which this pure love draws out; love is much occupied with its piercing and clear eyes, which discover the very smallest and most secret imperfections—things which, in a lesser love, would seem to be perfections. **GOD** carries out this work without the person being aware of it; for if one saw one's own imperfections, one would not be able to endure them. **GOD** shows the person the perfection that is in His work without letting them see their own imperfections; nonetheless, He takes them away, even though they should be recognized by no human understanding.

10. When **GOD** calls us to His love and draws us away from the love of the world, He finds us (1) full of sins and vices. And (2) He gives us a desire for the virtues. (3) He entices us toward perfections. And (4) afterward, He leads us through His grace, which He pours out into us, to the true annihilation <note>In mystical theology, "annihilation" refers to the process of emptying the self-will and ego so that the soul can be fully occupied by God.</note> of ourselves. And finally (5) to the true transformation into Him.

<margin>(a) Impassible <note>original Latin-derived term: *impassibilis*, meaning incapable of suffering or being affected by external pain</note>; the old edition has "impossible."</margin>

11. This is the order that **GOD** is accustomed to keeping in order to lead the soul to Him. But when the soul is annihilated and transformed, it no longer acts, it no longer speaks, it does not will, it does not feel, it does not understand, it does not comprehend, and it has within itself—neither internally nor externally—no longer any sensitivity that could be moved; instead, **GOD** governs and leads it in all things, without the mediation of any other creature. The state of these souls is then a sensation of such great peace and stillness that it seems to them as if they, with their heart and all their inward parts, internally and externally, were submerged in an ocean of the deepest and most blessed stillness, from which they never emerge, no matter what might happen to them in this life. They remain immovable, without being able to be disturbed; and the soul is so liberated from the passions (a) that it seems to her she feels nothing in the soul and in the spirit, internally and externally, except a most sweet peace. She is so filled with this peace that if one were to put her flesh, her veins, and her bones into a press, nothing else but peace would come out. At such times, she testifies how she spends entire days singing songs of joy, which she has made according to her own way <gloss>mode</gloss>:
> "Do you wish," she says, "that I should quickly show you what **GOD** is? He is Peace, and whoever separates himself from Him finds no peace."

<meta>catchword: Din</meta>

O miserable man! (she thus cried out in dismay at the folly of men) now you are so hardened that you will not think of this unavoidable misfortune; but know that you will undoubtedly find it at the time when it can no longer be helped, for the smallest flaw can have no place in eternity.

4. ### Of St. Catherine of Genoa. Ch. XI.

As for the things that **God** worked in her, it seemed to her as if **God** had, in a manner of speaking, forced her; for she did not see that she had consented, but rather that she had resisted, especially in the beginning; and this insight inflamed her in a fervent love.

6. Speaking generally otherwise, she said: **God** initially entices man to pull himself out of sin; thereafter He enlightens the understanding with the light of faith, and also kindles the will with a certain taste <note>original: "Geschmack." In mystical theology, this refers to a "spiritual relish" or an experiential "savoring" of divine presence that moves the heart beyond mere intellectual belief.</note>. The Almighty **God** does all of this in a single moment, even if we—in order to express ourselves in our own way—distinguish these as if they happened at different times. **God** does this, however, more abundantly or more sparingly according to whether He sees beforehand that it will produce much or little fruit; nevertheless, He gives everyone so much light and grace that they can be preserved by it, provided they do their part and give **God** their consent.

7. This consent happens in such a fashion: namely, after **God** has performed His work and knocked at the door, it is enough for the man to say: "Lord! I consent, and I am satisfied with this: do with me whatever pleases You. I am resolved never to sin again, and for the sake of Your love to leave all things of this world." And this consent happens as soon as the will of man unites with **God’s** will, although the will itself might not perceive this, and the man might not be able to see this secret consent.

8. This union now binds the person to **God** with an almost unceasing bond: for when **God** has obtained this consent from the man, He thereafter does almost everything; if the man then allows himself to be led by Him, He leads him to the perfection to which He has appointed him.

9. The more the man then recognizes his misery, the more he humbles himself and surrenders himself to **God**, recognizing that He alone is the one who must carry out this work of His; just as he then gradually learns to recognize this through the constant good inspirations that **God** sends him; when he then perceives these divine workings and their benefit, he says to himself: "It seems **God** has nothing else to do but to care for me." Oh, how sweet and lovely are the workings of **God** toward us!

10. O free will! [you who can either give room to these great workings or resist them] of how much good and of how much evil are you the cause? If you deprived yourself of your own self out of love for **God**, you would soon find yourself in a freedom that could never fail you thereafter; yes, you would recognize even in this life that *to serve God is truly to reign* <note>original: "GOtt dienen, wahrlich herrschen sey." This is a translation of the famous Latin paradox *servire Deo regnare est*, suggesting that true sovereignty is found in submission to the Divine.</note>; for because **God** frees man from sin, which makes him a slave, He redeems him from all servitude and places him, in contrast, into true freedom; otherwise, man always goes from one desire to another without ever being satisfied; for the more...

->She is completely lost in the love of **God**, without injury<-

->I.<-

This holy soul, who was transfigured <note>original: "vergestaltet." This suggests a fundamental change in her being or form to mirror the divine.</note> in **God** in such a high manner, told such deep and sublime things of **God**, her sweet love, that they surpassed all human understanding: I have, she said, through the grace of **God**, a satisfaction without nourishment <note>In mystical theology, "satisfaction without nourishment" refers to a state where the soul is fulfilled by God directly, without needing external spiritual "food" like specific meditations or rituals.</note>, and a love without fear, which is to say, one that never diminishes. Faith appears to me to be entirely lost, and hope to be dead; for it seems to me that I already have and possess that which I previously believed and hoped for; I no longer see a union, because I see only **God** alone without myself. I do not know where I am, and I do not seek to know it, nor do I wish to have any news of it. I am so sunken in the primal source of this great love, which exceeds all measure, just as if I were sunken in the sea and could see or feel nothing but the water; I am so sunken in this sweet fire of love that I can no longer comprehend anything but the love which makes, as it were, all the marrow of my soul and my body melt away.

2. It seems to me that I am no longer of this world, and I can no longer perform the works that I see others doing; they are all tedious to me, I cannot and I will not do anymore as they do, and as I myself did before. I feel myself entirely removed from the things of this earth, and especially from my own: it is unbearable to me to look at them further; and I say to all things: leave me in peace, for I can no longer have any care or memory of you, just as if you no longer existed as far as I am concerned.

3. I can no longer work, nor walk, nor stand, nor even speak: I look at myself as a thing that is useless and superfluous to the world. Many people wonder at this and are offended by it, because they do not know the cause of it: And truly, if **God** did not take care of me, I would be considered foolish by the world; because I live as if I were led away out of myself.

4. Nevertheless, this holy soul was guided by **God** in such a way that she was able to give satisfaction to everyone according to their necessity and fairness; and although she was entirely occupied with how she might satisfy her sweet Love, she never wished to displease her neighbor with words or deeds, nor cause him the slightest harm, nor leave him in his need. And she once said to **God**: You command me, O Lord! that I should love my neighbor, yet I can love nothing but You, and cannot allow anything else to mingle alongside You; what then shall I do? Whereupon she received an answer within: Everyone who loves me also loves everything that I love. You must be ready for the salvation of your neighbor to do everything that is necessary, both for his soul and for his body. This love is secure, because it has no self-interest; and in this way, the neighbor is loved not in himself, but in **God**.

5. Pure love, she said, is capable of no pain, nor can it comprehend what pain or torment might be. Indeed, if it were possible that it could feel all the pain of the devils and damned souls, it would not be able to say that such a thing was pain; for when pain is seen and felt, such a thing is truly outside of this Pure Love. True and Pure Love <note>The term "Pure Love" (reine Liebe) was a central concept in 17th and 18th-century mysticism, referring to a love for God that is completely disinterested, seeking no reward and fearing no punishment.</note> is of such great power that it keeps the lover always fixed and immovable upon the Beloved, and never gives him the capacity to see or feel anything other than Pure Love. Therefore, he who tries to make the things of this world sensible to it labors in vain; for it remains in its aim <note>original: "Vorwurf." In this context, it refers to the object of her contemplation or her spiritual orientation.</note> as immovable as a dead person.

6. This soul confessed that from the time she had been wounded by the love of **God** <note>The "wound of love" is a traditional mystical metaphor (often associated with the Song of Solomon) describing a spiritual longing so intense it feels like a physical injury.</note>, she never knew what it was to suffer, whether internally or externally, whether from the world, or from the devils, or from the flesh, or from wherever it might come; this was because she was internally so transformed <note>original: "vergestaltet." This implies her very form or being had been reshaped into the divine likeness.</note> in **God** that, although she had to suffer many adversities within herself, she did not feel them in her will as adverse things; rather, she accepted them as messengers from her Love; so much so, that being mingled with this love, they all together caused her great pleasure.

7. No words or images can be spoken of this love which, in comparison with the truth of what it is, would not be outright lies. One can understand nothing of it, except this: that it cannot be grasped by the intellect. And if one asks me: What is it then that I see and feel? I answer: That first I feel a thing that is beyond the understanding; and beyond this I feel another much greater thing; and beyond this again one that is much greater still; and so on, step by step from greatness to greatness, into the infinite.

8. I cannot understand it, she said, how man can be so blind that he does not see how everything which **God** does not support and maintain through His grace, and which He does not hold as pleasing, is filled with pure pain, heartache, bitterness, resentment, anger, sadness, misfortune, and torment, even already in this—

9. Oh, in what great danger is man in this life! When I think of it, and see how significant spiritual death and spiritual life truly are, I would die of terror if **God** did not sustain me. And if I could have any desire, it would be this: that I might be able to express to others what I recognize and feel regarding this; indeed, were it permitted for me to prove it to them through my own agony and torture, I do not believe there are punishments and torments to be found in the world so cruel that I would not willingly endure them, just to give people some sense of the importance of such a great matter. Oh, how significant and terrifying is the shadow of even the smallest deed committed against **God**! I no longer wonder that Hell is so terrible, for it was made for sin; yet, I believe that Hell itself is not yet as terrifying as sin is in its own right.

10. For this brave warrior <note>Catherine is often described as a "warrior" or "combatant" because of her intense struggle against her own ego and "self-will."</note>, nothing was difficult to endure except the sight of her having offended **God**. Regarding the offenses I have committed against You, I wish that they had never happened, and I cannot allow that I ever offended You; in the hour of my death, let all the devils, with all their terrors and judgments, appear before my eyes rather than the sight of my sins; for I count the former as nothing compared to the sight of an offense committed against You, (+) <note>This symbol likely refers to a marginal addition or a specific point of emphasis in the original manuscript.</note> however small it may seem—though it can never truly be small, because Your so great Majesty is offended by it.

11. What great evil does sin cause, no matter how small it may be? For it creates a discord and a separation between **God** and the soul; and if it were possible for **God** to endure any pain, He would suffer very great distress because of this separation; indeed, far more than the soul can endure, because **God** has infinitely more love for our souls than the soul has for **God**. It is said that the soul has "offended" **God** through sin, although, strictly speaking, **God** cannot be offended; <note>This reflects the theological concept of "divine impassibility"—the idea that God, being perfect and self-sufficient, cannot be "hurt" or "changed" by human actions, but that our relationship with Him is what suffers.</note> but one intends to convey by this that the soul has pushed **God** away, He who intended to do her good with such great love. Otherwise, one knows well enough that actually the person who sins suffers the damage from it and offends themselves; but because **God** loves us more than we love ourselves, and cares more for our benefit than we do ourselves, it is therefore said: "He is offended," just as it truly would be if **God** were capable of suffering.

12. But blinded man does not consider such great goodness, such great love, such great care from **God**. But when the soul [is touched] by divine love...

# Chapter Thirteen
## Of Self-Love and Divine Love, and the Qualities and Effects of Both.

-> I. <-

1. This holy soul once had a vision of self-love <note>In mystical theology, *Eigenliebe* (self-love) is the fundamental egoism that separates the soul from God.</note>: that its lord and master is the devil, and that it should better be called "self-hatred," because it causes every evil to be inflicted upon man and ultimately casts him into Hell. She saw how it is, as it were, naturalized and inherent within man, so that it is almost impossible to be purified of it in this life.

2. Self-love, she said, cares neither for the harm of the soul, nor of the body, nor of the neighbor, nor of an honorable name, nor for its own property or that of others; rather, it is truly cruel, both toward itself and toward others, simply so that it may satisfy its own will. It will submit to no one, no matter what resistance or obstacles it may encounter. If it has something in mind, it allows itself to be turned from its purpose neither by endearments nor by threats.

3. Self-love holds the person who is possessed by it in such slavery <term>Sclaverey: here meaning the spiritual bondage where a person's free will is overridden by their selfish impulses</term> that it does with him whatever it wishes; it pulls him wherever it pleases. He is so utterly subject to it that he dares not will, think, or perform anything except that which it dictates to him. Where self-love reigns, one does not care whether they are considered foolish or clumsy, or even if they are mocked and despised by everyone; one has eyes and ears closed to everything. One sees nothing except what self-love wants to see; everything else is regarded as nothing.

4. Self-love is a cunning thief <unclear>that it</unclear> even robs **GOD** without hesitation;

### Part Ten. The Life

...by appropriating to herself what belongs to **GOD**, and keeping it for herself, she furthermore insists that she does so by right, under the pretext of necessity—as if she could not live without it. In all of this, she works in such a subtle and hidden manner, concealing herself behind so many cloaks of good appearance, that one could never convict her of the contrary except through the clear-sighted and piercing light of true love. True love desires to remain naked and uncovered, both in heaven and on earth, because there is nothing in her that gives cause for shame or concealment. But self-love brings darkness and sin with it, by which she is blinded and can neither believe nor see the truth; rather, by believing that she possesses it—that is to say, because she believes her false opinion to be the truth—she regards the true truth as an enemy, or as something foreign and unknown.

5. Spiritual self-love <note>German: *geistliche Eigenliebe*. While carnal self-love involves physical appetites, spiritual self-love is the more dangerous tendency to take pride in one's own holiness or religious exercises.</note> is far more dangerous and much more difficult to recognize than carnal self-love. It is a very subtle and piercing poison that very few people escape, because it is even more deeply covered by a thousand subtle pretexts of health, necessity, and sometimes even of love, compassion, and countless other disguises. It makes a person so blind before **GOD** that, although it is the swiftest and most harmful poison, the person not only fails to notice it but even considers it something wholesome. One rejoices over a matter that one should rightfully weep over; and one ought to flee its deceptions with all one’s might, if only one knew what an obstacle this self-love brings to our well-being.

6. This self-love is the root of all misery in this and in the future world. From our father Adam <note>In traditional Christian thought, Adam represents the source of a fallen human nature prone to egoism.</note>, his nature is communicated to us, in which this almost incurable seed of self-love lies enclosed; so that a person’s veins and bones are filled with it in such a way that he can say, think, or do nothing that is not filled with this poisoned love. Indeed, even those thoughts, words, and deeds that are intended to aim for the perfection of the spirit are stained by it. Against such a great sickness, I know of no other remedy than **GOD**, who cleanses us from it through His grace.

7. Now, if this self-love has such power that a person <insert>driven by it</insert> regards neither death nor life, neither Hell nor Heaven; how much incomparably greater power will divine love then have, which is **GOD** Himself? And when it has been poured into our hearts through its immeasurable goodness, it is (contrary to what self-love does) solicitous for our benefit—both of the soul and the body—and even for the benefit of our neighbor, caring for his honor and well-being. It proves itself to be just as it is: namely, gentle, kind, and loving in all things and toward everyone. It denies all self-will and has no other willing than the will of **GOD**, to which it submits in everything. And **GOD** so inflames, cleanses, enlightens, and strengthens this enamored <note>German: *verliebte*. This refers to a soul that is "in love" or completely oriented toward the Divine.</note> will through His incomparable love that it fears nothing more than sin alone.

### Of Saint Catherine of Genoa. Chapter XIII.

->M m<-

8. This divine love, strictly speaking, is our true self-love, because it separates us from the world and from ourselves to unite us with **GOD**. The love of **GOD** is rest, peace, and indeed our true and only life; self-love <note>German: *Eigenliebe*. In this context, it refers to the ego or the selfish attachment to one's own desires rather than God's will.</note>, on the other hand, is nothing other than perpetual pain and sadness—indeed, it is our death, both in this world and in the next.

9. **GOD** is our true and proper love; therefore, love Him who loves you, namely **GOD**, and let go of that which does not love you, namely the love of all other things that are beneath **GOD**. For this false love is an enemy of true love and stands in its way. Oh, if only I could grant the ability to see, to touch, and to feel this truth through an internal "taste," just as I feel it myself! I am certain there would be no creature on earth who would not love this pure love; indeed, it would be such that if the sea (a) were this abyss of divine love, there would be neither man nor woman who would not go and plunge themselves into it. And whoever lived far from the sea would do nothing else but run there to submerge themselves in it as well: for this love is so sweet and charming that all other love, by comparison, is nothing but affliction and sadness. This love makes a person so rich that, outside of it, everything else seems like pure misery. It makes one so light that it seems he no longer feels the earth beneath his feet; and because his loving affection is so far above, he can feel no kind of pain on earth. There, he is so free that he dwells with **GOD** forever without any hindrance. If I am now asked: "What do you feel?" I answer: "I feel what no eye can see and no ear can hear; and of this I bear witness in truth, through the sensation that I have of it according to my capacity, without deceiving myself." But when I look at what I feel, it seems to me a shame that I speak of it with such frail words; for I am certain that everything one can say of **GOD** is neither **GOD** Himself, nor even like Him, but they are only certain small breadcrumbs <note>German: *Brodsämlein*. A reference to the biblical "crumbs that fall from the master's table" (Matthew 15:27).</note> that fall from His table.

10. This holy soul, with her understanding, will, and memory, was so swallowed up in the peaceful sea of her sweet love that she could find almost no suitable words to speak of either divine or external things. Instead, all her conversations consisted only of fervently flaming sighs, which were paired with a withdrawal from her sensuality <note>German: *Sinnlichkeit*. Here meaning the physical senses and worldly perception rather than modern "sensuality."</note>. When she was occasionally forced by necessity to speak of certain things or pay attention to something, she said: She saw things with an outwardly "dead" appearance, but internally they did not penetrate her.

11. She was so often wounded by the arrows of divine love that she became sick from it, and she was treated by physicians as if she had a physical illness.

12. At times she had such a great fire in her heart that, due to such on-

### Tenth Part. The Life

13. To allow the outer man <note>German: *äussern Menschen*. This refers to the physical body and the sensory self, which Catherine felt was overwhelmed by the intensity of her spiritual experiences.</note> to catch a bit of breath, she sometimes went alone into a chamber, laid herself completely outstretched upon the earth, and cried: "Love! Love! I can no longer [endure it]!"

14. Often she went walking in the garden and spoke with the plants and trees, saying: "Are you not then creatures of my **GOD**? Are you not truly obedient to Him?" and many other such words for her relief, so that one could sometimes listen to her for a good while without her knowing it.

15. [Yet she sought no kind of consolations or extraordinary gifts,] but said to her Love at times: "Is it possible, O sweet Love, that one cannot love You without comfort and without hope of any other good, neither in heaven nor on earth?" Another time she said: "O Love! I cannot grasp that one must love anything else but You, and it would be a great pain to me if I were able to grasp such a thing."

16. Because she now thought that other people loved **GOD** just as she did, she could not understand that anyone would have the will to sin; but if she saw someone doing such things that were undeniably sins, she still could not imagine it possible that they had committed them with a deliberate will and in a malicious manner.

17. Concerning her own faults, if someone perhaps said to her: "That is poorly done"; she gave as an answer: "If it is poorly done, then I do not wish to have done it, and I cannot will such a thing, so that it may never be said that true Love allowed the one who loves it to do anything evil."

18. She loved her sweet Love so much, and was in turn loved so powerfully by it, that everything in her proceeded according to the command and order of true Love; therefore she said to her **Lord**: "O Love! If others have one obligation to observe Your commandments, then I wish to have ten obligations to do so; for all Your commandments are entirely sweet, pleasant, and full of love. You command no things that cause any evil; rather, to the one who takes heed of Your commandments, You give a great peace, love, and union with Yourself. Whoever does not experience this cannot understand it."

19. This, her sweet Love, also gave her such confidence that when she was drawn to pray for something that **GOD** wished to grant her, it was said to her in the spirit: "Only command, for Love can do all things." And so she then received everything she asked for, and indeed with such great assurance and certainty that it is not possible to form a conception of it.

# The Fourteenth Chapter.

## On the Annihilation of the Soul and Its Powers, and the Loss of Sensory Perceptions; and of the Transformation into God that Follows.

->1.<-

After this holy soul had obtained the grace from her sweet Love that she had no other rest or pleasure than only the <margin>will of her Beloved</margin> (†), the same sent her so many deprivations, so many mortifications, indeed so many annihilations of herself that it cannot be expressed by any tongue; and for her part, she accepted everything from His divine hand that she encountered from moment to moment.

2. This divine will takes away all imperfection from our will; therefore she said with <margin>an enlightened zeal</margin> (†): "Man! You will find that God wills nothing else than what we also will, and that He regards nothing other than our spiritual benefit; but the coarse and imperfect person cannot recognize these things because of his imperfection. The more we make ourselves uniform with the divine will, the more one leaves imperfection behind and comes closer to perfection; and when one can no longer distance oneself from the divine will, one becomes completely perfect, completely united with God, and completely transformed <note>German: *vergestaltet*. This implies a change of form or transfiguration, where the soul takes on the "shape" of the divine.</note> in Him, and completely gentle and friendly toward one’s neighbor. Oh, how blessed is the soul which, so that it may die to itself, leaves its own will in all things; it then lives entirely for its God, indeed, God Himself lives in it."

3. When man, she said, loses his own will, then God takes his free will, so that He may work through it; He then also allows nothing to rise up in his will except what is pleasing to Him. O you annihilation of the will! You virtue of all virtues: you are a queen of heaven and earth; and just as you are subject to no thing, so you also find nothing that could cause you pain; for all pain and vexation arise only from spiritual or temporal selfhood <note>German: *Eigenheit*. This refers to the egoistic attachment to one's own opinions, desires, or possessions.</note>. Oh, that I could express what I recognize and feel of this noble annihilation of the own will! I am certain that everyone would abhor his own will as much as if it were the devil himself; one would nevermore stand by his own sense or opinion; one would nevermore excuse oneself; one would nevermore want to have anything of one’s own, and nevermore say of any thing, whatever it might be: 'This belongs to me.'

4. A humbled understanding sees, understands, tastes, and feels this great mystery, and soon comes <margin>home; (namely, to divine union</margin> (†)

union) but (†) an intellect without wisdom (that is, without flavorful and certain knowledge <note>The German *schmackhafte* (flavorful/tasty) refers to "sapiential" knowledge—from the Latin *sapere*, meaning both "to taste" and "to be wise." To a humbled intellect, GOD gives a supernatural light, through which it sees far more and higher things than it could see before; it also sees them with greater certainty and clarity, without having any doubt about them, and without needing to struggle to distinguish them; it sees them not bit by bit, but in an instant. In this new light (†), which is above the intellect itself, it is given to know everything that GOD wills for it to know.

5. Whoever does not lose his natural intellect cannot obtain this supernatural light; for when our natural intellect tries to seek it, our own imperfection accompanies it. GOD lets it seek as long as it can, until He finally leads it to the recognition of its own imperfection; once this is well recognized, GOD gives us this supernatural light, which casts the intellect down to the earth. When it is thus cast down, it no longer seeks anything in itself, but speaks to GOD: "You are my intellect, and I wish to know nothing more than what You want me to know; I will no longer trouble myself to seek anything, but I will remain in peace and quiet with Your intellect, by which my spirit is entirely possessed."

6. A humbled intellect is quickly enlightened.

7. Regarding the memory, she said she could keep nothing in it except for as long as the present moment lasted in which she thought of it. If something was said to her, she had forgotten it again the next moment; and if she perhaps said, "we want to perform this or that," it likewise escaped her memory immediately, especially where it concerned only external matters. But in what was necessary, GOD—who reminds such a soul at the proper time and place—took care of what she had to do, just as if the soul had someone who spoke it into her ear from moment to moment.

8. Which GOD does for this reason, leaving neither good nor evil to stick in the memory, so that the spirit has no hindrance from it. But instead of memory and intellect, GOD gives the soul a certain inner occupation, in which He keeps her so immersed that it seems to her as if she were drowned in a deep sea; since she is then occupied in such a great and divine matter, she can no longer exercise her natural functions; instead, she remains annihilated and sunken in this sea, and receives such a great communication of Divine Stillness <note>German: *Göttliche Stille*. This refers to the "Quiet" sought by mystics, a state of profound peace where the soul rests entirely in God’s presence.</note> that it would be enough to soothe the sufferings of Hell.

9. When the soul, through divine operation, finds itself annihilated <note>In the tradition of Christian mysticism, "annihilation" refers to the total surrender of the ego and self-will, allowing the soul to be filled entirely by God.</note>, it remains completely transfigured in God, who leads and moves it in all things, and fills it in His own way, without any human effort. And who can imagine what this creature then feels? If she were able to speak of it, her words would be so boiling hot that hearts as hard as stone would be set on fire. In this annihilation, she recognizes that all self-will is pain; all understanding is vexation; all memory is a hindrance; and she cries out only: O love of poverty! O kingdom of silence!

10. Now that the annihilation of the soul has taken place, the power and the effect of physical sensations are lost in the following manner: such a soul can no longer see anything on earth that might cause it pleasure or pain; even if she should see such things, she neither rejoices nor grieves over them. Because the soul is transfigured in God, He does not permit her to take part in physical sensations; instead, He gradually lets them all die within her without any pity. And so, even when this soul looks at something, she can no longer grasp it with physical "taste," <note>This refers to the "sensory appetite" or the ability to find worldly satisfaction in objects.</note> nor can she explain the nature of things that please other people. When she hears it said, "This is beautiful," or "This is good," she cannot comprehend what kind of beauty or goodness is supposed to be found therein. And it is exactly the same with all the other senses and perceptions of such a soul.

11. [Speaking of annihilation and transfiguration in God, she says:] If you (a) lived only so that you might reach your end <note>The "End" here refers to the final purpose of human existence: union with God.</note> once again, you would not respect your own being, but would say: "Quickly, quickly, pull me out of my own being, and place me into the fulfillment of my purpose, for which I was created." 
<note>(a) Actually, she says this regarding bread, which a person eats and transforms into his own nature, as a simile for spiritual annihilation.</note>

12. This is how God deals with man, who is created for eternal life, for the purpose of being united with God and transfigured in Him. He would have easily reached this state before the Fall of Man, as he was then so pure in soul and body that there was nothing misshapen or superfluous in him—nothing to be restored or separated—whereas after the Fall, there is much of that. Thus, just as there are two parts in bread—one that becomes substance, and the other which is cast out as something superfluous—so too does God separate and cast away from man all his evil inclinations, which were corrupted through Original Sin. This Original Sin gives man such a strong inclination toward all evil that, without the grace and working of God, we can neither overcome it nor even recognize its wickedness; instead, we would remain forever blind and incurable. Therefore it happens that the soul, recognizing its dangerous sickness, speaks thus: "I know no other medicine to find, than that I [unite] myself with..."

But instead of memory and understanding, **GOD** gives the soul a certain inner occupation in which He keeps her so immersed that it seems to her as if she were drowned in a deep sea; since she is then occupied in such a great and divine matter, she can no longer exercise her natural functions; instead, she remains annihilated and submerged in this sea, and receives so great a communication of Divine Stillness <term>Stille: a technical term in German mysticism referring to 'Quietism' or the 'Prayer of Quiet,' where the soul is wordlessly still before God</term> that it would be sufficient to soothe the sufferings of Hell.

# Of Saint Catherine of Genoa. Chapter XIV.
### M m 3
<meta>catchword: „Body</meta>

9. When the soul finds itself annihilated <term>annihilated: *Vernichtigung*, a mystical term for the process of emptying the self and the ego so that God may act without human interference</term> through the divine operation, it remains entirely transformed in **GOD**, who leads and moves it in all things, and fills it in His own way, without any human effort. And who can imagine what this creature then experiences? If it could speak of it, its words would be so boiling hot that hearts as hard as stone would be set on fire. In this annihilation, the soul recognizes that all self-will is pain; all intellect is annoyance; all memory is a hindrance; and it only cries out: **O Love of Poverty! O Kingdom of Stillness!**

10. Now that the annihilation of the soul has taken place, the power and effect of physical sensations is lost in the following manner: Such a soul can no longer see anything on earth that might cause it pleasure or pain; should it see such a thing, it is neither gladdened nor saddened by it. Because the soul is transformed in **GOD**, He does not allow it to take part in physical sensations; instead, He lets them all gradually die within the soul without any pity. Thus, even when this soul looks upon a thing, it can no longer grasp it with physical taste, nor can it explain the nature of things that please other people. When it hears it said, "this is beautiful" or "this is good," it cannot comprehend what kind of beauty or goodness is supposed to be found there. And it is exactly the same with all the other senses and feelings of such a soul.

11. [Speaking of the annihilation and transformation in **GOD**, she says:] If you (a) live only for the purpose of reaching your end <note>The "end" here refers to the final goal or purpose of human existence: union with God.</note>, then you will not regard your own being, but say: Quickly, quickly, draw me out of my own being and place me into the fulfillment of my purpose, for which I was created.

12. Thus **GOD** deals with man, who is created for eternal life, to the end that he might be united with **GOD** and transformed in Him. This would have been easily achieved before the Fall <note>The "Fall" refers to the biblical narrative of Adam and Eve’s original sin in Eden.</note>, when man was so pure in soul and body that there was nothing misshapen or superfluous, nothing to be restored or separated within him, as there is so much of now after the Fall. Therefore, just as there are two parts in bread—one that becomes substance and another that is cast out as superfluous—so also **GOD** separates and casts away from man all his evil inclinations. These have been corrupted through original sin, which gives man such a strong inclination toward all evil that, without the grace and operation of **GOD**, we could neither overcome it nor recognize its malice; rather, we would always remain blind and incurable. Therefore it happens that the soul, recognizing its dangerous disease, speaks thus: "I know no other remedy to find, except that I with..."

# Tenth Part. The Life

> “Body and soul, and with all that I have and what I can have, I sacrifice and give to **GOD**, so that He may take me into His treatment <note>original: *Cur*, referring to a medical course of healing or a "cure"</note>, and deal with me just as I do with the bread; of which my nature, after I have eaten it, retains only the good substance and throws the rest away.”

13. Certainly, if **GOD** did not wonderfully perform this in us through His sweet means, our own part would never allow itself to be annihilated <term>annihilated: *vernichtigen*, the mystical process of emptying the ego to make room for God</term>; instead, it would defend itself as long as it possibly could, however evil it may be. But when it finds itself under the guidance of **GOD**, He cuts and hews away all the roots of the tree. Once **GOD** has taken this care upon Himself, He consumes, kills, and extinguishes the soul’s evil inclinations in the following manner: He keeps the soul so gathered and occupied in Him that the body is left behind and remains without any pleasure; the soul, remaining firm in its gathering and peace, no longer takes notice of the body except for the most extreme necessities. And while **GOD** holds this blessed creature <term>creature: the human being as a created thing in relation to the Creator</term> in this state for a time, He consumes all its evil inclinations until finally the soul makes the body completely subject to itself; then they make peace with one another.

14. But you will object that the body will have much to endure before one can arrive at that state, and that it is to be wished that this path were not so desolate and difficult. But this is not possible; it is exactly as if one were to cut off the roots of a tree and yet wish that the tree should not wither. And just as the body dies when the soul is separated from it, so too, when the soul's effects are withdrawn from earthly things and the body, the body remains like a bird without feathers that wishes to fly—indeed, even more insensitive.

15. Just as we said before that nature retains one part of the bread it eats and throws the other part away, so the soul, through the operation of **GOD**, throws away from the body all excess and all evil habits acquired through sin, and retains within itself only the purified body, which thereafter acts through its purified senses. The more the soul increases in the spiritual life, the more the body loses its natural functions. And because spiritual foods provide it with no nourishment, the body must say: *It would be much better for me to be dead; for although I cannot live on spiritual things, I must nevertheless endure and bear this divine operation, which grows and oppresses me so much that death would be a pleasant relief to me.* Besides this, I am now and then overwhelmed with certain divine and so piercing rays that it is a miracle that I am still alive. and yet I must remain in this distress <note>original: *Beklemmung*, a feeling of spiritual or physical constriction and anxiety</note>, without being able to speak either to **GOD** or to creatures; and even when I have (†) <note>This symbol likely refers to a missing marginal note or a specific textual reference in the original manuscript</note> much to do outwardly, my hands and feet often sink away in weakness, and I go about only as one always complaining: *I can do no more!* In short, I am so distressed and oppressed that if I were still able to weep, I would gladly do so out of sorrow.

16. Now, after the soul has in this way consumed all the evil inclinations of the body through **GOD’s** grace—which body then returns to that original purity <note>original: *anfänglichen Reinigkeit*</note> in which our first father Adam was created, and without which we cannot be presented before our Creator—**GOD** consequently also consumes all the imperfections of the soul. He makes the soul more and more capable of recognizing His workings, both in regard to itself and in regard to the whole world; and as the soul daily sees these workings as ever greater, the understanding also receives more knowledge, the memory is filled, and the will is ignited in love. And because the understanding can, to some extent, grasp **GOD’s** work, the tongue can also, to some extent, speak of it, though not fully; for the understanding can perceive far more than the tongue can express. Nevertheless, because of the abundance of this knowledge and the sensation which **GOD** pours into the soul, the tongue cannot remain silent, even though it cannot say what it would wish; and then, one who has not cast off his own evil nature and (†) inclinations toward himself, and is not enlightened from above, cannot grasp what this tongue speaks.

17. Now, when **GOD** wishes to transform a soul into Himself—as was said above regarding the bread—He knows how to order and arrange the powers of the soul <term>powers of the soul: *Seelenkräfte*, referring to the traditional three faculties: Understanding, Memory, and Will</term> until He draws them out of their own workings. This is done so that the understanding can no longer grasp, the memory no longer retain, and the will no longer desire; even while, in the meantime, all these soul-powers together grasp something so great that it exceeds their capacity. Yet, little remains for the soul of what it grasps; for as **GOD** increases His working in this soul, He consumes the act of understanding and grasping, and thus casts out all the workings by which the soul might want to claim any spiritual thing for itself, whether for its own sake or for someone else, because otherwise it would not be pure and clear in His presence.

18. When the soul is then stripped <note>original: *entblösset*, meaning made naked or empty of self-will</note> of its own workings, **GOD** pours even more sublime gifts and graces into the interior, which never fail it but rather increase and multiply without ceasing. This is something that never moves or wavers, and through which one remains always in **GOD**, with an infusion of a pure, clear, and simple love. Through this, one henceforth loves **GOD** Himself without (a) cause and without a "why," which is also the true way in which **GOD** must be loved. And so the whole human being remains annihilated <term>annihilated: *vernichtiget*, the mystical state of being "naughted" so God can act fully through the person</term>, internally and externally, and can say with Paul:
> I live, yet no longer I, but Christ lives in me. <note>original: *Ich lebe, doch nicht mehr ich, sondern Christus lebet in mir* (Galatians 2:20)</note>

19. How then should such a soul not be able to say, with this very same Apostle:
> Who shall separate me from the love of **GOD**? <note>original: *Wer wird mich scheiden von der Liebe GOttes?* (Romans 8:35)</note>
And many other fervent, enamored, and bold words, which are nevertheless all as nothing in view of the infinite power of this love with which one is united. Since such a soul [desires] nothing

# The Fifteenth Chapter.
## Her perfect detachment, or inner and outer estrangement. Concerning the return into **GOD**, and the power of her Pure Love.

->I.<-

Those who did not understand the matters and workings of the spirit were unable to recognize this soul, even though they associated with her often. They judged and spoke of her as they would of themselves or of other people; when they saw that she made use of her senses, laughed at times, and otherwise behaved outwardly—as they thought—just like other humans. But they did not know the inner condition of her mind, nor the flavor <note>original: *Geschmack*; referring to the spiritual quality or "relish" that accompanies an action.</note> given to her sensory actions by it. It was also difficult to comprehend that within the interior of these holy souls there was so strong a wall that even if all the pleasures of the world, the flesh, and of creatures had been like sheer cannon fire or more piercing than lightning, they could not have moved the smallest stone of this wall from its place. Therefore it happened that she wondered how it was possible for people to take pleasure in anything that was below **GOD**, since she well knew that no true pleasure is to be found except in **GOD** alone.

She lived in the flesh without acting through the flesh; she dwelt in the world and did not know the world; she lived among men and did not know who they were; and when she heard them speak of things other than what she experienced in her inner self, she marveled greatly at it—especially when they spoke of such things with love and pleasure, which she could not comprehend at all.

4.
