[I, (a) who have written this, remind the reader here once and for all that in all these steps I have mentioned nothing in particular of her wonderful acts of penance, as I learned of them later; for she revealed to me only what was necessary to distinguish the steps of her penance; but I also did not want to put down one word more than she said; indeed, I have had to omit much. <note>The scribe, Brother Arnold, here inserts his own voice to explain his editorial process, emphasizing his commitment to accuracy over sensationalism.</note>]

V. The fifth step is self-knowledge; for since I had now been somewhat enlightened, I saw nothing in me but defects; I condemned myself, knowing for certain that I had deserved hell; and there I fell once more into bitter weeping and lamenting. Moreover, one must know that a considerable time always passed before I moved from one of these steps to the next. [It is therefore a great grief of heart and misery for a soul that it moves so sluggishly and goes toward God in no other way than with pain and a great burden, and progresses so slowly in it.] I had to remain there as if in weeping, and nothing else was yet given to me; for although it was a comfort to me that I could weep, it was nevertheless a bitter comfort.

Eleventh Part. The Life

# The First Chapter.
### An account of the origin of Angela, of the author of her biography, and of the first nine steps of her conversion.

->1.<-

This holy Italian woman, Angela of Foligno, is named after the place of her birth, Foligno, in the Duchy of Spoleto; where she lived at the end of the thirteenth century. At the beginning of her conversion, she still had a husband and many children, who all died one after another; after which she entered the Third Order of St. Francis <term>Third Order of St. Francis: A branch of the Franciscan order for laypeople who wish to live according to the spirit of St. Francis while remaining in the world.</term> and concluded her holy life in 1309. Little is known of her outward circumstances, but her inner form and guidance—which is our primary concern here—were mostly written down from her own mouth (as we have already seen in the preface) by her confessor, a Friar Minor <term>Friar Minor: A member of the Order of Friars Minor (Franciscans), founded by St. Francis of Assisi.</term> named Arnold. He compiled these accounts, along with her own letters, into a book, which he begins as follows:

<margin>(a) M. 8. (b) John 14:23.</margin>
[(a) Just as God allows His believers to truly taste, see, and touch through experience the Word of Life that became flesh] as He Himself spoke in the Gospel: Whoever (b) loves Me will keep My word, and My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our dwelling with him; and again: Whoever loves Me, to him I will reveal Myself. Thus God has recently given testimony of this experiential teaching through one of His believers, namely the blessed Angela of Foligno.

In the name of the most holy Trinity, I, an unworthy brother, then begin to describe what I was able to obtain from the mouth of this blessed woman with great effort and many prayers, even though I was very close to her and closely united in the love of Jesus. For she was very reserved and secretive regarding the gifts of God, so much so that perhaps nothing would ever have been obtained from her, had she not been moved to it by compassion when she saw my sadness because we suddenly had to be so far from each other, and it was uncertain whether I would ever see her physical face again. However, she was also at the same time entirely compelled by God to tell me these things, just as I, an unworthy scribe, also believe that I was urged by God to describe them.

<margin>(c) In an excessive alteration of the mind. <note>original: "In excessiva mentis alteratione." This phrase describes a state of spiritual ecstasy or an out-of-body experience common in mystical literature.</note></margin>

<meta>This page continues the autobiographical account of Angela of Foligno’s spiritual conversion, picking up from the fifth and sixth steps of her journey. Having previously described her initial confession and the recognition of divine mercy, she now moves into the deeper, more painful stages of her purgation and the stripping away of her worldly life.</meta>

Eleventh Piece. The Life

I received a deep knowledge of all my sins. I saw that I had offended all creatures who were created for me. All my sins came vividly into my memory, and they appeared significant to me as I confessed them before **God**. I begged the creatures who had been offended by me that they might not accuse me before **God**; it seemed to me they all had compassion for me. Then it was granted to me that I could pray with great fervor of love <note>original: *Liebesbrunst*. This term describes an intense, burning spiritual passion or "heat" common in mystical literature.</note>.

VII. Seventhly, it was granted to me that I looked upon the cross of **Jesus Christ**. There I saw how Christ had died for us; this vision was nonetheless without "taste" <note>original: *Geschmack*. In mystical theology, "taste" refers to spiritual sweetness or emotional consolation. Angela is noting that while she understood the truth of the Crucifixion, she did not yet feel the comforting "sweetness" often associated with divine presence.</note>, although not without great pain.

VIII. Eighthly, upon looking at the cross, an even greater knowledge was given to me of how the Son of **God** had died for our sins. And right there, I recognized all my sins with the greatest pain; I felt that it was I who had crucified Him. In this knowledge of the cross, such a great fire was communicated to me that, standing before the cross, I divested myself of all things and sacrificed myself entirely to the **Lord**. I promised Him—though not without fear—a perpetual chastity of my limbs and my senses, and begged Him for the grace to be able to keep this promise of mine; for on the one hand, I was afraid to make such a promise, but on the other hand, I was so driven to this promise by the aforementioned fire that I could not refrain from it.

IX. Ninthly, I felt a desire to seek out the Way of the Cross, so that I might sit down at the foot of the cross, where all sinners take refuge. And I received light and instruction, through which the Way of the Cross was shown to me. And it was whispered to me that if I wanted to go to the cross, I must strip myself of all things <note>original: *entblössen*. This refers to "spiritual nakedness," the total detachment from worldly possessions, status, and emotional ties.</note> so that I would be much lighter, and thus I should go to the cross naked. This stripping consisted of my having to forgive all who had offended me; that I must divest myself of all things on earth—of all men, all women, all friends, all relatives, and all others—as well as my goods, and finally of myself; I had to give my heart to Christ, who had shown me the aforementioned benefits, and should follow Him through the thorny path of tribulations.

From that time on, I gave up my costly fabrics, beautiful clothes, delicious foods, and my headdress. I did this, however, not without some shame and pain, for I had as yet experienced little sensitivity of love, and my husband was also still alive. Therefore, when I was treated unfairly or spoken to harshly, I felt it painfully; nevertheless, I bore it as well as I could.

Around this time it happened, according to **God’s** will, that my mother died, who was a great hindrance to me; after that my husband also died, as did all my children in a short time, one after another <note>To a modern reader, Angela’s reaction to her family's death seems jarring. In the context of 13th-century Franciscan mysticism, however, the death of her family was viewed as a "bitter mercy" that removed the final obstacles—her worldly duties as a wife and mother—to her total union with God.</note>. Their deaths were a great comfort to me, and I thought (after **God** had shown me the above) that from now on my heart must always be in **God’s** heart, and **God’s** heart must always be in my heart.

## The Second Chapter.

### Of the remaining nine steps of her conversion.

<margin>X.</margin> Tenthly, as I prayed to GOD, asking how I might do what was most pleasing to Him? Then He appeared to me in His kindness, both while I was awake and while I was sleeping, hanging upon the Cross. He told me: I should look upon His wounds; and He showed me in a wonderful way, and indeed at several different times, how He had suffered everything for me. And as He showed me everything particularly, piece by piece, what He had suffered for me, He said to me: *What then could you ever do for me that would be comparable to this?* He showed me His wounds and pains from His head to His feet, and how the hair had been torn from His head and beard; He showed me all His scourgings, and said: *All of this I have suffered for you.* As He said this, all my sins were brought to my memory, and it was shown to me how I had crucified the Lord JESUS anew through them; therefore I rightly had to have a greater sorrow over them than ever before, just as I truly wept for them with greater pain than ever.

During the time that He showed me His suffering, He constantly repeated these words: *What could you then do for me that would be sufficient?* At this I dissolved, as it were, into tears; indeed, I wept so bitterly and so much that the flesh of my face became like it was cooked <note>original: *gekocht*. This vivid description suggests her skin was raw, red, and swollen from the salt and heat of her intense weeping.</note> from the many tears.

XI. Eleventhly, as I recognized my sin in this manner, I gave myself over to an even more severe practice of penance <term>penance: voluntary self-punishment as an expression of repentance for sin</term>, about which I need not speak in detail. <insert>Of this step, says the scribe, there would be much to report; her practice of penance was wonderful and exceedingly severe, as is sufficiently known to me.</insert>

XII. Twelfthly, as it seemed to me that, burdened as I was with the things of this world, I would not be able to perform true penance or reach the Cross: I resolved to give up everything altogether. This resolution was given to my soul by GOD through His grace in the following manner.

I had such a vehement desire to become poor that I also often thought with much earnestness and fear whether I might perhaps die before I had become poor; on the other hand, I was simultaneously attacked by heavy temptations—that I was still so young, that going begging was dangerous and shameful for me, and that I might yet have to die of hunger, frost, and nakedness <note>original: *Blöſſe*. While it literally means nakedness, in this context it refers to the destitution of having no clothing or shelter to protect against the elements.</note>: additionally, my intention was discouraged by everyone who knew me.

But GOD finally took pity on me and gave me a living and great light in my heart, and indeed with such great certainty that I do not believe I shall lose it in eternity. By this light, I had soon made the complete conclusion that even if I knew for certain that I would die of hunger,

<margin>XVI.</margin> The sixteenth step <note>The "steps" (Staffel) refer to the thirty stages of Angela's conversion and spiritual ascent, a common metaphor in medieval mystical literature similar to a ladder to heaven.</note> was this: As I was once in a church, praying to GOD that He might show me some grace, and to that end was speaking the Lord's Prayer <note>The "Our Father" or *Pater Noster*.</note>, the LORD impressed the same into my heart with such great clarity, and with such great knowledge of His divine goodness and my own unworthiness, that it is impossible for me to express it. GOD explained to me every word of this prayer as I spoke it, which happened very slowly, and with much contrition and self-knowledge; so much so that although on one side I dissolved into tears because of my unworthiness and sins, I nevertheless received, on the other side, a great consolation. From then on, I began to taste something of the divine sweetness; for I discovered His divine goodness much more clearly in this prayer than in any other thing, as I still find it to be so even now. But because my sins and unworthiness were placed before my eyes at the same time, I fell into such great shame that I did not dare to lift my eyes.

> O you sinners! O, if you only knew how difficult it is for a soul to progress on the true way of penance! What strong bonds do not hold her back? What evil helpers does she not have in the world, the flesh, and Satan?

<margin>XVII.</margin> In the seventeenth step, a completely different faith was given to me than I had held until then, which appeared to me like a dead faith in comparison with this one; also, my previous tears seemed small and as if forced, in comparison with those which I now shed. From that same time on, everything I did, however great and laborious it might be, seemed to me to be very little and insignificant, and I had a firm will to undertake even greater exercises of penance. At that time, I enclosed my heart, as it were, in the sufferings of JESUS Christ; and hope was given to me that I would be redeemed through the same. I also began to have beautiful and comforting dreams—indeed, I continually felt divine sweetness, both while awake and while sleeping; but because I did not yet have full certainty in this, it was all still mixed with bitterness: my soul wanted something else from GOD.

<margin>XVIII.</margin> In the eighteenth step, I finally had great divine sensations, and I felt such great delights in prayer that I even forgot to eat because of them. I wished I had no further need to eat, so that I might have been able to remain in prayer at all times; yet some temptation mixed itself therein, namely, that I should eat either nothing at all, or far too little; but I soon noticed that this was a deception <note>In mystical theology, "deception" often refers to a trick by the devil to ruin a person's health through excessive, prideful fasting.</note>. I had such a great fire of love in my heart that I did not become weary, neither through frequent kneeling nor through any exercise of penance. 3. The suffering and torment of my soul is incomparably greater and more cruel. I see that the evil spirits place my soul in such a state where, like one who is hanged, I can no longer have the slightest support; even (a) the virtues that one previously possessed all vanish, and are destroyed and overturned before the soul's eyes. When the soul sees this and finds it cannot resist, it falls into such desperate pain and vexation that, out of dejection, I can sometimes hardly even weep; or if I do weep, it brings me not the slightest relief. Sometimes such raging forces of anger overcome me that I can hardly restrain myself from tearing myself apart; sometimes I cannot restrain myself at all, so that I strike myself hideously, such that my head and other limbs of my body are full of welts <note>original: "Beulen"; referring to bruises or swellings from self-inflicted blows</note>. 7\. At times, a certain vice attacks me inwardly, which has never been in me before, but which enters into me by God’s permission. This vice is more abominable than all other vices might be. This virtue or power then remains always, while the vice diminishes; this power holds me fast and does not let me fall into sin. Indeed, this virtue does not only hold me, but it has such power that it makes me thoroughly virtuous, and I truly recognize therein that God is present. I am so enlightened and strengthened by it that all the people of the whole world, and all the devils of hell, would not move me to the slightest sin, for here I retain a certain faith in God. Yet that vice is so loathsome that I dare not even name it; and so violent that if the aforementioned power or virtue is hidden from me and seems to forsake me, there is nothing in the whole world, neither shame nor pain, that would be able to hold me back from falling into that same sin. But as soon as the aforementioned power appears, it delivers me so completely that all the goods and all the sufferings of this world, as it seems to me, could move me to no sin.

8\. I am attacked in my soul by a certain false humility, and then also by a very terrifying pride <note>original: "Hochmuth"; an arrogant or haughty spirit</note>. This false humility consists in me seeing myself as fallen away from all good, from all virtue, and from all grace; and I see myself so filled with sins and defects that I can no longer believe that God will henceforth have mercy on me; I see myself as a dwelling of the devil, as his female collaborator <note>original: "Mitwirkerinn"</note> who believes the devil's deceits; I see myself as his daughter, and as one who no longer has any sincerity or virtue, and is worthy to sit in the lowest place in the abyss of hell.

9\. When I am attacked by it in my inner being, it seems to me as if I am surrounded by devils; I see nothing other than sins and defects in my soul and in my body. God is then to me, so...

More than once I have testified that if I were permitted to choose, I would rather have taken all kinds of misery, torment, and martyrdom upon myself than the sufferings of this state, which lasted for over two years.

<meta>This page continues the spiritual reflections of Angela of Foligno, shifting from her personal despair to a broader theological explanation of why God permits spiritual trials. It follows her "confession" where she felt like a hypocrite and an "idol," now interpreting those painful experiences as a necessary refining process.</meta>

# Angela of Foligno. Chapter III.

...is a very great purification of souls. Through this, I attain true humility, without which no one will be saved. The greater the humility, the greater the purity of the souls. I see that these temptations of the souls are fiery flames, through which the soul is purified and martyred as if in a furnace. The knowledge of one's sins and failings, which is obtained thereby, purifies the soul from all pride and frees it from the power of the devils. Therefore, the more a soul is plagued, humbled, impoverished, and brought low, the more it is purified and made capable of being elevated by God to the highest states <note>The "states" or "ranks" (Stände) refer to levels of spiritual perfection or intimacy with the Divine.</note>. No soul can be elevated by any other way or means than according to the measure it has been humbled and established in humility.

15. [Thus this practiced warrior of Jesus Christ had rightly learned from experience when she gave her spiritual children the following reminder:] My <margin>(a) This and the following paragraph are from our manuscript.</margin> dear children, I write to you that which has now been newly impressed upon my heart: namely, that man must also be punished again through the very same vice by which he offended God. First, concerning pride—which vice is a root of all evil—it happens that when the soul is humbled by divine grace, it seeks with all its strength to drive pride out of itself; and when the soul is born again of God, it becomes humble and desires with all its heart to be without pride. Nevertheless, pride indeed enters the soul without the soul willing it. But if pride comes and the soul takes pleasure or delight in it, then it becomes guilty; however, if this vice stirs without the soul taking pleasure, and it is rather bitterly distressed by it, then the soul stands firm in the seat of truth, wherein the soul is incapable of pride. But because it previously harbored this vice with its consent, the same now returns against its consent as a punishment for the former. Therefore, my dear children, be brave and strengthen yourselves, for God will punish your faults through faults <note>A paradoxical idea that the lingering impulse to sin acts as a refining punishment for past willful sins.</note>.

16. So it also goes with the vice of avarice <term>avarice (Geiz): specifically referring here to spiritual greed or a lack of generosity with divine gifts</term>; for when the soul gets to see the divine abundance, it becomes generous. Nevertheless, it is afterwards provoked by this very vice, as a punishment for what it previously deserved. So it also happens in regard to carnal lust, where not only those are punished who have fallen into what are properly called works of the flesh, but also those who, through their own negligence, have fallen into subtle carnal thoughts. Therefore, my dear children, do not wonder if we are punished through temptations; for upon every guilt, punishment necessarily follows. Do you not see how man cannot ward off [the attack] of vain glory and hypocrisy? And such happens either because of past guilt, or else for the greater <margin>(b) For the merit of the soul <note>original: "Propter meritum animæ"</note></margin> glorification of the soul. But let it happen from whatever cause it will, let it be enough for us if we only remain conquerors.]

## Chapter Four.

### The first revelation of God granted to Angela: God assures her that He wishes to come and dwell within her; He caresses her extraordinarily; He possesses her and holds the powers of her soul bound. God has few lovers, despite how heartily He loves them; He is Love itself and demands only love; He reveals Himself to her as the Highest Good.

->I.<-

Not long after the time when I was occasionally forced to cry out loudly—which I spoke of regarding the final stage of my conversion—and after the wonderful enlightenment I attained during the Lord’s Prayer, I received a very great consolation of the sweetness of God in the following manner:

2. Specifically, I was drawn to the contemplation of the divinity and humanity of Jesus Christ, and the union of these two in His person. This contemplation was so delightful to me and gave me such great comfort as I had never experienced until then. I was alone in my chamber at prayer, standing upright almost the whole day, and appearing as if outside of myself. But the divine delights enraptured my heart so intensely that I finally had to lie down and lost the power of speech; my female companion <note>Angela was often accompanied by a lay sister or companion after becoming a Franciscan tertiary.</note> came in just then and thought I was dying, but her presence was only a burden and a hindrance to me.

<margin>(a) Johann Arndt, *True Christianity*, Book II, Chapter 27, Section 2.</margin>
3. Another time (shortly before I had distributed all my goods to the poor and had only a little left for myself), I was at prayer one evening. As it then seemed to me that I had no taste or feeling of God at all, I began to complain and spoke to God:

> "You know well, my God, that everything I do in the abandonment of all things, I do only so that I may find You; so let me find You once I have carried this out."

As I said this and much else of the kind, I was answered:

> "What do you wish to have then?"

"Lord," I replied, "I desire neither gold nor silver, even if You were to give me the whole (a) world; I desire nothing but You alone." Then I received the answer:

> "Only take care that you soon carry out what you have intended; for when you have completed it, the entire Holy Trinity <note>The Christian doctrine of God as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.</note> will come into you."

4. After this, when I had set out on the way to Assisi <note>Assisi was the home of St. Francis; Angela was a member of the Third Order of St. Francis and frequently made pilgrimages there.</note>, the Lord fulfilled His promises to me, and the following was said to me:

> "I am the Holy Spirit, who comes to you to give you a comfort such as you have not yet had. I will be in you and accompany you to Assisi,"

After this, I perceived a certain entirely divine and entirely unspeakable fragrance; I also perceived so many other high things that, because I find no words to express myself, I must either speak of them briefly or remain silent altogether about the unspeakable sweetnesses I have tasted.

### Angela of Foligno. Chapter V.

...nor end; I did not see the tablet <note>The "tablet" (*Tafel*) is a metaphorical image common in medieval mysticism, representing a divine record or a surface upon which God's truths are revealed to the soul.</note> itself, but only what was on it. 9. 10. One day (these are the words of the **author** <note>The "author" refers to Brother Arnald, Angela’s confessor and relative, who transcribed her oral accounts into Latin. Since you could well have made it so that we were without all of this, yet still pleasing to you, and that we would have attained the same virtues that we can now have after all this has happened?"

And the like. My soul could then well comprehend that in truth it was as I thought, namely that **God** could well have made us virtuous and blessed without all this: indeed, I was, as it seemed to me, as if compelled and powerfully moved that I must think of these things and ask **God** about them; for I was just in prayer, with the intention not to distract myself from it, no matter what it might be, yet it seemed that I was led to this by **God**. And I presented this question to him for several days, yet without, as said, doubting in the least. And it was given to me to understand that **God** had so ordered and permitted it, both so that He might in such a way much better reveal his divine goodness to us, as also because such was best suited for us. This, however, was still not enough for me for a full understanding of what I asked.

11. So it happened another time, as my soul was drawn up, that I was given to see how that which I asked about had neither beginning nor end. My soul saw that it had entered as if into darknesses which surrounded it on all sides; it wanted to retreat from them back to itself, but it could not; and as it wanted to go further, so was it also...

# Eleventh Part. The Life of

->Angela of Foligno<-

...nor was it possible. Thereupon the soul was suddenly elevated higher and enlightened, and she saw the unspeakable power of **God**, His will, His justice, and His goodness, in which my soul fully and with certainty understood all that I had asked about, and there my soul was immediately pulled out of all the darknesses in which I had previously found myself. For this reason, as long as I was in the darkness, I had to lie stretched out upon the earth; but when that great illumination came, I stood upright on my feet—indeed, I touched the earth only with the very tips of my big toes—I * found myself in such great joy and nimbleness <note>The German *Hurtigkeit* implies a spiritual and physical lightness or agility often reported in ecstatic states.</note> of body, in such fresh health and renewal, the likes of which I had never had before. I was in such a great fullness of divine * clarity, that in this vision of the power, the will, and the justice of **God**, I recognized with the greatest joy and unspeakable peace not only the resolution of what I had asked; but I also recognized with a complete tranquility everything concerning all creatures: those who are blessed, and those who shall be blessed, as well as the damned, the devils, and whatever else belongs there. But I can make this understood with no words at all; for these things are entirely beyond our nature.

12. From this time on, I am and remain so content and immovably calm in all things that even if I knew for certain that I were to be damned, I could not grieve over it in the least, but would approve of **God’s** judgment without any unrest, and would no less apply myself to doing good, to praying, and to glorifying **God**; and there remains in my soul such a great peace, rest, and thorough stability, the likes of which I can never remember having had in such fullness, and in this I remained constantly.

13. After this, when I had seen the power, the will, and the justice of **God**, then my soul was enraptured and elevated even higher, as it seemed to me; and then I no longer saw either the power or the will of **God** in the manner as before, but I saw an *Intelligent Being* <note>original: *Verständiges Wesen*. This refers to a pure, intellectual perception of God’s essence rather than a sensory or emotional vision.</note>, so unspeakable that I can say nothing more of it than that it was *All Good*; my soul was in an unspeakable joy because of it. I did not see Love there, but only this completely unspeakable Being; I do not know whether I stood upright during the time I was in this very high state, nor do I know whether I was in the body or out of the body. All states in which I had been before seemed to me to be nowhere near as elevated as this one, which placed me in a complete mortification <note>original: *Ertödtung*. In mystical theology, this is the "dying" to one's own ego and vices to allow God to act within the soul.</note> of all vices, and in a certain possession of all virtues, and in such an inner condition that I love both what good and what evil happens to me, regarding which I also feel no more displeasure or disturbance.

14. This divine vision placed me in a great peace and reverence before **God’s** judgments; so that * when I am accustomed to say in prayer in the morning or the evening:

> Through your birth deliver me, dear **LORD**! Through your suffering deliver me!

I am almost most refreshed when I say:

> Through your holy judgments deliver me, dear **LORD**!

This I say in confidence; for I no longer recognize the goodness of **God** only in one who is blessed and holy, and in many saints—

## The Sixth Chapter.

**God reveals Himself to her as Love, as well as Light; then in the darkness as the Supreme Good; and afterwards, in even greater darkness, how this Supreme Good is the Holy Trinity.**

->I.<-

It happened once during Lent that it seemed to me I was quite in a dryness of the spirit <note>A common mystical term (*Dürre des Gemüths*) referring to "spiritual aridity," a state where one feels distant from God and unable to pray.</note> and without any devotion; then I prayed to **God** that He might give me something that came from Himself, because I was in myself so dry and so empty of all good. Then the eyes of my soul were opened, and I saw *Love itself*, which came entirely to me; I saw its beginning and its progression, but not its end; I cannot make this understood with any comparison to visible things. As it now came to me, I saw it immediately with the eyes of my soul much more clearly than one can see anything with physical eyes.

2. Then I was suddenly filled with an inestimable love and satiation. It did indeed satisfy me, but nonetheless, at the same time it caused me such an incomprehensibly great hunger that all the limbs of my body were as if dislocated, and my soul was groaning with the greatest longing to reach that which she lacked. I wanted to hear, see, or touch nothing more, nor did I speak, nor did I know * if I could speak outwardly; but inwardly my soul spoke and cried out to Love, that she might not torment me with such a bitter death, for life seemed to me a true death.

3. Afterward, as I had drawn so intimately to Love that, because of the love that had taken hold of me, I believed I had become entirely Love, **God’s** word came to me and said: "There are many who believe they are in love, and yet they are in wrath; others, conversely, think that I hate them, who are nevertheless in my love." Then the soul answered and said: "Should I then be entirely Love? Or am I also still in wrath?" But to this I received no answer in words; instead, He gave me clearly to see and most certainly to feel that for which I asked Him, so that I was entirely satisfied by it. Divine love filled me to such an extent that I do not believe that

4. After this, I saw within me two distinct parts, just as if a road had been made through me. On one side, I saw nothing but Love and every good thing, which I saw came from **God** and not from me. And on the other side, I saw myself as entirely dry and barren, and how no good could come from me. Therefore, I recognized that it was not I who loved [**God** from within myself], although I felt myself to be entirely immersed in love, but rather that such love came from **God** alone. Afterward, Love united these parts that had been separate, and through this union gave me a new, far greater, and more fervent love than I had before; and then an inward longing came upon me to go toward Love, to unite myself perfectly with it.

5. Among those various kinds of love of which I have spoken here, the first mentioned is so great that I would never have known that a greater love could have existed, had I not afterwards been seized by that other *deadly love*. <note>The term "deadly love" (*tödtliche Liebe*) refers to a mystical state where the intensity of divine affection is so overwhelming that the "self" feels as if it is dying or being consumed.</note> Yet, besides that first pure and quiet love, and the other deadly and most fervent love, there is still another love, of which I can say nothing, because its depth and the overflowing nature of its joy and delight exceed all expression. And at the time when I am seized by it, I wish that I might hear nothing, not even of the suffering of the Son of **God**, indeed, that one would not even name **God** to me, because I * then experience **Him** within me with such great delight that everything else (that one might tell me of **Him**) would only be a hindrance to me, because it would all be lesser than **He** Himself.

6. And after this love has passed, I am entirely satisfied, entirely peaceful, and like an angel; I then love even the most contemptible creatures, such as toads, and even the devils; <note>This indicates a state of "holy indifference," where the soul sees the divine will behind all of creation, even the fallen parts of it.</note> nothing displeases me then that I see happening, even when I see others commit a sin, because I believe that **God** permits such things according to His justice. When I am in this state, I would not care if I were eaten by dogs; it seems to me I would not worry about it at all, or feel any pain from it. In this state, one has no memory of pain, nor can one shed any tears. Once it happened to me that I was in this love, and at the same time I remembered the precious blood of the Son of **God**, through which the * reconciliation <term>Reconciliation (Versöhnung): The theological concept of the Atonement, where humanity is brought back into a right relationship with God through Christ's sacrifice.</term> was surely brought about, and was also communicated to me at that time. I was extremely amazed by this, how it was possible that these two things <note>The "two things" being the state of joyous, painless love and the memory of the bloody, painful sacrifice of Christ.</note> could exist together within me.

->I.<-

One day, as I was ravished in spirit, I saw **God** in such great clarity that I had never seen Him so clearly or brightly, nor so completely. I no longer saw Love there; indeed, I myself became without love, and the love I had previously held vanished entirely. <note>This marks a transition from "affective" mysticism (feeling love) to "essential" mysticism (beholding God’s pure essence), where even the concept of "love" is surpassed by the reality of God Himself.</note>

(II.) After this, I saw God in a dark gloom <note>The "Divine Darkness" or "Cloud of Unknowing" is a central concept in mystical theology; it suggests that God is so far beyond human reason that the mind perceives Him as "darkness" or "obscurity" rather than clear light.</note>, for God is such a Good that it far exceeds everything that can be thought or grasped. At that moment, my soul was granted a completely certain faith, a most firm hope, and such a fundamental and lasting certainty of God that I lost all fear. I withdrew myself entirely into this inexpressible Good <term>Good: translating the German *Gut*, referring here to the "Highest Good" (Summum Bonum), the ultimate source of all value and existence</term> that I saw in the darkness, and I received there such a great assurance that I possessed God that I can never again doubt that I truly have Him.

7. I often see God in this way, in this Good that the tongue cannot speak and the heart cannot grasp. In this completely certain and completely hidden Good, which can only be recognized in the darkness, I place all my hope. When I see it, I have everything I wish to know, for in it I see All Good. When I see Him, my soul cannot imagine that He would ever separate from her, nor she from Him, nor that such a separation would even be possible; rather, she draws an inexpressible joy from His fullness, without seeing anything that can be spoken or understood. She sees nothing, and yet she sees absolutely Everything. This great Good is all the more certain the more it is surrounded by darkness.

(III.) Furthermore, I sometimes see—in an even greater darkness—a Good that exceeds all goodness and all things; all other things are but darkness in comparison with this Good, and everything that can be thought is far less than this great Good. Even when my soul sees God’s power, or His wisdom, or His will—as has happened several times in a truly wonderful and inexpressible way—it is still something less than this completely certain Good: for this Good is Everything; the others are merely like parts. When these parts are seen, although they are inexpressible, they are still somewhat sensory because of the great joy in which even the body participates; but the vision of God in the bare darkness <insert>which is raised above all connection to the senses</insert> makes neither the mouth smile, nor creates any burning heat, nor tender devotion, nor flames of love in the heart. The body is not driven away by it, nor moved, nor changed, as happens in other divine visions. Here the soul sees alone; the body sees nothing, it rests, it sleeps, the tongue is tied and can say nothing. All the tender endearments God has ever shown me (for He has shown me many and inexpressibly great ones), all the sweet words He has spoken to me, and all the graces He has ever shown me, are far lower than this great Good that is seen only in the greatest darkness; so that I ground my hope only on this and not on those [gifts of grace].

# The Seventh Chapter.

## God reveals Himself to her as Omnipresent, and thereafter as the One who makes the soul blessed, through His wonderful, inexpressible, profound, perfect, and incomparable workings.

After some time, and after all that was mentioned above, the woman of Foligno <note>Angela of Foligno (c. 1248–1309) was an Italian mystic and Franciscan tertiary. Her "Memorial" was recorded by her confessor, known as Brother Arnold.</note> said the following to me upon my inquiry: In this past Lent, I found myself unexpectedly entirely inward in God, in a greater way than I had ever been accustomed to before. And it seemed to me that I was in the midst of the Holy Trinity in a higher way than before, because I also received greater goods than I was used to; indeed, I was placed within these goods themselves in a permanent way; and as I was thus within God, I was full of joys, full of delights, and inexpressible goods and pleasures, beyond all other goods I had previously experienced. In this state, such inexpressible divine workings occurred in my soul that no angel nor saint is capable of comprehending or recounting them.

2. I feel how I am then drawn away from all those other goods in which I previously found myself, and in which I used to draw such great pleasure—namely in the life and in the humanity of Jesus Christ, and in the contemplation of that mystery-rich company which God the Father has always loved so much that He gave it to His Son; I mean, the poverty, the suffering, and the contempt of Jesus Christ, which is my true resting bed. <note>Angela frequently refers to the "bed" of Christ's suffering and poverty as the place where the soul finds its ultimate rest and union with the divine.</note> From all of this I feel myself being drawn out, as also from that contemplation of God in the darknesses. I am drawn away from this, and from all other states, with such great anointing <term>anointing: from the German *Salbung*, referring to a spiritual ease or grace that facilitates a transition into a deeper state of prayer</term>, and as if by such a sweet sleep, that I would have in no way noticed these changes, except that I remember no longer having that which I had before.

3. Regarding the great and inexpressible goods and divine workings, one must know that God first presents Himself to the soul through these His divine and inexpressible workings, and that He afterwards reveals and opens Himself to the soul, and imparts even far greater gifts to her.

(1) First, God presents Himself to the soul in a most intimate way; and then I understand how God is present in all of nature, and in everything that has being, as much in the devil as in a good angel, so—

...as well in hell as in paradise. God makes Himself present to me often in this way: This divine presence is an illumination paired with great truth, and with such great divine grace, that when the soul sees Him, (a) she cannot sin at all. This illumination brings many divine gifts to the soul; and because of the presence of God, she is greatly humbled before Him and ashamed because of her sins; she also attains there a wise gravity, along with much divine comfort and joy.

(II.) The other kind of divine presence is more particular and is very different from the former. It gathers the soul entirely within herself and gives her a completely different joy than the one mentioned before; it brings forth many divine workings, which are paired with much greater grace and with an abyss of unspeakable illuminations and divine delights. This making-present of God is, in itself and without any other gifts, the true Good that the saints enjoy in eternal life.

4. Regarding the gifts which the saints possess in eternal life, some have more of them, others fewer; in these gifts, certain expansions occur in the soul, through which she becomes ever wider and more capable of grasping and possessing God and His gifts. Now, when God makes Himself present to the soul and opens Himself to her, He also expands her and shares such gifts and delights with her, the likes of which she has never tasted before, and which penetrate her more fundamentally than anything I might have said until now. This soul is then drawn out of all darkness; and a greater knowledge of God is shared with the soul than I can conceive to be possible; and indeed with such clarity, with such sweetness, with such certainty, and so (b) deeply profound, that no thought can reach it, much less comprehend it.

5. The Holy Scripture, which testifies of these things, has such a hidden and exalted sense that no man in the world, however learned he may be, even if he had all understanding and spirit, can so fully understand it in this life that the Scripture would not still go higher than his understanding; nevertheless, one stammers about it. But of these inward and divine workings, when God reveals Himself to the soul, one cannot speak or stammer at all.

6. But because my soul is often raised to the divine mysteries, I understand this and can well grasp how the Holy Scripture is both easy and also difficult, how it seems to say something and also to contradict it, how it is useless to some, how it condemns those who do not perceive it (and in that way is fulfilled in them), and how others who keep it are made blessed through it. These insights and realizations mean that when I return to myself from the contemplation of the mysteries of God, I then take the liberty to speak a few little words externally of these unspeakable divine workings.

7. Truly, if all heavenly comforts, if all spiritual joys, if all divine delights that one could ever have enjoyed here on earth; yes, if everything that all the saints from the beginning of the world until now have ever been able to tell of God and divine things; and if beyond that all other permitted and unpermitted pleasures of the whole world were all transformed into good and spiritual delights and given to me together, and even if all of this were to remain with me constantly until its perfection and until it led me to the unspeakable Good of this divine revelation: I would still not trade the very slightest moment of the satisfaction I experience in this entirely unspeakable revelation of God in my soul for all of that.

8. Nevertheless, I am sometimes susceptible to certain external movements of joy and sadness. But there is a special little chamber <note>German: *Kämmerlein*. A common mystical metaphor for the most private, interior part of the soul where God dwells.</note> deep within my soul, wherein neither joy nor sadness, nor any created delight of whatever kind it may be—even not concerning any virtue or whatever else one might name—can enter; that same place is open alone to this (a) One and All-Good, a Good outside of which no Good is to be found.

9. In this high revelation of God (which I only fear to blaspheme through my speaking, for no one is capable of speaking of it), in this revelation of God, I say, all truth is enclosed. I grasp and possess within it all truths of heaven, of earth, of hell, and of the whole world, [ in all places and in every single thing, and all delights that are to be found in heaven and ] in all creatures, with such great truth and certainty that even if the whole world spoke to the contrary, I would not believe it, and would only mock all its contradictions. For I see Him who is the Essence itself; I see how He is the Essence of all created things; and I see how He has made me capable of understanding the aforementioned things now far better than before this, when I saw them in the darkness in which my mind <note>German: *Gemüth*, referring to the soul's disposition or inner feeling.</note> used to take so much delight.

10. I see myself then alone with God and in God, entirely pure, entirely sanctified, entirely truthful, entirely righteous, entirely assured, and entirely heavenly in Him. And when I am therein, I remember no other thing. Once when I was in this state, God spoke these words to me: *Daughter of divine wisdom, temple and delight of my Beloved, daughter of peace! The whole holy Trinity and the whole truth rest in you, so that you possess me, and I possess you.*

11. But when I have come back to myself out of this sublime state, then I look at myself [ within myself ] as entirely sin, and as the obedience of sin, entirely perverse, entirely impure, entirely false, entirely deceitful; yet I remain calm in this; for there remains always in me a divine anointing, which is the most sublime of all other anointings I have ever had.

### Eleventh Part. The Life

12. Moreover, I did not place myself in this state; I have been led and raised to it by God; for of my own accord, I would not have known how to desire such a state. At present, I am almost incessantly in this state, and God often raises my soul there without asking for my consent; for when I least expect it, and am not thinking of it at all, my soul is suddenly raised by God. It then seems to me that I embrace *and rule* the entire world, and that I am no longer on earth, but in heaven, in God Himself.

13. I have experienced this revelation of God more than a thousand times, and every time in a new and different way. Among others, it happened one day, as God revealed Himself to my soul in the aforementioned unspeakable manner, that He simultaneously set the soul before its own eyes. Then my soul saw itself as being of such great nobility <note>German: *Adel*. In mystical tradition, the "nobility" of the soul refers to its divine origin and its capacity to mirror God.</note> and so exalted that I could never have thought or grasped it; indeed, I could never have believed that the souls of the saints in Paradise—to say nothing of my own soul—could have been of such high nobility. My soul could not comprehend itself.

14. This time, God presented my soul to itself with the greatest confidence, without having the slightest fear; and this happened with the greatest delight I have ever experienced, and with such an intimate and excellent joy, alongside which there was something truly wonderful, new, and clear, the likes of which I had never recognized in my soul. When God and my soul met one another in such a form, and He revealed Himself to me in this new and unspeakable way, certain words were spoken to me by God which were so exalted that I do not wish for them to be written down.

15. When my soul came back to itself, it found itself inwardly disposed in such a way that it took great pleasure in enduring all kinds of shame and pain for God's sake, and that henceforth it could be separated from God by nothing that might be done or said. For this reason, my soul cried out loudly and said: “O my dear Lord! what will henceforth be able to separate me from You?” <note>A reference to the Apostle Paul’s words in Romans 8:35: "Who shall separate us from the love of Christ?"</note> To which I received as an answer: That by means of His grace, nothing more would henceforth be able to separate me from God. Therefore, the day of death *greatly gladdens* me; yes, the day of death brings me an inestimable joy when I think of it.

The words that were spoken to me by God, I heard in a language so wonderful that I cannot express it; I was told: how this unspeakable revelation of God was the very same Good that the saints have in eternal life; it is not different in essence from that Good; but they enjoy it in a way that is so very different from that of which I have spoken, that the least among all the saints, who has the smallest portion in eternal life, nevertheless has more than any soul can receive in this life.

## Chapter Eight.

### She seeks and receives from God renewed assurance concerning the revelations, visions, and words spoken to her.

->I.<-

1. One day, not long after my conversion <note>German: *Bekehrung*. Angela’s conversion involved a dramatic shift from a worldly life to one of extreme asceticism following the death of her family.</note>, as I prayed that it might be made known to me that I was not being deceived by the words spoken to me, this assurance was promised to me on God's behalf. It was said to me: God has revealed Himself to you, He has spoken with you, He has given you the ability to feel His presence. See to it, then, that from this point on you speak nothing, see nothing, and hear nothing except according to His pleasure. This was said to me in a most solemn manner.

2. As soon as I began to practice these three things, my heart was so elevated above all earthly things and so anchored in God that whether I ate, spoke, or did anything else, it did not prevent my heart from being always in God. I could think of nothing, see nothing, and feel nothing but God. And when I had finished my prayer and wished to go to the table for a meal, I asked Him for permission, which He then gave me, saying: Go, and eat with the blessing of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. He gave me this permission sometimes more quickly, sometimes more slowly; this continued without ceasing for three days and three nights.

3. Another time, as I was in prayer, God spoke these loving words to me: My dear daughter, I delight more in you than you delight in me; my temple, my love! The heart of Almighty God rests upon your heart. He added further: God the Almighty has placed more of His love in you than in any other single woman in this city. God takes His pleasure in you and in your companion <note>German: *Gesellin*. This likely refers to the woman who accompanied Angela on her pilgrimages and shared her ascetic lifestyle.</note>. Therefore, strive to ensure that your lives are a light to all who wish to look upon them. And all those who * see this light and do not follow it, for them it shall be a heavy judgment. In this, my soul also understood that this judgment would be more cruel for the learned <note>German: *Gelehrten*. In Angela's time, this often referred to theologians or church authorities who might be skeptical of uneducated lay mystics.</note> than for the common people; for the learned despise such divine things, even though they know enough of them from the Holy Scripture.

4. He also said to me: God the Almighty bears such a great love for you that He is always with you, though not always in such a way as you feel Him now; and His divine eyes are now upon you. It also seemed to me that I truly saw these divine eyes with the eyes of my soul, which caused me such extraordinary delight and joy that it is unspeakable; and whatever I may say of it is, to my great regret, only a mockery of the truth. 5. These such great things, which had been said to me, began to throw me into consternation, so that I also said:
> “If You, who speak with me, were the Son of Almighty God, then surely my soul would receive a far greater joy from it than it tastes now; for feeling You within me, despite my unworthiness, I would surely not be able to bear the excess of joy therefrom.”

6. To have even more explanation and certainty of the truth of what He said to me, my soul cried out once again: 
> “Because it is then the truth that You are the Almighty God, and the things are true which You say to me, then give me a sign to assure me of it and to put me beyond doubt.”

But I meant a physical, visible sign. Whereupon He gave me as an answer: This sign which you demand would perhaps cause you a passing joy for the time when you saw or touched it, without drawing you out of your doubt; indeed, with such a sign you could still be deceived. But I will give you a far more excellent sign than you have desired; and this sign will be within your interior, where you will experience it at all times. Namely this: that you will always be in the love of God, inflamed by this love, and enlightened by His divine knowledge. This shall be a quite certain sign to you that it is I who deal with you; for no one but I alone can give you this sign. I give you this in the interior of your soul, and that is far better for you than everything for which you have asked. I pour my love into you, and indeed such a love through which your soul will always be fervent toward me. Yes, this love will be so fervent that if something evil is said or done to you, you will recognize it as a great grace; indeed, you will still judge yourself unworthy of such a grace; because I also bore such a love toward you and suffered everything with great patience and humility; from this you will certainly recognize that I am He. Yes, even if no one were actually to say or do anything evil to you, you would nonetheless have a great thirst and desire for it, and value it as a great grace. I saw all that this sorrowful <term>God-man</term> <note>A term for Christ emphasizing the union of His divine and human natures.</note> had suffered in His life and in His death through this heartfelt and inexpressible love; therefore, I could understand in a living way that it is entirely true that He did not love me in a feigned way, but that He loved me with an entirely sincere, most perfect, and most heartfelt love. On the other hand, I discovered the exact opposite in myself; and I saw that my love for Him [compared with His love] was nothing but pretense and mockery, and that I did not love Him according to the truth.

7. This discovery was so highly painful and unbearably distressing to me that I thought I must die from it; nonetheless, He repeated these words to me immediately afterward: *I have not loved you in a feigned way;* thereafter He added these: *I have not served you for appearance’s sake.* I have (a) not felt your miseries from afar.

These words increased my deadly pain; my soul cried out and said to Him: "O highest **Lord**! In me is found perfectly what You say is not in You; for I have indeed loved You in no other way than a feigned one."

### Eleventh Section. The Life

> “In a manner of falsehood and pretense: I did not want to come truly close to you, to feel something of those hardships that you were willing to suffer and endure for me, and I have never loved you in truth and for your own sake; but rather with double-heartedness <note>Original: "Doppelherzigkeit." Refers to a divided will or insincerity in one's devotion.</note> and carelessness.”

8. When I saw this—namely, how the **Lord Jesus** had loved me in truth, and how all the signs of a most truthful love were found in Him; how He gave Himself up without reservation to my service; how He drew so near to me that He even became a human being, so that He might truly feel and bear my pains within Himself—and I perceived in myself the exact opposite, this caused me such an overwhelming pain that I nearly died of it; it was as if my heart wanted to burst. As I later thought more specifically about the word: *I have not felt you and your miseries from afar*, He then added: **I am much more inward to your soul than it is to itself**; <note>This echoes the famous sentiment of St. Augustine: "interior intimo meo" (higher than my highest and more inward than my innermost self).</note> this doubled my suffering again; for the more I saw that **God** was so inwardly close to me, the more I saw myself, on my part, removed from Him.

9. After this, He spoke a few more words to me, which testified in the tenderest way to the love He bore for us: “If anyone,” He said, “had a desire to perceive me in their soul, I would by no means withdraw myself from them. If anyone desired to see me, I would give myself to be seen by them with great pleasure; and if anyone desired to converse with me, I would let them hear my voice with the highest delight.” These words put my soul into a longing that I might no longer perceive, nor see, nor speak, nor do anything else by which **God** could be offended. And this He also requires in a special way from His children and from His chosen ones; for because they are called and chosen by Him to perceive Him, to see Him, and to talk with Him, they carefully distance themselves from everything that is contrary to this.

10. **God** showed me this truth and said to me: “Those who are lovers and followers of the **poverty**, the **suffering**, and the **humility** in which I always lived on earth, those are my true children and real chosen ones. And those whose minds are constantly directed toward my suffering and my death (as that in which the true salvation and the quickening <term>quickening: the act of being made spiritually alive (Lebendigmachung)</term> of all consists, and nowhere else), those are my true children: and all the others are not.”

11. Another time, as I was in prayer and was contemplating the suffering of **Jesus Christ** with much compassion and pain of heart, I thought to myself how great the abomination of each of my sins must be, since **God** the Father could not be satisfied unless the Son of **God** not only prayed and pleaded with tears but even died on the wood of the cross, so that He might bring about forgiveness and reconciliation for me. ## The Life of Angela of Foligno. Chapter IX. ##

11. ...further, what great damnation, endless misery, and torment I have deserved through my heavy sins, since for their satisfaction <note>Original: "Gnugthuung." 12. This was shown to me so clearly and powerfully that I could hardly restrain myself from making this known with a loud voice and before all the world.

13. Then the **Lord JESUS** Christ appeared to me in the form in which He was nailed to the cross, and said Himself to me:

> “No human has any excuse to offer for why they are not saved; for to that end, one need only do exactly as a sick person does toward a physician. If they truly wish to become well, they only reveal their illness and prepare themselves to heed whatever the physician prescribes. No human needs to do more if they wish to be saved; one does not even need to buy the medicines, but only to show oneself to the [heavenly] physician, confessing one's miseries to Him, and preparing oneself for everything the physician prescribes, and taking care that one mixes nothing contrary into it.”

Then my soul recognized that the blood of **JESUS** Christ was the true medicine, which **JESUS** Christ shared for free, and which cost the sick sinner nothing more than that he simply conform himself to the order <note>Or "discipline." In this context, it refers to the spiritual path or the "prescription" of the Gospel.</note>. **JESUS** Christ was the physician who shares salvation and heals all spiritual illnesses.

14. At the same time, **GOD** let my soul see all its sins; and I became aware that every one of my limbs was afflicted with a particular illness. Therefore, after I had understood what was mentioned above, I immediately did my utmost to reveal to the supreme Physician all my miseries and sins which I had committed through all the limbs of my body and through all the powers of my soul, and I sought to lay them all out before Him, piece by piece.

15. After the **Lord JESUS** Christ had listened with great patience to everything I said to Him, He answered me quite lovingly, and with a joyful friendliness, that He wanted to heal me of all my illnesses. He let me see them one after another and said to me with great compassion:

> “Do not fear, my daughter, and by no means despair: even if you were afflicted with a thousand illnesses and killed by a thousand deaths, you can still perfectly recover from them through the medicine I will give you, provided you will use this medicine in true and fervent godliness.”

16. 19. For the sins of your mouth / and its lustful gluttony <note>Original: *Fraß*. 21. For the sins of your sense of smell / which you sought to please in a lustful way through all kinds of fragrant things: for that I felt and endured the gruesome stench of the nasty spit / that they threw into my nose / into my eyes / and into my whole face.

25. For the sins of your dressing up, your superfluous and vain clothes, I was stripped completely naked to be hung on the Cross; the most dissolute people gambled for my clothes before my eyes. 26. When I died, I did not even have my own grave, had there not been someone who, moved by love and compassion for my misery, took me into his grave. In short, I even stripped myself of all things, so that I gave my own blood and life to sinful men; I have thus kept nothing at all for myself, and have both lived and died in voluntary poverty. And because your soul drew an inner delight from all the aforementioned sins, you see also how my most holy soul was burdened from all sides with all kinds of the most cruel sufferings.

# The Tenth Chapter.

## Appearance of the infant Jesus, who praises smallness to her. The compassionate appearance of the Crucified One, who embraces His children, colors them with His blood, blesses them, and commands them to proclaim the way of the cross. What God requires of His true children.

->1.<-

One day, in an ecstasy of the spirit, I saw the child Jesus as He was being presented in the temple by His mother, and suddenly He was given quite naked into my arms. He opened His little eyes, raised them upward, and began to look at me. As soon as I looked into these divine eyes, I felt myself inwardly struck by such a powerful arrow of love that I became almost faint; for from these eyes there radiated such a living brilliance and such a powerful fire of love and delight that it far exceeds all my powers of expression. Afterward, in an instant, He let Himself be seen by me as an immeasurable and unspeakable Majesty, and said to me: "He who has not seen me small will never see me great." Then He added: "I have come to you and have offered Myself up for you, so that you also might offer yourselves up to Me." Then my soul offered itself up to Him in a most wondrous and unspeakable way; afterward, I also offered myself up together with my spiritual children, so perfectly that I kept nothing for myself or for them as my own. My soul also recognized how very pleasing this offering was to God, and that He accepted it with great joy.

<margin>(a) Our manuscript contains more on this, which we have mostly followed here. Compare <note>original: "Conf. Theol. de la Croix"</note> *Theology of the Cross*, pages 328 and 365.</margin>

2. [Although (a) this blessed soul was always and unceasingly receiving such lights from above, which swallowed her up in God in a way quite unspeakable to us; nevertheless, she also frequently received new gifts from the inexhaustible sea of divine goodness which she had never experienced before. These were generally more sublime than all her previous states and led her even deeper into the unfathomable abyss of God. So it happened on a certain Sunday, while she was in the church and the angelic song, "Holy, Holy" <note>The *Sanctus* of the Mass.</note> was being sung, that my soul (these are again her own words) was drawn away from itself by the Majesty of the highest and uncreated God in such a manner, and was taken into and swallowed up by the uncreated light itself, with such great enjoyment and enlightenment of the mind that it is entirely and utterly unspeakable. And whatever one might be able to say about it, it is all as nothing, for no mortal man can be made to understand the blessed essence of the uncreated, almighty God.

3. After this engulfment into the abyss of the Divinity, while the previous divine influence remained as ever, things changed, and there appeared to me the form of the <term>God-man<note>original: "Gottmensch" — A theological term referring to Christ as having both divine and human natures perfectly united.</note></term>, praised in eternity, in such a manner as if He had only just been taken down from the cross; and His blood seemed to flow quite fresh and red from His wounds, just as if the wounds had only now been made. All the joints of the limbs of this holy body also appeared so far removed from one another—because the murderous hands of the dissolute men had so unmercifully and cruelly pulled and stretched these virginal limbs upon the cross—that the veins and bones seemed to be entirely displaced from their natural seat, although one could perceive no opening in the outer skin.

4. As I had this sorrowful spectacle before my eyes, my inmost being was so moved and pierced by such great compassion that it seemed to me I was being <term>transformed<note>original: "vergestaltet" — Reshaped or conformed into the likeness of another; a central concept in mystical union.</note></term> with my whole body and soul into the pains of the Crucified One; yes, it was to me as if not only my entrails but also all my bones urged me to lament, making me feel entirely new and piercing pains in both soul and body. Also * I was quite bewildered by this divine influence, because on the one hand the uncreated God refreshed my soul with the unspeakable enlightenment of the brilliance of His <term>delightful Divinity<note>original: "schmackhaften Gottheit" — Referring to the "spiritual taste" (gustus spiritualis), where the presence of God is experienced as a sensory sweetness or satisfaction.</note></term>; and at the same time the very same blessed God-man Jesus pierced me through with compassion and pain over His crucifixion and bitter death, which were shown to me.

4. This happened not without reason, are the words of the <term>original scribe<note>original: "Uhrschreiber" — The primary recorder of Angela's visions, likely Brother Arnaldo.</note></term>, for it seems the blessed God-man Jesus wished, through an invisible effect, to grant this perfected soul the ability to bear His twofold state: namely, the state of <term>contemplation<note>original: "Beschauung" — The quiet, direct observation of divine mysteries.</note></term> here on earth, which is indeed not a perfect state but nevertheless agrees in some measure with the state of the blessed in heaven; and then the state of His outward crucifixion through compassion and the transformation into His death. For this soul truly, above all those I have ever seen with my own eyes, strove with the utmost diligence to be entirely uniform to the life of Jesus. Yet I will remain silent regarding her praise, because no tongue is capable of properly recounting her virtues, so let us proceed in the order we have begun.

6. As I was now at once entirely engulfed by the divine sweetness, and stood entirely crucified in the sight of the Crucified One, at once joyful and sorrowful, filled both with myrrh and with honey, as if deified and crucified; behold, there suddenly appeared around the Crucified One the multitude of my spiritual children, whom this blessed Jesus called to Himself, each and every one in particular, with great love. He embraced them, held their heads with His holy hands, and held them near to the wound of His side, so that they might kiss it. The demonstration of such an intimate and heartfelt love of Jesus toward my children caused me such great joy that I forgot all the pains I had previously felt.

-># of Angela of Foligno. Chapter X.<-

7. Regarding the way and manner in which the Savior held these children close to His side, I saw a great difference in their **ranks** <note>original: "Staffeln" — This refers to levels or degrees of spiritual maturity or proximity to God.</note>. Some He drew very close to Himself; others did not come as near; some He also pressed frequently to His side, and indeed, some were even drawn into it and hidden within. 8. The Savior also poured out the abundance of His blessings over each and every one, saying:

> Blessed are you who were found worthy to suffer poverty, pain, and contempt with Me, and also to have compassion for the sufferings of Him who was crucified for you, who endured infinite suffering so that He might make satisfaction for you and redeem you from infinite eternal suffering.

10. 
> Blessed are you who now have devotion and a share—or shall have in the future—in My Passion, which is the **masterpiece** <note>original: "Wunderwerk" — Can be translated as miracle or wondrous work; here it signifies the supreme act of divine intervention.</note> of all ages, the salvation and life of those who are lost, and the only refuge of sinners; for you shall truly have a share with Me in the kingdom, in the glory, and in the resurrection that I have earned through My suffering; you shall be My **joint-heirs** in all eternity.

11. 
> Be all blessed by My Father and by the Holy Spirit; be all blessed in the truth and with the very same blessing that I shall distribute to My elect on the Last Day! For when I came to My own, you did not reject Me as My persecutors did, but received Me as a guest into the house of your heart when I was so comfortless and abandoned. You who, when I hung quite naked on the cross—hungry, thirsty, weary, pierced with nails, even dying—did not withdraw yourselves from having compassion for My state, but became companions of My suffering, and have thereby fulfilled all **works of mercy** <note>Christ’s words here echo the Gospel of Matthew (25:31-46), suggesting that showing spiritual compassion for Christ’s suffering is equivalent to physical acts of charity toward the "least of these."</note>. For this very reason, on that day which is otherwise so terrible, you shall hear this voice: *Come here, you blessed of My Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you; for I thirsted on the cross, and you gave Me drink, as you had compassion and were partakers of My suffering.*

The Savior continued further with this Gospel-like blessing in an exquisite manner; and it is not possible for me to express the heartfelt love that radiated from the holy eyes of the Son of GOD as He looked upon these children and pressed them to the wound in His side, nor the love in all those words of blessing and other marks of His affection toward them.

# Eleventh Part. The Life of <note>The header is incomplete, referring to the life of the Blessed Angela of Foligno.</note>

...a wholehearted, inward love for you; He wishes to bear the entire burden of your penance. He only demands of you, my children, that you be shining examples of His poor, despised, and sorrowful life; to that end, He desires and demands to see you living-dead <note>A mystical term for complete detachment from worldly desires while still alive.</note>, so that your dwelling may be in heaven, and the use of your body alone on earth; so that just as a dead person is moved neither by honor nor dishonor, you too may remain unmoved by anything external in the world. May you preach the dying-to-self <term>Absterbung: the spiritual process of mortifying the ego or "dying" to worldly impulses</term> to others more through your life than with many words. In all your actions, let your motive and intent be directed toward heaven alone, toward the crucified and eternally praised God-man <note>A title for Jesus emphasizing His dual nature as both fully God and fully human.</note>; so that, whether you speak, eat, work, or whatever else you perform outwardly, you may always be inwardly (a) most deeply turned toward your God—praised in eternity—who wishes to carry you about always within Himself (b) and to stand by you at all times in all your affairs.

[As comforting as this may be for the "new man" <note>A biblical reference to the spiritually reborn self.</note>, it will, on the other hand, seem bitter to the unrestrained and unmortified natural mind, in whose ears the words our Blessed Lady <note>Angela of Foligno.</note> uses at the end of one of her letters, in the same vein as a greeting and reminder, will sound no less strange:]
> O my * dear child! she says, I desire from my whole heart that you may be a lover and follower of the pains and sufferings of Jesus Christ. And I desire with all my heart that you be stripped of all temporal and spiritual comfort. This very thing is my comfort; I pray you, let it be yours as well. For I seek to serve or love God not for any reward, but I seek to serve and love Him because of His incomprehensible divine goodness. And I wish that you may grow anew and be born again in this desire—namely, that you might be stripped of all comfort out of love for the comfortless God-man Jesus Christ. I write no other greeting to you than this: that you may always grow in divine union, and in the hunger and thirst to have tribulation and suffering as long as you live. (c)

## Chapter Eleven.

->GOD calls all people to eternal life, specifically through the path of tribulations; the preciousness of the same. GOD comforts His own in all sufferings: which she proves with glorious consolations that happen to her person from GOD.<-

I.

<meta>This page continues the spiritual instructions of Angela of Foligno, specifically elaborating on the metaphor of the divine banquet and the necessity of suffering as the path to intimacy with God. It follows from the previous page's discussion on "dying-to-self."</meta>

<page-num>353</page-num>
<header>of Angela of Foligno. Chapter XI.</header>

...[Imagine] one who has many friends, all of whom he had invited to a banquet that had been prepared with great care. Now, if many of those invited did not wish to come, even though he had prepared everything so expensively and abundantly for them, is it not so that he would become very indignant with them? And would he not receive the others who did come with much joy? Even though he would indeed receive them all with great pleasure, he would nevertheless let those whom he loved above others sit at his own table and near his own person; but his most intimate and trusted friends he would moreover allow to eat from the very same dish and drink from the very same chalice that he himself used. I replied to this with great love: "Lord, pray tell me, in what manner do You invite all people?" "I have invited them all," He said, "to eternal life; let whoever will, come. No one will be able to excuse themselves by saying they were not called to it. Some will always come, and I will set them at My table." He also gave me to understand that He Himself was both the table and the food upon it. <note>This is a central mystical concept: Christ is the host, the table, and the Eucharistic meal itself.</note>

2. Regarding those among the called who had come to the banquet, I asked Him by what path they had come? He answered: "By the path of tribulations." In this conversation with God, I was also told that all kinds of tribulations and mortifications <term>Ertödtungen: the spiritual practice of "deadening" or subduing the ego and physical desires to focus on the spirit</term>, such as abstinence, poverty, illness, loss of children, or loss of temporal goods, and the like—all were dealt by God Himself to His children for their true best interest, even if they did not think so or did not yet know how to recognize it, but were initially troubled by it. But the upright children would soon reach the point where they endured these things with patience, and indeed even with thanksgiving. And so it generally goes for all those who enter into eternal life; there is indeed no other way to enter into it.

3. I was also told that those who are seated at the Lord’s special table, and whom He allows to eat with Him from one dish and drink from one chalice, are those who specifically apply themselves to reaching the knowledge of the Father and Lord who has invited them; and who strive to become pleasing to Him through the following of His cross and the willing acceptance of poverty, contempt, and suffering. God allows it to happen that a multitude of all kinds of tribulations come upon such souls, which are given to them as so many quite special tokens of favor, so that they may one day eat with Him from one dish. "I myself," said the Lord Jesus Christ, "was called to this table, namely to drink the chalice of My sufferings, which indeed was very bitter in itself, but was sweet to Me because of the love I bear for you." It is the same for all true children of God who properly recognize the grace shown to them by the heavenly Father; for although the tribulations are sometimes very sensitive and bitter to them, they nevertheless become sweet to them over time because of the love, the grace, the glory, and the inestimable goods that are enclosed within them.

<meta>This page continues the spiritual memoirs of Angela of Foligno, exploring the mystical paradox where the believer finds divine sweetness and joy within intense physical and spiritual suffering, following the previous discussion on the path of tribulations.</meta>
