# Twelfth Part. The Life

“The infinite and uncreated Being possesses and works within this created being, but is infinitely far removed from the Nothingness, which is sin.

6. “But what is the soul doing in all of this? She loves. But what is it to love? It is to unite oneself. But what is it to unite oneself? It is to love. Let us then love, so that we may be one with God. Let us be one with God, so that we may love.

7. “In what, then, does innocence consist in this love and union with this Everything, who is the soul’s Bridegroom and God? The innocence of this love consists in its being without a human ‘why,’ without fear, without intention, and without rule.

8. “It is infinite in respect to the extension of its will, which desires God. If one throws something heavy by force out of its point of rest—<note>original: "Ruhepunt"</note> for example, when a stone is thrown into the air—it cannot rest until it has returned there again. The soul’s true point of rest is God; if the soul is in this state, then she has returned to her true point of rest, which is God. Thus it happens in this blissful state that the soul lies down to rest in God as her true center <note>The concept of God as the "center" or "gravity" of the soul was a common theme in 17th-century mysticism.</note>, without any hindrance; there is now her dwelling, there are her delights, there is her paradise on earth, the holy land.

9. “Here one must notice three parts in this state: First, the purity of life of these souls. Secondly, the purity of their love in God. Thirdly, the purity of their love for their neighbor. The purity of life in this state is so simple and so pure that no kind of effect is found—neither in the soul nor in her powers, nor in the body, nor in any actions of human life—that does not all come forth from her origin <note>The text uses the German "Ursprung" and provides the synonym "principe" (principle) in brackets.</note> and from the essence of her Everything, which is God, whom the soul possesses and by whom she is possessed; just as everything aims toward God and ends in God. And these souls have such a light that they see in all effects and deeds what must belong to God, and what must be done in Him and for Him.

10. “The purity of their love in God is here so pure, so simple, so strong, so fervent, and so constant that the world—yes, even a hundred thousand worlds and hell itself—would not be able to move it. O Love, you who alone give life! O Love, you who alone have taken death away from us! O Love, you who alone have opened heaven to us!

“I am not speaking here of visions <note>original: "Gesichtern," literally "faces" or "sights," referring to mystical visual revelations.</note> and revelations; the soul stands and knows everything here in God, and what God wants her to know. It is an enjoying love, where the soul enjoys the great Good, which is God Himself, and where she does nothing else but praise, love, and admire this Good with body and soul.

## The Ninth Chapter.

### Her life in solitude. Struggles with evil spirits, illnesses, and other trials. Manifold encouragement at this time. The power of her intercession.

->1.<-

In what manner the dear Johanna lived, suffered, and loved in this poor hermit’s hut, we shall now further observe for a little while: On December 8th, when she had not been enclosed for long, she wrote to her spiritual guide <note>original: "Führer" — a "spiritual director" who oversaw her religious life and discipline.</note> that she still felt she had too little time to commune with God. She received the Holy Communion daily; in the forenoon, she spent her time in interior prayer; in the afternoon until evening, she worked with her hands; the remaining time she devoted once more to prayer. She would have gladly spent the entire night in prayer with God and the citizens of heaven <note>The saints and angels.</note>, which would have been her paradise; but she said she must still torment herself by allowing her "evil body" a little rest. She concludes the letter with these words:
> “I pray to God, my dear Father, that He may so inflame you and me through His love, that henceforth we think of nothing else but love, that we speak of nothing else but love, that we live through nothing else but love, and that we die no other death than the death of love, so that we may live again eternally in this divine love; just as we already live here for the enamored heart of the sweet crucified Jesus, dying to ourselves through His bloody heart that was crucified out of love, and living for God through the golden heart of the love of Jesus.”

2. On January 6th, 1626, she wrote the following to her guide:

> “I greet you in the holy wound of the pierced side of our Bridegroom, Jesus; and I pray to God that the little Jesus may grant you for the New Year those two bridal chambers which are in His holy side: one is His heart of flesh and blood, which represents His humanity; the other is His golden heart, representing His divinity united with His humanity: and that you may take possession of these two chambers in such a way that you never come out again. I request that you also pray for me, that I may enter so deeply therein that I remain dwelling there for all eternity.”

> “Furthermore, He who alone possesses my heart and all my inclinations knows that I love neither my relatives, nor other people, nor anything else under heaven, except only in GOD and for GOD; and I desire to have no other commerce than in GOD and before GOD. Regarding my father, who fathered me physically, I have, through the grace of GOD, fathered him spiritually. Do you know in what manner? I have wept so much over his sins that no bucket would be large enough to hold all my tears. In short, GOD, who is so entirely kind and gracious, has granted me my father, with the assurance of his salvation <note>original: "Seligkeit" — refers to eternal happiness or the state of being saved in heaven.</note>; he lives now like a true clergyman <note>The text suggests he took up a life of religious devotion similar to a monk or priest.</note>, and daily has his regular hours for prayer, without losing even a half-hour that he does not employ most usefully. GOD be eternally praised!”

4. After she had lived for some time in her lonely little chamber, various unusual trials and battles arrived; the evil enemy <note>A common historical term for the Devil or Satan.</note> made use of her fearful nature to disturb her in all sorts of ways, much as one reads regarding the first Christians. She often thought her little house was filled with evil spirits; sometimes he knocked and made all sorts of clamor in her chamber; sometimes she was awakened at night by a cruel howling of animals and children; sometimes it was as if a hidden power wanted to throw her down the stairs; sometimes, in a strange way, she broke the pot in which she wanted to prepare something to eat, so that her hand was grievously injured in two places, no matter how much she tried to take care; and many such things happened at this time. In all this, she was always strengthened in faith and mocked the enemy, saying: 
> “Go away, proud spirit! Are you not ashamed that you attack a lowly daughter and poor sinner in such a way?”

5. She was also put to the test regarding her outward necessities, as she occasionally had to suffer no small lack of supplies. Once, when she had allowed her thoughts to wander a little too far into this fear, she received a sharp rebuke in her inner self, and because of it, she had to do without her usual union with GOD for a whole day. She felt that there was an obstruction between the LORD and her soul, so that she cried out in affectionate lament: 
> “O Love! where art Thou? O Love! what have I done that is displeasing to Thee? Tell me, O Love! for I cannot be separated from Thee.” 
Then her fault was shown to her, and how she had focused too much upon herself.

6. Along with such trials came all sorts of weaknesses and illnesses of the body, which she had to endure without human comfort or help. This single short letter to her biological brother can give us a picture of it:

7. It was also no small cross for her at this time that she received so many visits from men, women, and daughters, who without hesitation revealed to her their condition, their spiritual exercises, their sufferings, and their sinful inclinations, and sought her advice on how they should conduct themselves and please GOD. She complained about this to her spiritual guide <note>original: "Führer" — a director or confessor who provided spiritual oversight.</note>, under the pretext that she herself was blind and imperfect, and that she should be ashamed to advise others; “it seems to me,” she said to him, “that I find myself much more drawn to mourn my sins in solitude than to speak with creatures, even regarding spiritual things; I desire to leave the world entirely, and all creatures, etc.” Regardless of this, she was required by the command of her guide to continue giving an account and an answer to everyone; just as she also, around this very time and upon this occasion, wrote her **Treatise on the Improvement of the Married State.**

Thus she found her work and suffering just as much in her closed-off little chamber as she had previously among people; the Lord, however, was also there inside with her, and strengthened her with various graces, divine visitations, and His most intimate union, of which we shall mention one thing or another hereafter.

8. First, we must now remind and demonstrate how the interaction and intercession of the dear Johanna was blessed to the salvation of many souls; one will indeed be able to notice this here and there in this history of her life, but there would still be many remarkable things to cite regarding it. It was experienced on many occasions that she could recognize the thoughts of other people, and that her prayer was a pleasing sacrifice before GOD. To touch upon just a few examples of this:

On September 17, 1627, five or six vain young women from the city of Lille <note>original: "Ryssel" — the Flemish name for the city of Lille in modern-day France.</note> had joined together to visit the cloistered Johanna out of pure curiosity <note>original: "Vorwiz" — an idle or meddlesome inquisitiveness.</note>, to see what she might have to say; as soon as they arrived, Johanna recognized that they had come only with a frivolous mind; she asked them why they had come to her, a poor daughter, when there were so many good and wise teachers in the city? “We come,” they said, “to hear something good from you.” Johanna replied: “Yes, you come out of a little curiosity, to hear for once what the cloistered woman knows to say.” They, however, constantly denied it, and begged that she would speak something good with them. “Well then,” she said with a smiling mouth, “because you desire to know what I can do, I will then speak”; and thereupon she began to preach to them in a veiled manner about everything that she recognized in their inner selves; so that one blushed with shame, another turned pale, and some [confessed] their

She encouraged me greatly for the struggle and said it was high time to put a stop to this evil. While I was in conversation with her, I felt inwardly compelled to desire her assistance and prayer; however, I paid no mind to this inner impulse and let the time pass by.

10. A certain distinguished [so-called] clergyman near Lille <note>original: "Ryssel" — the Flemish name for the city of Lille.</note>, who led an entirely vain life and in more than one way conducted himself in a manner unbecoming of his station, came to Johanna in the year 1626 and asked her to pray for him; shortly thereafter, he was fundamentally converted to God and is now pursuing perfect sanctification. This change in himself he attributed [after God] to the prayer of Sister Johanna.

11. A murderer, who sat imprisoned awaiting death and remained in the most gruesome hardening and rage—so much so that it caused a stir in the whole city—was suddenly converted through her prayer. He became as gentle as a lamb and died, against all human expectations, in a state of repentance <term>Busse: a state of penitence or atonement for sins</term>.

12. In September of the year 1625, as she entered into prayer to pray for her biological mother, she felt a strong internal urge to pray for the soul of a certain person of high rank who had set out on a journey that very same day. She could have known nothing of this had it not been worked within her by God. In the spirit, she saw this person raised up before God, and she begged that God might make his soul blessed and preserve him against the dangers of the devil and the world; she said to God, in her accustomed manner:

> My God, grant me this soul!

Then she saw the Savior with open and bleeding wounds, where especially the wound in His side was wide open, and the blood flowed out over that soul, by which all his sins were washed away, and she was given an assurance of the salvation of his soul.

13. In April of the year 1622, she spoke with a pious person who stood in great longing for sanctification; this man now complained to her that, despite all his labor, he could not reach perfection nor the enjoyment of divine love. He therefore earnestly requested of Johanna that she might pray to God on his behalf so that He—where it might otherwise serve His honor—might grant him some divine comfort and some supernatural graces, and this not to satisfy his own tastes, but so that he might love God all the more heartily,

### Twelfth Piece. The Life

...and might also be so much more edifying to others in his office. When our Johanna saw all the good intentions of this man, she was moved to pray for him from the bottom of her heart; then God gave her to understand that because this person had gone through no suffering, he must also not have the desired consolations. A few days later, when he visited Johanna again, she asked him (without letting on in the slightest what God had made known to her) whether he had also experienced many sufferings in the world? He answered: No, he had never had any; everywhere he had been, he was always loved and respected. Then she said to him that if one wanted to have divine consolations, one must pass through tribulations, adversities, and suffering. With this, she merely encouraged him to love God as heartily as he possibly could.

14. In the year 1628, on the 13th of March, when her biological brother was undergoing suffering and heavy persecution from men, she said to God in prayer, out of compassion for her brother: 
> “My God, how can you watch your bride endure such suffering? Although I was (these are her own words) composed in God’s will; I offered my heart and the heart of my brother to the sweet Bridegroom of our souls, and then He spoke these words to me in an intelligible way: ‘If you wish for Me to take your brother’s heart, he must also be crucified with your heart and with My heart, so that I may make it into a burnt offering <term>Brandopfer: a sacrifice entirely consumed by fire, symbolizing total devotion to God</term> to God My Father.’ I was satisfied with this, and offered Him my brother’s heart, my heart, and His heart, with the plea that He might be pleased with this sacrifice. Nevertheless, my nature <note>original: "Natur" — referring to her human, physical, or un-transformed self</note> was terrified, and I thought about what more I might be able to suffer. Afterward, I reflected further on what was said to me—namely, that the heart of Jesus was crucified and suffered with our heart—and I thought: how is it possible that God can suffer? Then He spoke these words: ‘You suffer in your brother because you love him, and I suffer in you and in him because I love you; but because you are still in the mortal and frail body, you feel the pains.’ He showed me the quality of love, and the suffering of love, and how He suffers in His creatures without pain <note>Johanna is describing a mystical paradox: God participates in human suffering out of love, yet as a divine being, He remains beyond physical agony.</note>. I cannot better describe this vision; but even a heart as hard as rock would have had to convert, if it had heard God speak thus and seen what I have seen, and so forth.”

## Chapter Ten

**Her longing for Paradise. High prayer and transformation in GOD, wherein she loses sight of her sins and her virtues. God's love toward humanity. Jesus as her heart. The wound in His side as her bridal chamber, and His heart as the bridal bed.**

->1.<-

The preceding account was primarily cited to show what intimate access she had to God and what power her prayer held with Him; now we must also recount several other graces with which she was gifted by God in her little chamber <note>The "Kämmerlein" refers to a private room for prayer and contemplation, often associated with Matthew 6:6.</note>:

In the year 1626, on the 13th of February, as she looked through the window at the firmament and the stars in the evening, she was seized by a mighty flame of divine love. This placed her in such a vehement longing for Paradise that, breaking out into weeping and sobbing, she could say nothing else but, "Paradise! Paradise!" For she felt both the presence of God in her heart and saw Him in spirit in heavenly glory.

2. On the 24th of October of this same year, she wrote the following concerning her state to her spiritual guide:

> “In order to fulfill my obedience, my Father, I write to you the manner and way of my prayer in which I practice—not indeed of myself, but as God governs me and leads me to Himself; although otherwise, as much as is in me, I seek to keep to the common path <note>The "common path" refers to standard, structured liturgical or meditative prayer used by most believers, as opposed to extraordinary mystical states.</note>; yet I cannot resist the great God, who deals with His creatures and works in them according to His will. My life is then a perpetual prayer.
> 
> “Regarding the actual designated time for prayer, I initially bow myself with shame before God and beneath all men. And in this vision of my nothingness, I say with the Patriarch: My God, I will speak with Thee, although I am but dust and ashes <note>original: "ob ich gleich Staub und Asche bin" — a reference to Abraham’s words to God in Genesis 18:27.</note>. And such I say with the renunciation of all confidence in myself, into which I am led by the inward love that I feel in the depths of my heart. This fills me so completely with confidence that, when I emerge from this vision of my nothingness, I see myself immersed in a certain light—which is indeed not visible, but yet is clearer and more radiant than any created light may be. And therein I do nothing myself, except that I surrender myself to God, because I have forsaken everything that is in the world. I feel that I am being made alive by an inexpressible Good, namely by the love of my heavenly Bridegroom, with whom I see myself united; there I find nothing

This vision gives the soul such a great love for GOD and such a great knowledge of its own nothingness <note>In mystical theology, "nothingness" (Nichts) refers to the realization that the soul has no independent existence or goodness apart from God.</note> that it seems impossible that one could elevate oneself over any virtue practiced, or over any praise from men, because everything outside of GOD is nothing. What I say here are only incidental things during my prayer; as for the prayer itself—how GOD speaks with me, and how I speak with GOD, and the enjoyment of GOD in prayer, and what occurs therein—I cannot make that understood at all; I can only say this much: that the principal act (although it is no act, but I use this word to make myself understood) or the main thing that occurs between GOD and me is nothing other than love; in which love I would remain for three times twenty-four hours <note>Seventy-two hours, or three full days.</note> (if it were possible for me to be so long without eating, drinking, and sleeping) without growing weary of this prayer; and when I have finished, I find myself ready to begin anew.

4. “Sometimes I see the Bridegroom as a bridegroom with his bride, and I speak with GOD as with my Bridegroom; love brings about this intimacy; I forget everything that is base in me and see nothing but GOD in me, and myself in GOD, through a transformation of love. Sometimes I also see and taste the holy humanity of my Bridegroom in the Divinity; sometimes I speak with Him as in His childhood; sometimes as to my Father. This way I have always had.

5. “Regarding what I have said, that I could no longer see my sins except outside of GOD and outside of myself, this is always the case for me, even when I am not [specifically] in prayer; therefore my sins are so terrible to me that I can no longer look upon the least of them. So it also happens with a devout soul; however good its deeds and life may be, it is yet far too poor a garment to enjoy the embraces and the unions of her heavenly King; therefore, after the divine Bridegroom to

### of Johanna von Cambry. Chapter X.

> “...this poor soul, this peasant girl <note>original: "Baurendirne." In mystical literature, the "peasant" or "beggar" represents the soul's humility and lack of spiritual "wealth" before God.</note>, whom He has chosen as His bride, does her best to adorn herself with her clothes through her strengths and virtuous exercises, and applies all her possible effort to please her beloved JESUS; so He finally, after He has wedded her, wishes to clothe her with His royal garments; He lets her put off her peasant clothes—that is, her virtues—to clothe her with His graces, with His intimate love, and other gifts which are impossible to recount in full. From this arises such intimate communion and familiarity that she embraces her GOD. I use this word ‘embrace’ because I do not know how else to make this perfect union understood. See there, how I find myself now; I cannot make this manner of my prayer understood in any other way than only by saying the incidental things <note>original: "das Zufällige." In theological terms, these are the outward details or secondary sensations of an experience, rather than its core essence.</note> that accompany it, and even those I say crudely enough. To GOD be the glory, and to me the shame!”

6. One day God let her see the manifold effects of His love toward His creatures: how through this love He carries the sinners, and how lovingly He leads those who already stand in His grace out of their blindness and failings. The Lord also let her see how, through this same love, He holds back the devils, who otherwise would do infinitely more evil; by which she was moved to great compassion for poor sinners and to heartfelt prayer for them. She also saw the greatness of the love with which her Bridegroom cried out from the wood of the cross: *Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.* <note>A reference to Luke 23:34.</note> Thus Johanna, out of wonder at everything God had given her to see, cried out: “O God! O Love! what have I deserved, that You let me see Your love in such a way? I am entirely unworthy of it.” But the Lord answered: “The bride must see the secrets of the bridegroom.” These words made her heart melt, as it were, in divine love.

7. In December of this same year, she fell into an ecstasy one afternoon, where she saw her own heart and the little Jesus resting in its center as if on His bed; and it seemed to her as if her heart were no longer her own, but Jesus’ heart, and the heart of Jesus had become her heart. Through this vision she was ignited with the most intimate fervor of love, and from that time on she always maintained the habit of calling Jesus “her heart,” without thinking of her own lowliness.

8. At this point, I am reminded of another (a) excellent discourse by this deeply experienced person, which she set down some years earlier, concerning the spiritual bridal chamber and the bridal bed of JESUS and the faithful soul, from which I must insert something here to stir up love.

There this banquet is held, where the soul, according to its full desire, partakes of unbelievable delicacies. There it sucks in this lovely blood.”

# Twelfth Piece. The Life

> “In this opened wound <note>The wound in the side of Jesus, a central focus of medieval and early modern devotion, representing a doorway to His heart.</note> she makes her dwelling; and whoever wants to find her must go there and seek her there. This is the chamber where the beloved soul reveals her love, where, as if completely intoxicated, they carry on a thousand conversations of love; she contemplates the beauties of the Beloved according to her desire, enjoying His goodness and loveliness. For it is here that the sweet JESUS, through His love, encloses her most intimately within His side, and He caresses and He kisses her; He speaks to her a thousand divine words of love until the soul is completely filled and says to Him: ‘My heart, it is enough! My heart, it is enough!’ Love now has no further law; love has no more restraint <note>original: "Respect." Here meaning the formal distance or social boundaries usually kept between a subject and a king.</note> in this chamber; for after she has drunk of this lovely wine—namely, of this divine blood—according to her full desire, and has become intoxicated, she has no further rule in this secret conversation with GOD. The soul speaks of nothing but love; all her longing is love, her breathing is love; there is nothing there but love. So let us love, then, let us drink, let us live, and let us die for love in this chamber of the opened wound in the side of JESUS. Let this be our chamber and our burial place; in this burial place the soul is dead to all things of the world; she cares no longer for anything created, nor does she long for any other dwelling but this holy chamber. Well then, dearest souls, let us seek this chamber and beg the Bridegroom that He may open the portal for us and let us enter; and when we have gone inside, let us never come out again, and so forth.
> 
> 9. “Now that the wedding has been held, after they have eaten, drunk, and become intoxicated with heavenly delights, one must also go to bed; but what kind of bed shall be found for this bride? Truly none other than the divine Heart of JESUS. Yes, in this beloved, sweet Heart of JESUS the soul shall lay herself down to rest; with it the soul is united, and from two hearts only one single heart shall become through the union of love, and so forth.
> 
> “O divine Heart! what do You see in this evil and ungrateful creature that You love it so? It is only Your piercing and burning love which makes You love Your poor creature—the work of Your hands—in such a way! Since GOD then loves what He has made, why should we ungrateful ones not love Him who made us? He who allows us to love Him, who invites us to it, indeed commands us that we should love Him with all our heart, with all our soul, and with all our strength: oh! what is easier than to love such a good GOD? A GOD who is so in love with our souls? Oh! how is it possible that so few fulfill this sweet commandment? and so forth.”

->I.<-

**B**ut so that we may resume the sequence of this history: it happened not long after Johanna had received the aforementioned ecstasy <note>A state of mystical rapture where the soul is perceived to be outside the body or in direct union with the divine.</note> that she fell into great inner darkness and suffering; and then the doubts of her guide <note>Her spiritual director or confessor. In this era, women mystics were required to have a male director to "discern" if their visions were truly from God.</note> regarding her condition began again. Instead of supporting her, he only placed her in even greater distress. Toward the end of the year 1626, she wrote the following to him:

> “It seems to me that you are in doubt whether this secret operation of love in
> “me could persist amidst these darknesses? I wish to answer this and make
> “known to you the state of my soul: I love **GOD** just as fervently on Mount
> “Calvary <note>The site of Christ’s crucifixion; represents a state of spiritual suffering and desolation.</note> as on Mount Tabor <note>The site of the Transfiguration; represents a state of spiritual glory and consolation.</note>. Now I love Him on Mount
> “Calvary, where He hangs on the cross; yes, I love Him as wounded, torn, and
> “crowned with thorns; I love Him in His soul-pains, as abandoned by **GOD**
> “His Father; I love Him among the blasphemies and judgments of His creatures;
> “I love Him, and I throw myself into His arms, completely permeated with
> “pain; yes, finally in His death, where I, nailed to the cross in His arms,
> “desire to die with Him; I love Him in the darkness of the elements, where
> “the sun and the moon are darkened; I love Him during the earthquake; in short, I
> “love Him in all those darknesses which were seen at His holy death.

2. “I love this **GOD** of love, as much in the darkness as in the light, as
> “much in tribulations as in consolations, as much when He strikes, hits, and
> “cuts me, as when He caresses me with His divine consolations, enticements, divine
> “enlightenments, and other glorious graces.

> “Now I am on Mount Calvary, where the taste of His heavenly lights is darkened

### Of Johanna von Cambry. Chapter XI.

“...given to understand; and that I only wanted to leave my convent so that I might have my **freedom**, etc. Now it is known to God with what truth and faithfulness I have everywhere sought His honor and my salvation; both when I left my convent, and when I left the city of Menen <note>original: "Menain"; a town in Flanders where Johanna had previously lived.</note>, when I fled the honor that was offered to me, so that I might be poor in solitude; I left the world and fled the marriage that was offered to me, indeed, to which they wanted to force me; I allowed my body no delights or comforts; shall I then now lose my crown because of the imperfections that I do not have in my power to overcome through <term>mortifications</term> <note>Mortifications are spiritual exercises or acts of self-denial used to discipline the body and "kill" worldly desires.</note>? I see that you weigh them heavily, and that you therefore doubt the graces that God shows me through His goodness. Oh, what! what should I do then? I told you from the beginning that I had imperfections, and I say it still; I do not believe that I will ever be rid of them [here on earth]; I am a **child of Adam**, I carry an imperfect nature within me, which I will likely keep until my grave. Meanwhile, I see that you waver; I notice it quite well; but what should I do? Should I also let my courage sink, when I see that my guide, who should lead me to heaven, is in doubt about my state? Truly, dear Father, I am quite distressed.”

> 5. “On the other side of grace, I feel burning desires for God, and behold, this is my struggle. How can fire and water agree with each other? How dare I think of the things that are above, when I am sunk into such a dark sea of so many terrible temptations and cruel attacks of the devils? For my state is such that at one and the same time I am sunk in such struggles, while the heart is united with God. The mouth speaks, the **lower parts** <note>The "lower parts" (untere Theile) refers to the sensory or animal nature of a human, which mystics believed could experience temptation even while the "higher" soul remained pure and focused on God.</note> revolt, but the heart says: My God, I do not want this, I abhor sin, I testify and vow that I never want to offend You. I praise God, I perform an act of love for God, and I feel myself truly inflamed in His love at that moment. And that is what causes me such great distress, namely, that I see through the lower parts such **cruel beasts** <note>A metaphorical description of intrusive thoughts or physical temptations.</note>, which are contrary to pure love, pass through, and that despite all this, I remain united with God, and the spirit stands elevated toward Him. I marvel at my state, and I wonder what God wants of me. I tell you only the very least of it, for it is impossible for me to say everything, no, not even the thousandth part of what goes on. I pray you, consider it: is it fair that I remain unhelped?”

6. I break off from these tiresome dealings which our Saint had with her guide, of which much more could otherwise be reported; more follows later. He was called a **soul-leader** <note>original: "Seelenführer"; the standard term for a spiritual director.</note>, but he was truly more her **soul-confuser** <note>original: "Seelenverwirrer"; a play on words by the author to criticize the director's lack of understanding.</note>, however well-meaning he might otherwise have been; and so it goes when one does not heed the Apostle's warning that not everyone should undertake to be teachers. Meanwhile, for those who love God and seek Him in sincerity, all things must work together for their salvation; God uses all kinds of artists to make a saint; let whoever can help, help them to become small and pure.

Twelfth Part. The Life

7. Finally, it happened on the last day of March 1627, that she was suddenly freed from all her sufferings in such a way that her small room was filled with God and the saints of heaven, just as it had previously seemed to her to be filled with nothing but evil spirits. The Lord spoke these words to her: **"Love me, my daughter, and continue to love me; your love is pleasing to Me."**

## The Twelfth Chapter.

**The dying Jesus looks upon His own. A vision of the Wisdom and Justice of God. Extraordinary sufferings. She appeases God’s righteous anger against the world. Three books in which she studies. Opening of the earthly Paradise.**

---

->I.<-

---

On the 10th of April, it was given to her to understand how the kind Jesus, at the time of His death, had looked upon every soul in particular. She also had a vision of the special love which the Lord had for each of those souls who were to be saved and be a fruit of His suffering, and that He had felt joy over them; however, over those who would not make use of His suffering, He felt the greatest of pains.

2. On the evening of the 6th of September, God showed her the secrets of His Wisdom and Justice in a most wonderful way, so that Johanna cried out:
> "O! O! O! wonderful God! How have I, alas, so often wavered in my judgment regarding the dark ways of divine decrees? Now I see it, to my shame, down to every iota <note>original: "jota"; the smallest letter of the alphabet, meaning the smallest detail.</note>, that everything God allows to happen to His creatures is well done, and that right and justice are done to all creatures in everything that happens to them, and that they have no reason to complain at all."

3. On the 11th of this month, she wrote the following: 
> "When the Spirit of God reveals the failings of a neighbor to a soul, that soul feels within itself a sense of love, kindness, and compassion for the neighbor, and finds itself compelled to pray to God for them; but if these signs are not present, then it is very much to be doubted that such a revelation of a neighbor's failings comes from God. Indeed, God can sometimes prompt a devout soul to ask Him that a sinner might be punished; however, this always happens with love and compassion, and the punishment aims only at what is physical and temporal so that the soul may be preserved, which is a great mercy of God toward a sinner."

4. On the morning of the 12th of this month, she found herself entirely dry, dark, and in extreme sadness and suffering, as if all of hell had been stirred up against her,

### Of Johanna von Cambry. Chapter XII.

...without her being able to find a cause for it. In this state, she offered herself up to God, willing to be in whatever condition it might please Him to place her; it was then given to her to understand how she must serve God in faith and in the practice of virtues, without leaning upon extraordinary divine lights <note>original: "sonderbare göttliche Lichter"; these refer to mystical insights or visions that provide intellectual clarity.</note>; for where one could see and taste, there was no faith.

5. The Lord dealt with her in such a way quite often, namely that He always humbled her either immediately before or after a special grace was shown to her, through certain states of abandonment <note>original: "Verlassungen"; a common mystical term for the feeling of being deserted by God, often called the "dark night of the soul."</note>, so that she had to be comforted by someone, even if it were only a little child.

6. > "On the 18th of September, as I wished to pray (she says), my spirit was led before God, and I saw myself and all the children of men before God. I saw God above the clouds with a sword in His hand, ready to execute His judgment upon all sinners; I was urged to pray for the whole world, but could do nothing else but cry out in spirit: Mercy! Mercy! And it seemed to me that I offered all the merits of the sufferings of Jesus to God and showed Him His wounds; whereupon it appeared to me as if the Lord let His anger subside and took us all into His mercy. Immediately I came to myself again and found that I was dissolving in tears, and my whole body trembled; indeed, it still does so as I write this. Thereupon our God drew me to Himself, into a gentle rest and union of love; He comforted me regarding what He had shown me and also exhorted me to continue in such intercession. For this I praised God and showed Him that reciprocal love which He Himself had granted me; for looking at myself, I saw myself as far too wretched."

7. Around this same time, her director <note>original: "Führer"; her spiritual guide or confessor.</note> requested that she should give him an account of her state; which she then did through a letter, of which an extract follows here:

> "My Father! The way through which God leads me is unknown to me, and I do not know where I am going; I only surrender myself to Him to follow the movements of His guidance. Regarding those temptations and imperfections which are unknown to me, as soon as I recognize them, I have a great desire to annihilate them and to do what is most pleasing to God, even should it cost me my life. Nevertheless, the kind God does not cease—regardless of all these my imperfections—to gift me with His graces, although because of my unworthiness I deserve hell much more than the caresses of God. For when I see myself so far removed from the perfection which is required for such graces as He shows me, and I am ashamed and humbled before God because of it; then He shows me my failings, and as if He wished to excuse me, He comforts me and encourages me to serve Him. This then causes me to be even more ashamed and to love Him more, because of His so great goodness toward me."

### Twelfth Section. The Life

8. "Know, my Father! that the kind God has given me (a) three books, so that I may constantly read, study, and find all kinds of nourishment within them; without these books, I could not have endured what I have suffered for a year now, during which I have emerged victorious in the battles against evil spirits.

"The First is the book of the mystery of the holy Trinity, toward which God draws me, but in quite a different way than in former times; for when I am presently in prayer, and am sunken into this great and incomprehensible mystery, I see within it His infinite and eternal essence, and therein I lose myself, along with the memory and the knowledge of my corrupt nature <note>original: "verderbten Natur"; a theological term referring to the state of humanity after the Fall, prone to sin.</note> and my own being. I do not mean by this an ecstasy <note>original: "Entzückung"; typically refers to a state of being overwhelmed by divine joy or visions.</note>, but rather a losing of the entire soul and its powers through a completely secret working of God; I cannot describe it otherwise than that I am lost outside of myself and in God.

"After God has raised me up in such a manner, to Himself and into Himself, He lets me set my foot upon the earth again; that is, He gives back to me the knowledge and memory of the created nature of man and of myself; and then I see how this created nature, in the midst of the uncreated essence, is in the eternal and infinite God—just as if there were a foot’s breadth of land in the middle of the sea. Even so is created nature in the middle of this immeasurable sea of uncreated essence, where I look upon the whole world in spirit, and all creatures that have ever been, as a tiny point in the midst of the essence of the eternal God.

9. "The second book is the book of the sufferings of the Son of God, in which book I find the life of the soul and the body, in all the opened holy wounds of the sweetest *Jesus*. In this book, I find power and strength to endure what I have to suffer; with this, God nourishes me; and this is the retreat <note>original: "Retirade"; a place of refuge or a military-style defensive position.</note> where He leads me.

"It has now been two years since the Beloved led me into the wound of His holy side, and since then I have not gone out from there, however unworthy a creature I may be; and presently, God leaves open to me all the chambers of His holy wounds. We all otherwise believe these mysteries which are hidden in these three books, but presently, as God draws me to Himself, these books are always open to me through a vision and a knowledge the likes of which I never had before. And even though the Beloved occasionally shows me other mysteries—whether it be that I have Him in my heart as in His childhood, or that I see Him in His glorious Resurrection, or in another way—it always happens without my leaving the chamber of His sufferings.

"It is true, I am a sinner, and have my imperfections, such as you (b) see in me; since it is also not possible for me to do more than I do my-

"...to bring the same to death: it seems to me a mystery of God lies beneath it. I know not why God leaves me in this state; for, concerning my will, I would regard neither health, nor life, nor death, if only to banish from myself whatever I think might be displeasing to Him.

10. The third book is the book of the world and of the works of God, which are always open to me, that I may see the wonders of God therein. Sometimes I look at heaven and earth for two or three hours, and I see everything on earth blooming with the highest pleasure and without weariness. I cannot refrain from saying something extraordinary that sometimes happens to me, and indeed for a month now: namely, when I look at the sky, the earth, and everything that turns green on earth, the blooming and fruit-bearing trees, I visibly see in all this a certain clarity <note>original: "Klarheit"; here referring to a supernatural radiance or divine light perceived within the physical world.</note>, not like the clarity of the sun, the moon, the stars or planets, but a thousand times more beautiful; and this clarity pours itself through the whole air, through all trees and plants with a wonderful serenity, which gives my soul such great joy, delight, and comfort, that I could well look at this clarity for entire days, even entire weeks on end, if this vision should last so long. But I do not have this whenever I want, but rather when it pleases God, sometimes for an hour, sometimes two hours, sometimes even longer. See there, how I read in these three books, and how it stands now with my soul."

Twelfth Part. The Life

> "...say that you have not fulfilled the purpose for which God sent you here; namely, that we should act uprightly regarding God and our perfection, and how it displeased God that this has not happened. Know that God allows this to be said to you with great love, as He who well knows what adversaries you have had, and also knows our strengths, which are nothing without Him. You know better than I how one must work in God through the complete surrender of one’s judgment and will to God; do not complain that God reveals this to me. Be on your guard, however, and keep watch <note>The "watch" or "sentinel" is a common mystical metaphor for maintaining constant spiritual alertness against temptation.</note>; for the devil wishes to sift you <note>A biblical allusion to Luke 22:31, where Jesus tells Peter that Satan has asked to "sift you as wheat."</note>, as well as me; but we have God with us, who shields us at every moment; and if we call upon Him in truth and with firm faith, He will never leave us.
> 
> "Forgive me for speaking thus, and if henceforth I speak with you in a different tone for the glory of God than is usual: recognize the paths through which God leads me; for there are mysteries in all of this, which I bring to your notice for your information.
> 
> "God has imposed it upon me that I should take a special care for your soul. I know well that God has also imposed upon you the care of my soul; I also remain your child forever, and I consider myself in every way unworthy to be a footstool for your feet. But if I now henceforth—according to the rule of love, by which God has in turn imposed upon me the care for your soul—speak with you about the state of your souls, according to what God may inspire in me or command me; then do not wonder at it at all, for it shall only serve for our perfection and be intended for that purpose."

2. > "As I was in prayer this morning, I complained to God about the fact that He willed that I should behave toward you in such a manner and say this to you; I represented to Him that He knew well how much I wished to be a child, and that as a child I have always been so willingly obedient to my leader <note>original: "Führer"; referring to her spiritual director or confessor.</note>; why then did He presently want me to turn it around, and no longer speak as a child? Thereupon God said to me in the depth of my soul: He would have it so; whereupon I then replied: Well, my God, I will do it.
> 
> "Therefore, I must indeed give you this notice: afterward we will deal with one another concerning everything that pertains to the interior life <term>interior life: the hidden spiritual life of the soul in its relationship with God, as opposed to outward religious practice.</term>; of the most secret ways of uniting oneself with God; of those difficulties that arise in regard to nature <note>In this context, "nature" refers to human impulses, ego, and physical inclinations that often conflict with spiritual growth.</note>; how one must go to work with it so that it may serve the spirit; when the soul can be united with God without images <note>This refers to "apophatic" or "image-less" prayer, a high state of contemplation where the mind lets go of all mental pictures and concepts to meet God in "divine darkness."</note>; how one may attain perfection and union with God, even if one does not feel this inner fire in the depth of the soul; and in a word, of many internal matters, by which we would have already been far advanced toward the end if we had done as I have so often told you, and as it was the will of God; but God will direct it for the good, and so I hope that we will find again what we have lost."

### of Johanna von Cambry. Chapter XIII.

“Well then, my dear Father <note>Johanna is addressing her spiritual director, a priest.</note>, what shall hinder us so that this earth of ours does not burn? Since God loves us so much, why do we not melt away in His holy love? Let us set out toward God and toward the perfection to which God calls us: help me to run, and I will be of assistance to you, because God wills it so.

3. On the 30th of this month, she wrote the following, among other things, to her guide:

> “When God commands me something, I say: Well, my God, I will do it. Yes, **My Heart**, I will do it. I am so carried away that I say: **My Heart**, without thinking about it, because God wills it so. Afterward, it comes to my mind that you forbade it to me; I was not to call God **My Heart**; regardless of this, God makes me say it without thinking about it; love carries the spirit away. I then also say: My God, my guide will not want to believe me. But He answers: Do your duty by telling him. See there, my Father, what has occurred, which is not without hidden mysteries: I tell it to you so that I keep no burden upon myself. Do not reject the simple and external exercises [or means] to go to God, nor some small devotions: God makes Himself a child with him who becomes a child; and from there He raises the soul <term>Gemüth: refers here to the inner disposition or spirit</term> to great things that even exceed our capacity for understanding. Ah! if only I could tell you what I see, and what a great good would have fallen to our lot if we had taken the short path <note>The "short path" is a common mystical term for direct union with God through surrender, often contrasted with long, labor-intensive religious rituals.</note> a year ago, as God wanted it: well, I hope that God will let it serve for the best for both you and me, etc.

4. However, all her heartfelt presentations must have found very little reception, either with her guide or with others, as is evident from the following:

> “On October 5th, I complained to God in prayer that He commanded me to tell men His holy will, yet I achieved nothing by it, because men do not understand what God wants and also could not comprehend His workings in me: therefore, I thought it would be better if I remained silent? But our gracious God gave me this answer: **There would yet be those who should understand me; He would give them light. Afterward He spoke the following words to me: I am compelled to make myself common <note>Meaning "to make Himself familiar or accessible."</note> with the little ones and with simple daughters: because the little ones open the door of their hearts to me. But the wise, to whom I have given knowledge, blind themselves through the natural light <note>Natural light refers to human reason and intellectual learning, as opposed to divine revelation.</note> that I have given them, and keep their gate closed to the supernatural light that I wish to communicate to them.**

5. A few days later, she received a command from God that she should say to her guide that as often as he had dealt so severely with her, he had caused suffering to God within her and had grieved Him. In the beginning, he had led her rightly for several years; but after she had been sufficiently tested, he should let God work in the soul, and the soul...

“...great distress; moreover, the evil spirits made use of this matter and were always whispering to me: ‘You are damned; your guide says so, and because he says it, you are damned.’ I, for my part, found my conscience quite calm through all of this; nevertheless, because of what my guide had written, the devilry had great power to shake me and cast me down, as God had left me to myself for three weeks. I begged God from the bottom of my heart that He might preserve me from despair; I would rather die than offend Him and falsely claim His graces for myself, etc. Then God spoke to my poor soul: ‘My daughter, be comforted, you are my dearly beloved; I am more to you than all creatures.’ As I was still standing in fear that my guide might bring me into disgrace and slander among the people—because of the suspicion he had against me, as if I were being deceived by the devil, just as other unwise guides had done to me twenty-four years ago—God showed me in the spirit and said: ‘That all slanders and all praise of creatures are as a pure nothing.’ I saw also that God was everything to me; these words of God brought such a benefit to my soul, as if He had moved me from hell into heaven; a grace which, with God's help, I shall not forget my whole life long. Oh, what does all the judging of men matter? I say with <term>Saint Susanna</term> <note>A biblical figure from the Book of Daniel who, when falsely accused, declared it better to fall into God's hands than to sin by following the will of men.</note>, it is better to fall into the hands of God than into the hands of men.

2. It is surprising how, despite all this, the dear Johanna was some time later placed into new sufferings and <term>scruples</term> <note>In a religious context, "scruples" refers to obsessive anxiety that one has committed a sin where none exists, or a persistent doubt about the state of one's soul.</note> by her inexperienced guide, even concerning these assurances received from God, until God once more gave her to understand that He alone was the true judge. ‘In Him alone’ (these are her words) ‘should I place my trust; before Him henceforward should I bring my complaint; I should not complain to men.’ He also gave me to understand that if I were His dearly beloved, I must also die just as He died. Whereby I was again comforted, yet my nature was horrified that I should no longer complain, since I found myself in such bitter suffering and was contested by both devils and men; but the LORD drew me once again to Himself and showed me that He alone was the certain, faithful, and unchangeably steadfast one, whereas all creatures were but vanity and inconstancy.

3. ‘On December 19th, God showed me that the inner acts of a living faith were very pleasing to Him, and that we must practice them everywhere and in all things; even if one had visions, revelations, and inner comforts, one must not dwell on them as if they were the end goal of these graces. In such a way, a soul can walk in peace with God, and He would then infallibly help her, even if the devil should want to disguise himself as an angel of light.’ This is the certain way that God has shown me: that one should cling to God through the inner acts of a living faith, above all lights, visions, and revelations. To Him be the glory, and to me the shame!’

# Twelfth Part. The Life

„from now on drawn to do what God wants of me; that is, that I devote myself to the **Interior** <term>Inward life: the mystical practice of focusing one's attention on the presence of God within the soul</term>. Also I am compelled to tell him, my **Father** <note>original: "Pater," referring to her spiritual director</note>, that if he is not of a mind to fulfill the content of the writings he has there, and to set his hand to the work, he should only send them back to me again; they retain the freedom to do it or not, I say it only with simplicity, as I feel it, so that I may unburden myself of it; I do not trust myself, and I do not mistrust myself, I leave it to him and his judgment. Concerning my **Interior**, I abandon myself to the will of God, who knows the ground of my soul and all my thoughts. He knows whether I seek His honor or my own. I lean upon His great goodness, above all **creatures** <note>In this context, "creatures" refers to all created things or people, as opposed to the Creator</note>. 5. This letter could not possibly please her leader, and just as he was already standing in temptation against her, he was brought even more **to arms** <note>original: "ins Harnisch," an idiom meaning to be incensed or provoked to anger</note> against her by this, so that she simply had to remain silent and suffer again.

6. On March 6, 1628, she wrote the following to the same man: „My dear Father, since I see that he takes everything from me so poorly, it happened this morning, as I had lifted my mind in prayer to God, that I found myself powerfully urged to report the following to him; he may take it how he will.

„I was namely in worries as to how I should behave according to the will of God, in view of all the evil opinions that you have conceived of me, even even of my chastity; afterwards, as I was in prayer and had let all these thoughts fall, I found myself with God, and I saw our **Savior** entirely wounded and bleeding before me, in the form in which He was scourged, with bound hands. Then He said to me in an audible way: **What compassion I have with you, with Me, and with the whole world!** At the same time, He gave me an impression in my mind that you would once again recognize the truth of my state; He also instructed me that I should always speak in love to you, as to the whole world. I also find in the ground of my soul a love for you; I pray for you, as has always happened before, and for the rest, let the vision be what it is; if it is the devil, he will be overcome: whoever practices love cannot err.

7. „On November 4th, as I was at my needlework in the afternoon, I received such a violent attack from the evil enemy, with temptation and sadness, that I had to leave my work and betake myself to prayer. I complained to the Savior and said: My God! You are truly a **Blood-Bridegroom** <term>Blood-Bridegroom: a mystical reference to Exodus 4:25, used here to describe a spiritual intimacy forged through intense suffering and sacrifice</term> to me. Yet in my complaining, I was composed and well-satisfied. But it was answered to me in the spirit: **Be comforted, my daughter, how can you then not endure until death?** At which words I was again entirely comforted, and at the same time became eager to suffer a thousand times more, if only I had the strength, so long as I did not offend God.

Along with this, I also saw the nature of the soul, and how it hovers here in darkness, and like a bird in a **cage** <note>original: "Kesicht," an archaic variant of "Käficht"</note>; and because it does not know its own nature, it is terrified by the things of the other world, and the memory that it must go there causes it anguish.„

### Twelfth Piece. The Life

"I still carry that very same love for you that I ever harbored for you before.
"You write that you do not doubt that I will yet be comforted by GOD, and plagued by men. Truly, my Father, I believe that GOD has given you to recognize my condition; for it is the truth, GOD comforts me more than ever before, and men also persecute me more than ever before.
"See, that is now my condition: I have a body and a soul, a spirit and a nature <note>In this context, "nature" refers to the physical, human impulses and the lower part of the psyche, as opposed to the "spirit" which communes with God.</note> about me; on the side of GOD, few days pass without the apex <note>original: "Spitze," the highest point of the soul where it connects with the divine</note> of my spirit receiving some light from GOD—indeed, one light after another; and there is no moment in the day in which I do not see GOD united with my soul. I see Him in a clear and certain light, in which I recognize such truths as are impossible for me to speak, and in the ground of my soul, I feel my heart in a perpetual movement of love for GOD, so that it seems as if it must break at every moment from the love I feel for my GOD, which is so intense that my heart is wounded by it; yes, I feel within it a sensible pain, which is further increased by the sight of the miserable state of the world, for which I must pray at the command of GOD, so that His just judgment might be turned away, etc.

"All the rest—namely, the powers of my soul, which are lower than this upper part—stand together with nature in unbelievable suffering. In view of the lower parts and nature, I am sunken in a sea of all desolation and bitterness, and besieged by a fierce struggle of the devils.

"Externally, I am attacked by the strangest persecutions from all men, for there are only two of them who have compassion for me. Nevertheless, I am well satisfied in all of this, and as long as it pleases GOD, I do not wish for a single moment to be otherwise, because in these darknesses down there, I see the **Sun of Justice** <note>A biblical reference to Malachi 4:2, often used by mystics to describe Christ's illuminating presence.</note> shining in the summit of my spirit, which penetrates with its rays into the ground of my soul, and there makes divine love fruitful. As often as nature falls down under the weight, I see that the kind GOD, through His fervent love, holds His gracious hand under my head <note>A reference to the Song of Solomon 2:6: "His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me."</note>, so that I am not injured; thus only nature falls, but the soul remains unharmed, because it has no other will than to please GOD, and does not wish to offend Him in any way. I see how my crucified GOD holds His arms open to me, into which I throw myself so lost, and thus I suffer, singing the praise of GOD in the midst of my suffering.

"I will explain it to you through a **parable**: The sun has its course in the heavens; it has all its light and clarity, even though it is often darkened down here by clouds, rain, snow, hail, and storm-winds; and when the earth is frozen or covered with snow, this only prepares it to bear much better fruit in the spring. So it also happens with my soul; GOD, as the **Sun of Justice**, shines in the summit of my spirit; He has His firm seat in this my heart, in my will; all around He lets His storms rage, and this will happen until the heat of the love of the Sun of Right- <meta>catchword: -eousness (completing "Gerechtigkeit")</meta>

2. To the very same person <note>Likely her spiritual director or confessor, to whom she reported her internal life.</note>, she wrote the following, among other things, in June of the year 1632:

„I greet you in the loving heart of JESUS, so that I may satisfy your desire, since you wish to know the state of my soul; I have already made known to you the terrifying persecutions of N. <note>In 17th-century spiritual biographies, "N." was commonly used to anonymize names, often representing an antagonist, a specific critic, or a person in authority.</note>, for which you have also comforted me. Regarding the present state of my soul, I will tell you the pure truth: it consists of two points, namely, suffering and the enjoyment <term>Enjoyment: In the context of mystical theology, "enjoyment" (derived from the Latin *fruitio*) refers to the soul's direct, experiential delight in God's presence, rather than just intellectual belief.</term> of my loving JESUS, who possesses my heart and my soul.

<margin>(a) Psalm 43:1.</margin>
„Regarding the sufferings, it would be a true abyss if I were to recount the terrifying persecutions I endure; it is not possible to express them. When at times their intensity forces me to complain a little to my friends, I only mention the outward aspects, for otherwise it would not be believed; and so I endure it with my GOD and complain to Him, throwing myself into His gracious hands, and so I accept everything that people may do to me. I say: 'My GOD, men would have no power over me if it were not given to them from above;' and when I see that many pious people believe the false accusations made against me, I say: 'Judge (a) me, O GOD, and plead my cause against the unholy nation, and deliver me from the deceitful and wicked people.' <note>The author translates Psalm 43:1 from Latin into German here: "Richte mich, Gott, und führe meine Sache aus wider das unheilige Volk, und reiß mich aus von den falschen und bösen Leuten."</note> This and other similar verses then comfort me. Since Easter, I have been so dreadfully persecuted that at times I did not know where to turn; then I threw myself down before GOD, weeping with loud sobs, and repeated my little verse mentioned above. Then our kind GOD opened His gracious arms, embraced me lovingly, and wiped away my tears, just as a mother does with her child, whereby I was then completely comforted. Since that time, I have never been so despondent again, but rather I have a strength to suffer even more than before. To be sure, as you well know, I have always had enough courage, through GOD’s grace, to suffer for His sake; however, I now have such a poor body, which is so utterly weakened and broken by the continuous suffering, that I would certainly need new strength from above, although I expect nothing else [but suffering] until my grave. The Son of GOD died on the cross; I too shall die on the cross. See, that is something of my sufferings.

3. „Regarding the enjoyment of GOD, I am somewhat ashamed to say anything, since I am such an unworthy little worm; but since Your Reverence knows that GOD is so good that it is to be attributed solely to His goodness, and not at all to any merit of man, that He unites Himself with us and with all those who open their hearts to Him, I will tell you just something of the ways through which GOD leads me:

# Twelfth Part. The Life

> „I have then, in any case, in my soul a vision of the malice of human nature, and another vision of the beauty of souls, created after the image of GOD. When I now look at what happens daily out of human frailty, I have not the slightest difficulty in bearing such things in every way among people, for I too am frail, and I bear such frailty with love; but the sin which happens out of malice is unbearable to me; I become (a) indignant over the malice of men, although in that very same moment I embrace them in my heart with a love of compassion for their souls, which are created after the image of GOD. Thus, one sees the indignation outwardly, but does not know its cause. Although even when I am so indignant, it happens only as if in passing, and does not last long at all, and comes merely from the vision of an extreme malice; I hate only the sin that happens out of malice, and I would also hate it in myself if I had it, from which may GOD preserve me. Concerning the vision that I have of the beauty of the human soul, created after the image of GOD, the same has such an impression on my mind that, according to the love I bear for GOD, with a single act of love, I enclose in my heart all people who are in the whole world. I cannot express how fervent this fire of love is within me. But for my friends, for the chosen souls drawn to GOD, I have a special little chamber in my heart; these I love together with my GOD. I cannot, however, show this to them outwardly, for one would not be able to understand how such a thing proceeds inwardly; indeed, I fear one would interpret it poorly and consider it a foolish <insert>impure</insert> love, which is not worthy of being called love, because there is only one love, namely, the love with which I love my GOD.
>
> 4. „The love I bear for my GOD is inexpressible, and my heart is truly wounded: concerning my prayer, the same is perpetual; when I work, when I eat, when I talk with people, or walk about in the chamber and carry out my poor housekeeping, my spirit is always with GOD; and my heart is always groaning and thirsting for love of GOD. When I pray aloud, it happens while standing or walking about, because since my heart stands in a perpetual act of the love of GOD, my spirit is immediately carried away—as soon as I kneel down—by this or that powerful effect of divine love, which I cannot resist. I also take my food standing or walking, for when I sit down and say the blessing over my meager food, behold, my spirit is raised to GOD in contemplation of the goodness He shows to me, an unworthy woman, that He nourishes my poor body and my soul; and so I then cannot eat, or my heart would fall into a faint <term>Faint: In mystical literature, a "faint" or "swoon" (leipothymia) describes a state where the physical senses are overwhelmed by the intensity of spiritual ecstasy.</term> for love of GOD. I sometimes think I shall die of it, and my heart fly away to GOD, so that I must cry out loud to give my heart some air again, which is an inexpressibly sweet martyrdom.
>
> 5. „For inward prayer <term>Inward prayer: Also known as "mental prayer" or "recollection," where the soul communicates with God without necessarily using spoken words.</term> I used to spend five or six hours of the day, indeed the whole night; but now I have only two hours of the day for it,

## The Sixteenth Chapter.

### The various dwellings and the Cabinet of Souls. The state of nakedness, in total divestment of all trust in self and one's works, and bare trust in GOD alone: In which she blessedly died and went to GOD.

->1.<-

<margin>(a) Chapter LXIX.</margin>
And see, thus was also the life of this saint <term>hidden with Christ in GOD</term><note>A reference to the New Testament verse Colossians 3:3, often used by mystics to describe a life focused entirely on the internal presence of the divine rather than outward appearance.</note>. A worldly eye certainly saw no form in her that would have pleased it: she was an imprisoned, poor, weak, old, sickly woman, persecuted and abandoned by everyone until her death, so that most probably held her life to be insane and her end a disgrace, and might still hold it so. But how exceedingly glorious was this king's daughter within—yes, this royal bride! Her body had only a narrow, poor little hut for its lodging, but her spirit was translated into the heavenly essence; she was led to the King in his innermost <term>Cabinet</term><note>In the 17th century, a "cabinet" was a small, private room for prayer, study, or the storage of treasures. In mystical writing, it refers to the deepest center of the soul where God dwells.</note>, and rested with Him in the bridal chamber, as she spoke of it so movingly here and there from her own experience. In her last writing, called *The Mystical Torch* <note>Original: *La Flambeau Mystique*, Cambry's final treatise on the stages of the spiritual life.</note>, she describes (a) the various dwellings and the Cabinet of Souls in such a way that one can well feel she must have seen with her own eyes what she proclaims to us. I will yet share a passage from it, especially since otherwise no further reports remain of these last years of her life.

### Twelfth Part. The Life
<meta>catchword: „GOD’s</meta>

3. „Let us speak of this in order, and first of the **beginners**; their chamber is this: they have natural gifts, or workings of **nature**, which are, however, helped by **grace**, through which they then **mortify** <note>original: "mortificiren"; the practice of subduing physical desires and the five senses to focus on the spiritual.</note> their five outer senses, and the natural inclination, which previously went toward the world, is now directed toward **GOD**. For one must begin by giving nature over to **GOD**, and becoming faithful with a good will to the holy convictions when **GOD** knocks at the door of our heart, so that He may lead the soul into the first chamber, where she receives a complete sorrow over her sins, and has a desire to arrange her life according to the will of **GOD**.

4. The second chamber for the **advanced**, is this: When **GOD** draws the soul to Himself through spiritual gifts of grace, such as the gift of inward **prayer**, of **contemplation**, and the like, with which **mortification** <note>original: "Absterbung"; literally "dying-away" to the self and worldly attachments.</note> is always paired. In this chamber, the soul walks with her dearly beloved **JESUS**; she embraces and she kisses Him; but these are still imperfect kisses, because she has not yet been led into the bridal chamber.

5. „In the third chamber, which belongs to the **perfect**, there are experienced supernatural graces, unions, spiritual intoxications, ecstasies, and the like. Here the Bridegroom receives His dearly beloved with a perfect kiss; however, she does not enter into this chamber otherwise than with pages and lackeys; her lackey, who goes everywhere with her, is **mortification**; and her page, who always goes before her, is **humility**.

6. „But let us now also speak a little of the **Cabinet** <note>In the 17th century, a "Cabinet" was the most private room in a palace, used for intimate conversation or deep study.</note>, into which the Bridegroom leads His bride; where He speaks with her **mouth to mouth** <note>A biblical idiom (from Numbers 12:8) signifying direct, unmediated communication between God and a person.</note>, where He embraces her, and kisses her, where He shares with her His precious jewels, the golden chains, rubies, and diamonds. I understand by the **golden chains**, the workings of love; by the **rubies**, the sight of the transfigured humanity of the Son of **GOD**, the wounds of His side, His hands, and His feet, etc.; by the **diamonds**, the sight of the shining whiteness and purity of the humanity of **JESUS**. This Cabinet of the heavenly Bridegroom is now the **Godhead**, into which the soul is swallowed up and led by **GOD**, and there she speaks with **GOD** mouth to mouth; that is, the created essence of the soul unites with the uncreated essence; and there **GOD** lets the soul, His dearly beloved, see through an everlasting vision the secrets of His uncreated wisdom, of the uncreated essence of **GOD**, of the unity of the three persons, the holy **Trinity**, of the humanity which is united with the Godhead, of the glory of this humanity joined with the Godhead; in short, everything that is in **GOD**, and what **GOD** permits her to see, not through **speculation** <note>In mystical theology, "speculation" refers to intellectual or theoretical study, as opposed to "enjoyment" (fruition), which is direct, experiential union.</note>, but in an enjoyable manner.

7. „The embraces of the Bridegroom in this Cabinet cannot be explained otherwise than by saying that this embrace is an enjoyable knowledge of all the works of **GOD** outside of nature, and just as they are in **GOD**; and then also just as they are in their nature and in their natural workings, according to the decree

## Of Johanna von Cambry. Chapter XVI.
->Kkk 2<-
<meta>Catchword: 11. „The</meta>

> „of **God**, are: O blessed embrace! In this embrace, **God** gives Himself entirely to the soul, and lets her enjoy all His works: and there the soul also gives herself entirely to **God**. Here they are in the bridal chamber, and when the heavenly Bridegroom has spoken to His beloved there and embraced her, He also kisses her, which occurs through the meeting of their mutual love—namely, the love of the infinite Essence of **God**, and the love of the created being, which **God** unites with Himself. etc.

8. The last letter of the dear Johanna cited above was written, as already reported, in June of the year 1632. The remaining accounts of her inner and outer life, which lasted for more than seven years, were also written down; however, these writings all fell into the hands of robbers in the year 1646 and were never found again. Only this following little letter has been preserved, which she wrote to her biological brother one year before her end:

> 9. „My dear brother! So that I may satisfy your desire, I will tell you briefly of my exercises <note>original: "Uebungen"; refers to "spiritual exercises" or disciplined practices of prayer and reflection.</note>. Know then, that I rely on myself in nothing; instead, I renounce trust in all my outward actions—in eating, drinking, and interaction with people. I renounce trust in all my penitential exercises, and in all my prayers that I may perform for myself or for others. I stand always on the watchtower and wait, so that my soul is completely naked: and so must she be, in order that she may be clothed with **Jesus Christ**. In this manner I live and walk, with the help of **God**, elevated above myself and above all my natural inclinations and imperfections. I renounce trust in myself in all things: I renounce trust in creatures <note>In this context, "creatures" refers to all created things or people, as opposed to the Creator.</note>, and lean only on **God** alone.
> 
> „I eat, I drink, I speak with people, because I am obligated to do so by necessity. I love all creatures in their order, as **God** created them, except for the sin and the evil nature of the same. The reason why I thus let go of all trust [except in **God**] is this: because our malicious nature is so false and cunning that if one does not act so, it mixes itself in unperceived, and thus our good works become stained.

> 10. „You must also come to this point, my dear brother! without relying in the least on yourself, on your understanding or judgment, or on anything that you perform.
> 
> „When I look at how people go to work in all things through this hidden trust in themselves, I cannot restrain myself; I must contradict them, for I see this truth much clearer than the bright sun. When my friends commend themselves to my prayer, I say to them: I will do it, if it pleases **God**; but place your trust in **God**: I always fear they will place their trust in my prayers. For when one prays, one must renounce all trust in one's own prayers, and look only at the goodness of **God** alone, in the trust that He will give us our request without our merit.
> 
> „And this renouncing of trust in oneself, and in all people, gives the soul the greatest good that one can attain on earth. And in this consists properly the putting off of the **old man** <note>A biblical reference to the "old self" or the unregenerate human nature (Ephesians 4:22).</note>, of which many people prattle without knowing what it is: They think that it is when one leaves the coarse world, but we have our greatest enemy within ourselves.

<meta>This page concludes the "Twelfth Piece" concerning the life of Johanna von Cambry. It contains the final sections of her last preserved letter to her brother and a biographical account of her death in 1639, followed by her epitaph. It marks the end of the second volume of the work.</meta>

# Twelfth Piece. The Life of Johanna von Cambry.

> 11. „The Scripture also means this when it says that the left hand should not know what the right hand does: namely, our lower part and our malicious nature should not know what our inward will and the other higher parts are doing, which reign with **God** upon His throne; that is, our works should be so pure and so humble that we do not reflect upon ourselves in the process, except to offer them to **God** entirely naked <note>original: "nacket"; refers to the mystical concept of "spiritual poverty" or "nakedness," where the soul is stripped of all ego and self-interest.</note> and as if from outside of ourselves.

> 12. „I feel that I am coming to my end, and I do not think that I shall survive the Lenten season [she wrote this on the 14th of February, 1638.] Unless **God** were to perform a miracle. I thought that I would have died this night; I write this to you as news, so that if I should perhaps be found dead, my body may return to the earth and my soul to **God**, when it pleases Him. When I am in Paradise, I will pray for you.

> 13. „I go hence, completely naked before **God**; and even if I had performed all the good works of all the saints in Paradise, and had suffered all the pain and torment which all the martyrs together endured: I would still regard it as if I had done nothing. One must never prize one's good works highly, however virtuous and holy they may be in this world: **God** will nevertheless give us what pleases Him, for everything comes from Him.

> 14. „Think nevermore of your good works, but rather of **God** and of your imperfections, for in ourselves we have nothing but poverty.
>
> „If there should be anything in this letter that you cannot understand, then report it to me before my passing; that is, if it should happen that **God** lets me recover again, although I do not expect such a thing, especially since I am not otherwise provided for; for because I am old and worn out, I cannot go on much longer; I fear that I may die suddenly one day, as I have already fallen into faints on several occasions.”

15. After she had written this, she did indeed live another seventeen months contrary to expectations: but no further news remains of that time, nor of the circumstances of her death; only this is known, that on the 19th of July, 1639, in her enclosed little chamber near St. Andrew's Church in **Rissel** <note>Rissel is the historical German name for the city of Lille, now in northern France.</note>, she departed this temporal life, and was translated forever from her wretched dungeon and body into the vast palace, even into the innermost cabinet of her Bridegroom, after she had lived, suffered, and loved here on earth for fifty-eight years and eight months.
